title.zh: 卷七十六 列傳第一 后妃上
title.raw: 卷七十六 列傳第一 后妃上 Volume 76 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts 1

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 25%唐制：皇后而下，有貴妃、淑妃、德妃、賢妃，是為夫人。

translations.literal: Tang regulations: Below the empress there were Noble Consort, Pure Consort, Virtuous Consort, and Worthy Consort—these were called Ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang institutions, ranking below the empress were the four consorts of highest grade—Noble, Pure, Virtuous, and Worthy—collectively termed Ladies.

sentences.zh: 昭儀、昭容、昭媛、修儀、修容、修媛、充儀、充容、充媛，是為九嬪。

translations.literal: Bright Lady, Bright Beauty, Bright Fair Maid, Cultivated Lady, Cultivated Beauty, Cultivated Fair Maid, Fulfilling Lady, Fulfilling Beauty, and Fulfilling Fair Maid—these were the Nine Concubines.
translations.idiomatic: The nine ranks of concubine—Bright, Cultivated, and Fulfilling, each in Lady, Beauty, and Fair Maid grades—formed the Nine Concubines.

sentences.zh: 婕妤、美人、才人各九，合二十七，是代世婦。

translations.literal: Lady of Handsome Fairness, Beauty, and Talented Lady, nine of each, totaling twenty-seven—these stood in for the Zhou dynasty's shi fu.
translations.idiomatic: There were nine each of Lady of Handsome Fairness, Beauty, and Talented Lady—twenty-seven in all—corresponding to the ritual office of shi fu in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 寶林、御女、采女各二十七，合八十一，是代御妻。

translations.literal: Treasure Grove, Imperial Maid, and Selecting Maid, twenty-seven of each, totaling eighty-one—these stood in for the Zhou dynasty's yu qi.
translations.idiomatic: Treasure Grove, Imperial Maid, and Selecting Maid, twenty-seven apiece—eighty-one altogether—served as counterparts to the ancient yu qi.

sentences.zh: 自餘六尚，分典乘輿服御，皆有員次。

translations.literal: Besides these, the Six Chief Offices each administered imperial carriages, apparel, and furnishings, all with fixed quotas and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining Six Chief Offices of the inner palace, each overseeing imperial transport, dress, and household service, likewise had prescribed numbers and precedence.

sentences.zh: 後世改復不常。

translations.literal: Later ages changed and restored these offices without consistency.
translations.idiomatic: In later times the titles were altered and revived again and again without settled rule.

sentences.zh: 開元時，以後下復有四妃非是，乃置惠、麗、華三妃，六儀，四美人，七才人，而尚宮、尚儀、尚服各二，參合前號，大抵踵《周官》相損益云，然則尚矣。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, because having four consorts below the empress was deemed improper, they established the three consorts Hui, Li, and Hua, six Ladies of Ceremony, four Beauties, and seven Talented Ladies, with two each for Chief of Palace, Chief of Ceremonies, and Chief of Apparel, combining earlier titles—generally following the Offices of Zhou with additions and reductions—thus reaching a high point.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan, the court judged the revival of four consorts beneath the empress unsound and instead instituted the Hui, Li, and Hua consorts, six Ladies of Ceremony, four Beauties, and seven Talented Ladies, doubling the Chiefs of Palace, Ceremonies, and Apparel and blending earlier designations—largely adapting the model of the Rites of Zhou—so that the system at last attained its fullest form.

sentences.zh: 禮本夫婦，《詩》始后妃，治亂因之，興亡係焉。

translations.literal: Rites take husband and wife as their root; the Book of Songs begins with empress and consorts; order and disorder follow from them, rise and fall depend on them.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual grounds itself in the bond of husband and wife; the Odes open with empress and consort; through them governance turns to order or chaos, and dynasties rise or perish.

sentences.zh: 盛德之君，帷薄嚴奧，裏謁不忓於朝，外言不內諸閫，《關雎》之風行，彤史之化修，故淑範懿行，更為內助。

translations.literal: A sovereign of great virtue keeps the inner quarters strict and deep; private audiences do not impinge on court, outside words do not enter the women's quarters; the spirit of 'Guan Ju' prevails, the red histories' teaching is cultivated—thus pure models and excellent conduct become further aid within.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler of outstanding virtue keeps the inner palace austere and sealed: private audiences never disrupt the court, and outside talk never crosses the women's gate. Where the ethos of 'Guan Ju' flourishes and the annals of the inner court are kept with care, virtuous example becomes the emperor's true support within.

sentences.zh: 若夫艷嬖之興，常在中主。

translations.literal: As for the rise of dazzling favorites, it commonly occurs under middling rulers.
translations.idiomatic: The ascent of dazzling favorites, by contrast, usually belongs to rulers of merely average caliber.

sentences.zh: 笫裯既交，則情與愛遷；

translations.literal: Once bed-mats are exchanged, affection and favor shift.
translations.idiomatic: Once the bed is shared with another, feeling and favor drift away.

sentences.zh: 顏辭媚熟，則事為私奪。

translations.literal: When countenance and speech grow skilled in flattery, affairs are seized for private ends.
translations.idiomatic: When looks and words grow expert in charm, public business is taken for private gain.

sentences.zh: 乘易昏之明，牽不斷之柔，險言似忠，故受而不詰，醜行已效，反狃而為好。

translations.literal: Riding the twilight when judgment is easy to dim, tugging at softness that cannot be severed, treacherous words seeming loyal—thus received without inquiry; when ugly conduct has already taken effect, one grows accustomed and takes it for good.
translations.idiomatic: They exploit the hour when the mind grows dull, play on tenderness the ruler cannot cut off, and speak treachery in the guise of loyalty—so he accepts it without question. Once shameful conduct has already succeeded, he grows used to it and calls it virtue.

sentences.zh: 左右附之，憸壬惎之，狡謀鉗其悟先，哀誓楗於寵初，天下之事已去，而恬不自覺，此武、韋所以遂篡弒而喪王室也。

translations.literal: Those at his side attach to them, slanderers incite them, crafty schemes clamp his awakening beforehand, pitiful oaths wedge him at the first moment of favor—the affairs of the realm are already lost, yet he remains placid and unaware; this is how Wu and Wei were able to carry out usurpation and regicide and bring the royal house to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers cling to them, villains stir them on, cunning plots forestall the ruler's second thoughts, and feigned grief locks him in at the dawn of favor. The realm is already lost while he rests easy and knows it not—thus Wu and Wei could usurp the throne, murder their sovereigns, and destroy the Tang house.

sentences.zh: 至於楊氏未死，玄亂厥謀；

translations.literal: As for Lady Yang, before she died Xuanluan threw her plot into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In Lady Yang's case, rebellion broke out before her death and overturned her designs.

sentences.zh: 張后制中，肅幾斂衽。

translations.literal: When Empress Zhang held the reins, Suzong nearly drew in his robe in deference.
translations.idiomatic: While Empress Zhang held sway, Emperor Suzong all but shrank before her in the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 吁，可嘆哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Ah—it is heartbreaking to recall!

sentences.zh: 中葉以降，時多故矣，外有攻討之勤，內寡嬿溺之私，群閹朋進，外戚勢分，后妃無大善惡，取充職位而已，故列著於篇。

translations.literal: From the mid-dynasty onward the times held many troubles: outwardly there was the toil of campaigns, inwardly little room for indulgent attachment; eunuch factions advanced in groups, consort kin lost consolidated power—empresses and consorts showed no great good or evil, serving only to fill their offices; therefore they are set forth in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: From the mid-Tang onward the age was full of troubles: wars pressed from without, and within there was scant leisure for royal dalliance. Eunuch factions rose together, and maternal kin lost their old dominance. Empresses and consorts neither greatly helped nor greatly harmed the state—they merely occupied their titles—so they are recorded here in sequence.

sentences.zh: 高祖太穆順聖皇后高祖太穆順聖皇后竇氏，京兆平陵人。

translations.literal: Empress Taimu the Shunsheng of Emperor Gaozu—Lady Dou of Pingling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Taimu the Shunsheng, consort of Emperor Gaozu, was née Dou, of Pingling in Jingzhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 父毅，在周為上柱國，尚武帝姊襄陽長公主，入隋為定州總管、神武公。

translations.literal: Her father Yi, in Zhou served as Supreme Pillar of State, married Emperor Wu's elder sister the Princess of Xiangyang, and entering Sui became regional commander of Dingzhou and Duke of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Dou Yi had been Supreme Pillar of State under Northern Zhou and had married Emperor Wu's elder sister, the Princess of Xiangyang. Under Sui he became regional commander of Dingzhou and Duke of Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 后生，髮垂過頸，三歲與身等。

translations.literal: When the lady was born, her hair hung past her neck; at three it equaled her height.
translations.idiomatic: At birth her hair already reached below her neck; by age three it was as long as she was tall.

sentences.zh: 讀《女誡》、《列女》等傳，一過輒不忘。

translations.literal: Reading the Admonitions for Women, Biographies of Exemplary Women, and similar works, she never forgot them after a single reading.
translations.idiomatic: She read the Admonitions for Women, the Biographies of Exemplary Women, and similar texts, and never forgot a passage after reading it once.

sentences.zh: 武帝愛之，養宮中，異它甥。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu loved her, raised her in the palace, and treated her differently from other nephews and nieces.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu favored her, kept her in the palace, and singled her out among his kin.

sentences.zh: 時突厥女為后，無寵，后密諫曰：「吾國未靖，虜且強，願抑情撫接，以取合從，則江南、關東不吾梗。」

translations.literal: At the time a Turkic woman was empress but without favor; the lady secretly advised: 'Our state is not yet settled, the barbarians are still strong—I beg you to restrain your feelings and treat her with kindness to win alliance, then south of the Yangtze and east of the Pass will not obstruct us.
translations.idiomatic: A Turkic woman then held the title of empress but had fallen from favor. The young Lady Dou privately urged Emperor Wu: 'The realm is not yet secure and the nomads remain strong. Please master your feelings and treat her with kindness to secure their alliance—then the south and the eastern provinces will not stand in our way.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘉納。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and followed her counsel.

sentences.zh: 及崩，哀毀同所生。

translations.literal: When he died, her grief and devastation were as for a birth parent.
translations.idiomatic: When he died she mourned with the grief of a daughter for her own father.

sentences.zh: 聞隋高祖受禪，自投床下，曰：「恨我非男子，不能捄舅家禍。」

translations.literal: Hearing that Sui Emperor Gaozu had received the abdication, she threw herself from the bed, saying: 'I hate that I am not a man and cannot rescue my mother's clan from disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When she learned that Yang Jian had taken the throne, she flung herself from her couch crying, 'I regret I am not a man—I cannot save my uncle's house from ruin!

sentences.zh: 毅遽掩其口，曰：「毋妄言，赤吾族！」

translations.literal: Yi hastily covered her mouth, saying: 'Do not speak rashly—you will exterminate our clan!'
translations.idiomatic: Her father clapped a hand over her mouth at once: 'Do not speak recklessly—you will bring death upon our whole clan!'

sentences.zh: 常謂主曰：「此女有奇相，且識不凡，何可妄與人？」

translations.literal: He often told the princess: 'This daughter has an extraordinary countenance and uncommon understanding—how can she be given rashly to anyone?'
translations.idiomatic: He often told the princess, 'This girl has an extraordinary face and uncommon judgment—she must not be married off carelessly.'

sentences.zh: 因畫二孔雀屏間，請昏者使射二矢，陰約中目則許之。

translations.literal: Therefore he painted two peacocks on a screen and had suitors shoot two arrows, secretly agreeing that only one who hit the eyes would be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore painted two peacocks on a screen and invited suitors to shoot two arrows, secretly resolving to accept only the man who struck both eyes.

sentences.zh: 射者閱數十，皆不合。

translations.literal: Archers passed by in the dozens, none meeting the condition.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of suitors tried and failed.

sentences.zh: 高祖最後射，中各一目，遂歸於帝。

translations.literal: Gaozu shot last, hit each eye, and thus she was given to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu shot last, struck each eye, and won her hand in marriage.

sentences.zh: 始，元貞太后羸老有疾，而性素嚴，諸姒娣皆畏，莫敢侍。

translations.literal: At first the Yuanzhen Dowager was frail and aged with illness, yet by nature stern—all the daughters-in-law feared her and none dared attend her.
translations.idiomatic: At first Dowager Yuanzhen was frail, elderly, and ill, yet by nature severe. The other daughters-in-law all feared her and none dared nurse her.

sentences.zh: 后事之，獨怡謹盡孝，或淹月不釋衣履。

translations.literal: The empress alone served her, cheerful and careful in full filial devotion, sometimes for a month not removing clothes or shoes.
translations.idiomatic: The empress alone attended her with cheerful reverence and complete devotion, sometimes going a full month without changing her clothes or shoes.

sentences.zh: 工為篇章規誡，文有雅體。

translations.literal: She was skilled at composing admonitory essays, her writing possessing an elegant style.
translations.idiomatic: She excelled at moral essays and admonitions written in a refined classical style.

sentences.zh: 又善書，與高祖書相雜，人不辨也。

translations.literal: She was also skilled at calligraphy; mixed with Gaozu's writing, people could not distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: She was also accomplished in calligraphy—when her hand was set beside Gaozu's, no one could tell them apart.

sentences.zh: 崩於涿郡，年四十五。

translations.literal: She died in Zhuo commandery at age forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Zhuo commandery at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 帝在煬帝時，多畜善馬，后見曰：「上性樂此，盍以獻？

translations.literal: When the emperor was under Emperor Yang, he kept many fine horses; the empress saw this and said: 'His Majesty delights in these—why not present them as tribute?
translations.idiomatic: While still a prince under Emperor Yang, he kept many fine horses. The empress said to him, 'The emperor loves such horses—why not present them to him?

sentences.zh: 徒留之速罪，無益也。」

translations.literal: Keeping them for nothing will hasten punishment—it is of no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Keeping them will only bring punishment sooner. There is no gain in it.

sentences.zh: 不聽，頃果坐譴。

translations.literal: He did not listen; soon he indeed suffered reprimand on that account.
translations.idiomatic: He refused—and soon was indeed punished for it.

sentences.zh: 帝後見隋政亂，多妄誅殛，乃為自安計，數奏鷹犬異駒，煬帝果喜，擢位將軍。

translations.literal: Later, seeing Sui government in disorder and many put to death without cause, he devised a plan for his own safety, repeatedly presenting rare hawks, dogs, and horses; Emperor Yang was pleased and promoted him to general.
translations.idiomatic: Later, seeing Sui politics in chaos and arbitrary executions multiplying, he adopted a plan of self-preservation and repeatedly sent rare hawks, hounds, and horses to the throne. Emperor Yang was delighted and promoted him to general.

sentences.zh: 因泣謂諸子曰：「早用而母言，得此久矣！」

translations.literal: He wept and told his sons: 'Had I early followed your mother's words, I would have had this long ago!
translations.idiomatic: He wept and told his sons, 'Had I listened to your mother sooner, I would have enjoyed this rank long ago!

sentences.zh: 帝有天下，詔即所葬園為壽安陵，謚曰穆。

translations.literal: When the emperor possessed the realm, he decreed that the garden where she was buried become Shou'an Mausoleum, with posthumous title Mu.
translations.idiomatic: After he won the empire, he ordered her burial garden renamed Shou'an Mausoleum and gave her the posthumous title Mu.

sentences.zh: 及祔獻陵，尊為太穆皇后。

translations.literal: When she was enshrined at Xian Mausoleum, she was honored as Empress Taimu.
translations.idiomatic: When her spirit tablet was placed in Xian Mausoleum, she was honored as Empress Taimu.

sentences.zh: 始，太宗生，有二龍之符，后於諸子中愛視最篤。

translations.literal: At first, when Taizong was born there was an omen of two dragons; among all sons the empress loved and regarded him most deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong was born, an omen of two dragons appeared, and among all her sons the empress loved him most devotedly.

sentences.zh: 後即位，過慶善宮，覽觀梗欷，顧侍臣曰：「朕生於此，今母后永違，育我之德不可報。」

translations.literal: Later, having taken the throne, passing Qing Shan Palace, he viewed it with choked sobs and told his attendants: 'I was born here; now the empress dowager is gone forever—the grace of raising me cannot be repaid.
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne he passed Qing Shan Palace, gazed upon it with choked sobs, and told his attendants, 'I was born here. Now my mother is gone forever—the debt of her nurture can never be repaid.

sentences.zh: 因號慟，左右皆流涕。

translations.literal: He then wailed aloud, and those at his side all wept.
translations.idiomatic: He broke into loud lamentation, and all those beside him wept.

sentences.zh: 乃享后於正寢。

translations.literal: He then offered sacrifice to the empress in the main chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He then performed a memorial offering to her in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 它日幸九成宮，夢后若平生，既悟，潸然不自勝。

translations.literal: Another day, visiting Jiucheng Palace, he dreamed of the empress as in life; upon waking, tears flowed beyond his control.
translations.idiomatic: On another day, while visiting Jiucheng Palace, he dreamed of her as though she were still alive. When he woke, he could not hold back his tears.

sentences.zh: 明日，詔有司大發倉賑貧瘠，以為后報焉。

translations.literal: The next day he decreed that officials open the granaries on a large scale to relieve the poor and emaciated, taking this as repayment to the empress.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he ordered the granaries opened on a grand scale to relieve the poor, as an act of gratitude in her name.

sentences.zh: 上元中，益謚太穆神皇后。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era her title was further augmented to Empress Taimu the Divine.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shangyuan era her posthumous title was further elevated to Empress Taimu the Divine.

sentences.zh: 太宗文德長孫皇后太宗文德順聖皇后長孫氏，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Empress Wende the Shunsheng of Emperor Taizong—Lady Changsun of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wende the Shunsheng, consort of Emperor Taizong, was née Changsun, of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 其先魏拓拔氏，後為宗室長，因號長孫。

translations.literal: Her ancestors were the Tuoba of Wei; later one became chief of the imperial clan, hence the surname Changsun.
translations.idiomatic: Her clan descended from the Tuoba of Northern Wei; an ancestor became chief of the imperial lineage, whence the surname Changsun, 'chief of the long lineage.'

sentences.zh: 高祖稚，大丞相、馮翊王。

translations.literal: Her great-grandfather Zhi was Grand Chancellor and Prince of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-grandfather Zhi was Grand Chancellor and Prince of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 曾祖裕，平原公。

translations.literal: Her great-great-grandfather Yu was Duke of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-great-grandfather Yu held the title Duke of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖兕，左將軍。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Si was General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Si served as General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 父晟，字季，涉書史，趫鷙曉兵，仕隋為右驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: Her father Sheng, styled Ji, versed in books and histories, swift and fierce and skilled in warfare, served Sui as General of the Right Agile Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Sheng, courtesy name Ji, was learned in history, bold and skilled in military affairs, and under Sui served as General of the Right Agile Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 后喜圖傳，視古善惡以自鑒，矜尚禮法。

translations.literal: The empress delighted in illustrated histories, viewing ancient good and evil as her mirror, and prized ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: The empress loved illustrated histories, took ancient examples of good and evil as her mirror, and held fast to ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 晟兄熾，為周通道館學士。

translations.literal: Sheng's elder brother Chi was a scholar of the Tongdao Hall under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's elder brother Chi had been a scholar of the Tongdao Hall under Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗聞太穆勸撫突厥女，心誌之。

translations.literal: He once heard of Taimu's counsel to soothe the Turkic empress and kept it in mind.
translations.idiomatic: He had heard how Empress Taimu urged conciliation toward the Turkic empress and kept the lesson in mind.

sentences.zh: 每語晟曰：「此明睿人，必有奇子，不可以不圖昏。」

translations.literal: He often told Sheng: 'This is a clear and wise person—she will surely have an extraordinary son; you must not fail to arrange a marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He often told Sheng, 'She is a woman of insight and will surely bear an extraordinary son. You must secure her for your house.

sentences.zh: 故晟以女太宗。

translations.literal: Therefore Sheng gave his daughter to Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason Sheng gave his daughter in marriage to Taizong.

sentences.zh: 后歸寧，舅高士廉妾見大馬二丈立后舍外，懼，占之，遇《坤》之《泰》。

translations.literal: When the empress returned home, her uncle Gao Shilian's concubine saw a great horse two zhang tall standing outside the empress's quarters, feared it, and divined, obtaining Kun changing to Tai.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit home, a concubine of her uncle Gao Shilian saw a huge horse two zhang tall standing outside the empress's quarters. Terrified, she cast the hexagrams and received Kun changing to Tai.

sentences.zh: 卜者曰：「《坤》順承天，載物無疆；

translations.literal: The diviner said: 'Kun submits and receives Heaven, bearing all things without limit;
translations.idiomatic: The diviner said, 'Kun submits to Heaven and bears all things without limit.

sentences.zh: 馬，地類也；

translations.literal: the horse belongs to the category of earth;
translations.idiomatic: The horse belongs to the creatures of earth.

sentences.zh: 之《泰》，是天地交而萬物通也，又以輔相天地之宜。

translations.literal: changing to Tai means Heaven and Earth join and the myriad things flow through; moreover she will assist in harmonizing Heaven and Earth's proper roles.
translations.idiomatic: Tai means Heaven and Earth unite and all things prosper—she will aid in harmonizing their proper order.

sentences.zh: 繇協《歸妹》，婦人事也。

translations.literal: The line statement accords with Gui Mei—the affair of a wife.
translations.idiomatic: The judgment accords with Gui Mei—the work of a wife.

sentences.zh: 女處尊位，履中而居順，后妃象也。」

translations.literal: A woman occupying the honored position, treading the center and dwelling in submission—this is the image of empress and consort.
translations.idiomatic: A woman in the honored place, centered and yielding—this is the sign of empress and consort.

sentences.zh: 時隱太子釁鬩已構，后內盡孝事高祖，謹承諸妃，消釋嫌猜。

translations.literal: At the time the Hidden Crown Prince's feud was already formed; within, the empress exhausted filial service to Gaozu, carefully received all consorts, and dissolved suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: By then the feud with the Crown Prince was already brewing. Within the palace the empress devoted herself to Gaozu in filial service, treated the other consorts with care, and eased mutual suspicion.

sentences.zh: 及帝授甲宮中，后親慰勉，士皆感奮。

translations.literal: When the emperor donned armor in the palace, the empress personally comforted and encouraged the men, and all were moved to ardor.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor armed himself within the palace, the empress went among the soldiers to encourage them, and all were stirred to zeal.

sentences.zh: 尋為皇太子妃，俄為皇后。

translations.literal: Soon she became crown princess, and shortly after, empress.
translations.idiomatic: She soon became crown princess and shortly thereafter empress.

sentences.zh: 性約素，服御取給則止。

translations.literal: By nature frugal and plain, in dress and use she stopped when needs were met.
translations.idiomatic: By nature she was frugal and plain, taking only what sufficed for dress and daily use.

sentences.zh: 益觀書，雖容櫛不少廢。

translations.literal: She read books all the more, never neglecting them even while dressing her hair.
translations.idiomatic: She read all the more diligently, never setting her books aside even while attending to her hair.

sentences.zh: 與帝言，或及天下事，辭曰：「牝雞司晨，家之窮也，可乎？」

translations.literal: Speaking with the emperor, if matters touched on the realm she declined, saying: 'When the hen announces the dawn, the household is ruined—how can that be?
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor spoke with her of state affairs, she refused, saying, 'When a hen crows for the dawn, the household is ruined—how could I do such a thing?

sentences.zh: 帝固要之，訖不對。

translations.literal: The emperor pressed her firmly, but in the end she did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed her again and again, but she would not reply.

sentences.zh: 後廷有被罪者，必助帝怒請繩治，俟意解，徐為開治，終不令有冤；

translations.literal: When someone in the rear palace was guilty, she always helped the emperor's anger and asked that they be bound and punished; when his mood eased, she slowly opened the way to remedy, never allowing injustice in the end;
translations.idiomatic: When someone in the inner palace fell under blame, she would first share the emperor's anger and urge strict punishment; when his temper cooled, she would gradually plead for leniency, and in the end no innocent person suffered;

sentences.zh: 下嬪生豫章公主而死，后視如所生；

translations.literal: when a lower consort bore the Princess of Yuzhang who then died, the empress treated her as if born of herself;
translations.idiomatic: when a lesser consort bore the Princess of Yuzhang and died in childbirth, the empress raised the child as her own;

sentences.zh: 媵侍疾病，輟所御飲藥資之。

translations.literal: when attendant maids fell ill, she set aside her own food and medicine to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: when attendant maids fell ill, she gave them her own food and medicine.

sentences.zh: 下懷其仁。

translations.literal: Those below cherished her benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Those below were grateful for her kindness.

sentences.zh: 兄無忌，於帝本布衣交，以佐命為元功，出入臥內，帝將引以輔政，后固謂不可，乘間曰：「妾托體紫宮，尊貴已極，不願私親更據權於朝。

translations.literal: Her brother Wuji, originally the emperor's companion in common cloth, through aiding the founding mandate became a chief merit-holder, entering and leaving the sleeping quarters; the emperor was about to bring him in to assist in government—the empress firmly said it could not be, seizing an interval to say: 'Your servant's body rests in the Purple Palace, honor already at its limit—I do not wish private kin to hold power again at court.
translations.idiomatic: Her brother Zhangsun Wuji had been the emperor's friend in humble days and, as a founder of the dynasty, ranked among its greatest servants, entering even the imperial bedchamber. When the emperor meant to bring him into the government, the empress firmly opposed it and said at an opportune moment, 'I already stand at the summit of honor in the Purple Palace. I do not wish my own kin to wield power at court again.

sentences.zh: 漢之呂、霍，可以為誡。」

translations.literal: The Lü and Huo of Han may serve as warning.
translations.idiomatic: The Lü clan and Huo Guang of Han should be our warning.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，自用無忌為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen and on his own appointed Wuji Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed her and appointed Wuji Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 后密諭令牢讓，帝不獲已，乃聽，后喜見顏間。

translations.literal: The empress secretly instructed him to firmly decline; the emperor, having no choice, consented, and joy showed on the empress's face.
translations.idiomatic: The empress secretly urged Wuji to decline firmly. Unable to refuse further, the emperor yielded, and her pleasure showed plainly in her face.

sentences.zh: 異母兄安業無行，父喪，逐后、無忌還外家。

translations.literal: Her half-brother Anye was without conduct; at their father's funeral he drove the empress and Wuji back to her mother's family.
translations.idiomatic: Her half-brother Anye was a man of bad character. At their father's funeral he drove the empress and Wuji back to their mother's family.

sentences.zh: 后貴，未嘗以為言。

translations.literal: After the empress rose in honor, she never spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: After she became empress she never mentioned the matter.

sentences.zh: 擢位將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to general.
translations.idiomatic: He was nevertheless promoted to general.

sentences.zh: 後與李孝常等謀反，將誅，后叩頭曰：「安業罪死無赦。

translations.literal: Later he plotted rebellion with Li Xiaochang and others; about to be executed, the empress kowtowed and said: 'Anye's crime deserves death without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Li Xiaochang and others in plotting rebellion. When execution was imminent, the empress kowtowed and said, 'Anye's crime deserves death without mercy.

sentences.zh: 然向遇妾不以慈，戶知之；

translations.literal: Yet in the past he met your servant without kindness—all households know it;
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the past he treated me without kindness, as all the world knows.

sentences.zh: 今論如法，人必謂妾釋憾於兄，無乃為帝累乎！」

translations.literal: if now he is punished according to law, people will surely say your servant released old resentment against her brother—will this not burden Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: If he is punished by law now, people will surely say I settled an old score against my brother. Would that not burden Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 遂得減流越巂。

translations.literal: He was thus able to have his sentence reduced to exile in Yuexi.
translations.idiomatic: His sentence was reduced to exile in Yuexi.

sentences.zh: 太子承乾乳媼請增東宮什器，后曰：「太子患無德與名，器何請為？」

translations.literal: The wet nurse of Crown Prince Chengqian asked to increase the Eastern Palace furnishings; the empress said: 'The crown prince's worry is lack of virtue and fame—what need is there to ask for vessels?'
translations.idiomatic: The wet nurse of Crown Prince Chengqian asked for more furnishings for the Eastern Palace. The empress said, 'The crown prince lacks virtue and a good name—why should he ask for more vessels?'

sentences.zh: 從幸九成宮，方屬疾，會柴紹等急變聞，帝甲而起，后輿疾以從，宮司諫止，后曰：「上震驚，吾可自安？」

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor to Jiucheng Palace, she was just ill when urgent news came of the crisis with Chai Shao and others; the emperor rose in armor, and the empress, ill though she was, followed in her carriage; palace officials advised her to stop—the empress said: 'The emperor is shaken—how can I rest secure?
translations.idiomatic: While accompanying the emperor to Jiucheng Palace she fell ill. When urgent news arrived of the uprising involving Chai Shao and others, the emperor rose and armed himself. Though ill, the empress had herself carried along. Palace officials urged her to stop, but she said, 'The emperor is in alarm—how can I seek my own ease?

sentences.zh: 疾稍亟，太子欲請大赦，汎度道人，祓塞災會。

translations.literal: Her illness grew somewhat severe; the crown prince wished to request a great amnesty, ordain Daoist priests, and perform rites to ward off disaster.
translations.idiomatic: As her illness worsened, the crown prince wished to request a general amnesty, ordain Daoist priests, and perform rites to avert calamity.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「死生有命，非人力所支。

translations.literal: The empress said: 'Life and death have their mandate—it is not what human effort can sustain.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, 'Life and death are ordained—it is not for human effort to decide.

sentences.zh: 若修福可延，吾不為惡；

translations.literal: If cultivating merit could extend life, I have done no evil;
translations.idiomatic: If merit could prolong life, I have done no evil.

sentences.zh: 使善無效，我尚何求？

translations.literal: if goodness is without effect, what more do I seek?
translations.idiomatic: If goodness avails nothing, what more should I ask?

sentences.zh: 且赦令，國大事，佛、老異方教耳，皆上所不為，豈宜以吾亂天下法！」

translations.literal: Moreover amnesty is a great affair of state; Buddhism and Daoism are foreign teachings—the emperor does none of these; how should my sake disorder the laws of the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, amnesty is a grave matter of state, and Buddhism and Daoism are foreign teachings that the emperor does not practice. How could my illness justify overturning the laws of the realm!

sentences.zh: 太子不敢奏，以告房玄齡，玄齡以聞，帝嗟美。

translations.literal: The crown prince dared not memorialize it, told Fang Xuanling, and Xuanling reported it—the emperor sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince dared not memorialize the request and told Fang Xuanling instead. When Xuanling reported her words, the emperor sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 而群臣請遂赦，帝既許，后固爭止。

translations.literal: Yet when the ministers asked to proceed with the amnesty and the emperor had already agreed, the empress firmly contested and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers nevertheless pressed for an amnesty and the emperor had already consented, the empress firmly objected until he withdrew his promise.

sentences.zh: 及大漸，與帝決，時玄齡小譴就第，后曰：「玄齡久事陛下，預奇計秘謀，非大故，願勿置也。

translations.literal: When her illness grew critical, she took final leave of the emperor. At that time Xuanling had received a minor reprimand and returned to his estate. The empress said: "Xuanling has long served Your Majesty, sharing in extraordinary plans and secret stratagems. Unless there is a grave offense, I beg you not to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: As her illness turned grave, she bade the emperor farewell. Fang Xuanling had just been lightly censured and sent home. The empress urged him: "Fang Xuanling has served you for years and helped shape your boldest plans. Unless he has committed a serious wrong, please do not remove him from office.

sentences.zh: 妾家以恩澤進，無德而祿，易以取禍，無屬樞柄，以外戚奉朝請足矣。

translations.literal: My family rose through imperial favor—we hold salary without merit and readily invite disaster. We need no share in the pivots of power; for kin of the empress to attend court audiences as guests is enough.
translations.idiomatic: My clan advanced only through your grace; we enjoy rank without deserving it and court ruin. We should not hold the levers of government—it is enough that your wife's kin appear at court as honored guests.

sentences.zh: 妾生無益於時，死不可以厚葬，願因山為壟，無起墳，無用棺槨，器以瓦木，約費送終，是妾不見忘也。」

translations.literal: In life I brought no benefit to the age; in death I ought not receive a lavish burial. I wish to be buried along the mountain slope, with no mound raised, no coffin used, utensils of tile and wood only, and funeral costs kept sparing—that would mean I am not forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: I have done the times little good in life; do not honor me with a costly funeral. Bury me in a mound along the hillside—no tomb mound, no coffin, only simple vessels of tile and wood, and keep the rites frugal. That is how I would know I am remembered.

sentences.zh: 又請帝納忠容諫，勿受讒，省遊畋作役，死無恨。

translations.literal: She also asked the emperor to accept loyal counsel and remonstrance, not to heed slander, and to reduce hunting tours and corvée labor—then she would die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: She went on to ask him to heed loyal advisers, reject slander, and cut back on hunting, travel, and forced labor—then she could die content.

sentences.zh: 崩，年三十六。

translations.literal: She passed away, aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: She died at the age of thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 后嘗采古婦人事著《女則》十篇，又為論斥漢之馬后不能檢抑外家，使與政事，乃戒其車馬之侈，此謂開本源，恤末事。

translations.literal: The empress had once gathered ancient women's affairs and composed ten chapters of Standards for Women; she also wrote a discourse criticizing Empress Ma of Han for failing to restrain her kin and letting them join in government affairs, thereupon warning against the extravagance of carriages and horses—this is what is meant by opening the root source and caring for the final matters.
translations.idiomatic: She had collected stories of exemplary women from antiquity and written ten chapters called Standards for Women. She also argued that Empress Ma of the Han failed to restrain her family and let them meddle in politics, and warned against lavish carriages and horses—what the text calls tending the root and minding the branches.

sentences.zh: 常誡守者：「吾以自檢，故書無條理，勿令至尊見之。」

translations.literal: She often admonished the keeper: "I wrote this for my own self-examination, so the book lacks order—do not let His Majesty see it.
translations.idiomatic: She often told the keeper of the manuscript, "I wrote this only to examine myself, so it is disorderly—do not let the emperor see it.

sentences.zh: 及崩，宮司以聞，帝為之慟，示近臣曰：「后此書可用垂後，我豈不通天命而割情乎！

translations.literal: When she died, palace officials reported it. The emperor mourned deeply and showed the book to close ministers, saying: "The empress's book can be handed down to posterity—would I fail to understand Heaven's mandate and cut off my affection!
translations.idiomatic: After her death the palace staff informed him. He grieved deeply, showed the work to his closest ministers, and said, "This book of hers can guide future generations—am I so blind to fate that I would deny my love?

sentences.zh: 顧內失吾良佐，哀不可已已！」

translations.literal: Yet within I have lost my fine helper—my grief cannot be stopped!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have lost my finest counselor within the palace—my sorrow will not end!"

sentences.zh: 謚曰文德，葬昭陵，因九嵕山，以成后志。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Wende; buried at Zhaoling, along Jiuzong Mountain, fulfilling the empress's wish.
translations.idiomatic: She was given the posthumous title Wende and buried at Zhaoling along Jiuzong Mountain, in keeping with her wishes.

sentences.zh: 帝自著表序始末，揭陵左。

translations.literal: The emperor himself composed a memorial stating the beginning and end, and posted it on the left of the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote a preface recounting her life and had it inscribed on the left side of the tomb.

sentences.zh: 上元中，益謚文德聖皇后。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era, her title was further augmented to Wende the Sagely Empress.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan reign her title was elevated to Sagely Empress Wende.

sentences.zh: 太宗賢妃徐惠太宗賢妃徐惠，湖州長城人。

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort Xu Hui of Taizong—Virtuous Consort Xu Hui—was a native of Changcheng in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort Xu Hui of Emperor Taizong was from Changcheng in Huzhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 生五月能言，四歲通《論語》、《詩》，八歲自曉屬文。

translations.literal: At five months she could speak; at four she mastered the Analects and Odes; at eight she understood composition on her own.
translations.idiomatic: She spoke at five months, knew the Analects and Book of Odes at four, and by eight could compose essays on her own.

sentences.zh: 父孝德，嘗試使擬《離騷》為《小山篇》曰：「仰幽巖而流盼，撫桂枝以凝想。

translations.literal: Her father Xiaode once tested her by having her adapt the "Li Sao" into "The Little Mountain Piece," which reads: "Raising my gaze to dark cliffs I cast my look; stroking cassia branches I fix my thought.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xu Xiaode once asked her to rework the "Li Sao" into a piece called "Little Mountain," which begins: "I lift my eyes to shadowed cliffs and gaze; I touch cassia boughs and lose myself in thought.

sentences.zh: 將千齡兮此遇，荃何為兮獨往？」

translations.literal: Shall I meet here for a thousand years—why should you, orchid fragrance, go alone?
translations.idiomatic: Here we might meet for a thousand years—why must the orchid spirit walk on alone?

sentences.zh: 孝德大驚，知不可掩，於是所論著遂盛傳。

translations.literal: Xiaode was greatly startled, knowing her talent could not be hidden, and thereafter her writings circulated widely.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode was astonished and knew her gift could not be concealed; from then on her writings spread widely.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之，召為才人。

translations.literal: Taizong heard of her and summoned her as Talented Lady.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard of her, he summoned her to the palace as a Talented Lady.

sentences.zh: 手未嘗廢卷，而辭致贍蔚，文無淹思。

translations.literal: Her hand never ceased holding a scroll; her phrasing was rich and ample, her writing without prolonged thought.
translations.idiomatic: She never set aside her books; her style was lush and fluent, and she wrote without laboring over each line.

sentences.zh: 帝益禮顧，擢孝德水部員外郎，惠再遷充容。

translations.literal: The emperor showed her ever greater courtesy; Xiaode was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Waterways, and Hui was twice transferred to Fulfilling Fair Maid.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated her with growing regard, promoted her father to vice director in the Ministry of Waterways, and twice advanced Hui to the rank of Fulfilling Fair Maid.

sentences.zh: 貞觀末，數調兵討定四夷，稍稍治宮室，百姓勞怨。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguan, troops were repeatedly mobilized to subdue the four border peoples and palaces were gradually built; the common people grew weary and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhenguan era the court repeatedly sent armies against the frontier peoples and slowly expanded the palaces; the people grew exhausted and bitter.

sentences.zh: 惠上疏極諫，且言：「東戍遼海，西討崑丘，士馬罷耗，漕饟漂沒。

translations.literal: Hui submitted a memorial of stern remonstrance, saying in part: "Garrisoning Liaodong in the east and campaigning against Kunlun in the west, soldiers and horses are worn out and grain transport sinks and is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Hui submitted a forceful memorial of remonstrance, writing in part: "We garrison Liaodong in the east and campaign toward Kunlun in the west; men and horses are spent, and grain shipped by water is sunk and wasted.

sentences.zh: 捐有盡之農，趨無窮之壑；

translations.literal: We abandon farming of finite yield to rush into a bottomless pit;
translations.idiomatic: We sacrifice finite harvests to chase an endless abyss;

sentences.zh: 圖未獲之眾，喪已成之軍。

translations.literal: We seek peoples not yet obtained and lose armies already formed.
translations.idiomatic: we pursue peoples we have not yet won and destroy armies we have already built.

sentences.zh: 故地廣者，非常安之術也；

translations.literal: Thus vast territory is not a technique of enduring peace;
translations.idiomatic: Vast territory, then, is no recipe for lasting peace;

sentences.zh: 人勞者，為易亂之符也。」

translations.literal: when the people are exhausted, it is a token of easy disorder.
translations.idiomatic: and a worn-out populace is a sign that chaos will come easily.

sentences.zh: 又言：「翠微、玉華等宮，雖因山藉水，無築構之苦，而工力和僦，不謂無煩。

translations.literal: She also said: "The palaces at Cuicui, Yuhua, and the like, though built with mountain and water and without the pain of piled construction, still require labor power and hired service—not to say they cause no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: She added: "Palaces such as Cuicui and Yuhua may follow the contours of hills and streams and avoid heavy construction, yet they still demand labor and hired workers—they are hardly free of burden.

sentences.zh: 有道之君，以逸逸人；

translations.literal: A ruler of the Way gives ease to give the people ease;
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who holds the Way rests so that his people may rest;

sentences.zh: 無道之君，以樂樂身。」

translations.literal: a ruler without the Way uses pleasure to pleasure himself."
translations.idiomatic: a ruler without the Way seeks pleasure only for himself."

sentences.zh: 又言：「伎巧為喪國斧斤，珠玉為蕩心酖毒，侈麗纖美，不可以不遏。

translations.literal: She also said: "Craft and cleverness are the axe that destroys a state; pearls and jade are poison that unsettles the heart; extravagant beauty in fine detail cannot go unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: She also wrote: "Ingenuity is the axe that fells a kingdom; pearls and jade are poison for the mind; luxury and delicate ornament must not be allowed to run unchecked.

sentences.zh: 志驕於業泰，體逸於時安。」

translations.literal: Ambition grows proud when enterprise flourishes; the body grows idle when the times are secure."
translations.idiomatic: Ambition swells when success is great; the body slackens when the age is calm."

sentences.zh: 其剴切精詣，大略如此。

translations.literal: Her keen remonstrance and penetrating argument were broadly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Her remonstrance was pointed and precise, and its tenor was much like this throughout.

sentences.zh: 帝善其言，優賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved her words and rewarded her generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised her counsel and lavished gifts upon her.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，哀慕成疾，不肯進藥，曰：「帝遇我厚，得先狗馬侍園寢，吾志也。」

translations.literal: When the emperor died, grief and longing became illness; she refused medicine, saying: "The emperor treated me generously; to precede his hounds and horses in serving the garden tomb is my wish.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's death she fell ill from grief and refused medicine, saying, "He treated me with great kindness. To go before him and serve in his tomb garden with his hounds and horses is what I desire.

sentences.zh: 復為詩、連珠以見意。

translations.literal: She also composed poems and linked pearls to express her intent.
translations.idiomatic: She also wrote poems and linked-verse pieces to voice her feelings.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年卒，年二十四，贈賢妃，陪葬昭陵石室。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui she died, aged twenty-four; she was posthumously made Virtuous Consort and buried beside Zhaoling in a stone chamber.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yonghui she died at twenty-four, was posthumously named Virtuous Consort, and was buried in a stone chamber at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 惠之弟齊聃，齊聃子堅，皆以學聞，女弟為高宗婕妤，亦有文藻，世以擬漢班氏。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Qi Dian; Qi's son Jian—all were renowned for learning. A younger sister became Lady of Handsome Fairness under Gaozong and likewise had literary grace; the age compared them to the Ban clan of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Qi Dian and Qi's son Jian were both famed scholars. A younger sister became a Lady of Handsome Fairness under Gaozong and was likewise accomplished in letters; contemporaries likened the family to the Ban clan of Han.

sentences.zh: 高宗廢后王氏高宗廢后王氏，并州祁人，魏尚書左僕射思政之孫。

translations.literal: Deposed Empress Wang of Gaozong—Deposed Empress Wang—was a native of Qi in Bingzhou, granddaughter of Wei Zuosi, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Empress Wang of Emperor Gaozong came from Qi in Bingzhou and was the granddaughter of Wei Zuosi, left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 從祖母同安長公主以后婉淑，白太宗以為晉王妃。

translations.literal: Her father's mother's younger sister, Princess Chang'an of Tong'an, because the future empress was gentle and comely, told Taizong to make her Prince of Jin's consort.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandaunt, Princess Chang'an of Tong'an, praised the girl's gentle beauty and recommended her to Taizong as consort to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 王居東宮，妃亦進冊，擢父仁祐陳州刺史。

translations.literal: When Wang dwelt in the Eastern Palace, the consort was also advanced in rank; her father Renyou was promoted to prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince lived in the Eastern Palace she was formally invested as his consort, and her father Wang Renyou was made prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong ascended the throne, she was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 仁祐以特進封魏國公；

translations.literal: Renyou was made Grand Mentor and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Renyou was granted the honorary title of Grand Mentor and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei;

sentences.zh: 母柳，本國夫人。

translations.literal: her mother the Liu clan, Lady of the State.
translations.idiomatic: her mother, of the Liu clan, was made Lady of the State.

sentences.zh: 仁祐卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: Renyou died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Renyou died he was posthumously appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 初，蕭良娣有寵，而武才人貞觀末以先帝宮人召為昭儀，俄與后、良娣爭寵，更相毀短。

translations.literal: At first Concubine Xiao had favor; the Talented Lady Wu, in late Zhenguan summoned from the late emperor's palace women as Bright Consort, soon vied with the empress and the concubine for favor, each slandering the other.
translations.idiomatic: At first Concubine Xiao held the emperor's favor. Wu, a former woman of Taizong's harem, was recalled late in Zhenguan and made Bright Consort; she soon competed with the empress and Xiao for favor, and the three traded accusations.

sentences.zh: 而昭儀詭險，即誣后與母挾媚道蠱上，帝信之，解魏國夫人門籍，罷后舅柳奭中書令。

translations.literal: But the Bright Consort was crafty and dangerous; she at once accused the empress and her mother of using bewitching arts to ensnare the emperor. The emperor believed it, revoked the Duke of Wei's household register, and removed the empress's uncle Liu Shi from Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was cunning and ruthless. She accused the empress and her mother of sorcery and enchantment, and the emperor believed her. He struck the Wang clan from the register of the Duke of Wei and dismissed the empress's uncle Liu Shi from the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 李義府等陰佐昭儀，以偏言怒帝，遂下詔廢后、良娣皆為庶人，囚宮中。

translations.literal: Li Yifu and others secretly aided the Bright Consort; with biased words they enraged the emperor, who then issued an edict deposing the empress and concubine both to commoners and imprisoning them in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu and others secretly supported Wu; with one-sided reports they inflamed the emperor until he issued an edict deposing both the empress and Xiao to commoner status and imprisoning them within the palace.

sentences.zh: 后母兄、良娣宗族悉流嶺南。

translations.literal: The empress's mother, elder brother, and the concubine's entire clan were exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's mother and brother and all of Xiao's kin were banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 許敬宗又奏：「仁祐無他功，以宮掖故，超列三事，今庶人謀亂宗社，罪宜夷宗，仁祐應斫棺，陛下不窮其誅，家止流竄，仁祐不宜引庇廕宥逆子孫。」

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong further memorialized: "Renyou had no other merit but rose to the three highest offices because of the inner palace. Now the deposed woman plotted to overturn the altars of state—the crime should annihilate the clan. Renyou's coffin ought to be opened. Yet Your Majesty does not carry the punishment to its limit and only exiles the family—Renyou ought not to be cited to shield and grant favor to rebellious descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong further argued: "Renyou had no merit beyond his daughter's place in the harem, yet he rose to one of the three highest offices. Now his daughter is accused of treason against the dynasty—the whole clan should be destroyed and Renyou's coffin opened. Your Majesty stops short of full punishment and merely exiles the family; Renyou should not be allowed to shield rebellious descendants.

sentences.zh: 有詔盡奪仁祐官爵。

translations.literal: An edict was issued stripping Renyou of all offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Renyou of every office and title.

sentences.zh: 而後及良娣俄為武后所殺，改后姓為「蟒」，良娣為「梟」。

translations.literal: Soon the empress and concubine were killed by Empress Wu; the empress's surname was changed to "python," the concubine's to "owl."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward both women were killed on Wu's orders; Wang's clan name was changed to "python" and Xiao's to "owl."

sentences.zh: 初，帝念后，間行至囚所，見門禁錮嚴，進飲食竇中，惻然傷之，呼曰：「皇后、良娣無恙乎？

translations.literal: At first the emperor thought of the empress and went by stealth to the prisoners' place. Seeing the gates strictly barred, he sent food and drink through the hole and felt poignant grief, calling: "Empress and Concubine, are you unharmed?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still thought of Wang and slipped away to the place where they were held. Finding the gates heavily barred, he sent food and drink through a small opening and was moved to pity, calling out, "Empress, Concubine—are you well?

sentences.zh: 今安在？」

translations.literal: Where are you now?
translations.idiomatic: Where are you now?

sentences.zh: 二人同辭曰：「妾等以罪棄為婢，安得尊稱耶？」

translations.literal: The two answered together: "We have been cast off as maidservants for our crimes—how can we bear honored titles?
translations.idiomatic: Both answered together, "We have been cast down as guilty servants—how can we still be called by those titles?

sentences.zh: 流淚嗚咽。

translations.literal: Tears flowed; they sobbed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: They broke down in tears and sobbing.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「陛下幸念疇日，使妾死更生，復見日月，乞署此為『回心院』。」

translations.literal: They also said: "If Your Majesty would kindly recall former days and grant us death and new life to see sun and moon again, we beg this place be named the Court of Returning Hearts."
translations.idiomatic: They added, "If Your Majesty remembers our past and restores us to life and daylight, we beg that this dwelling be named the Court of Returning Hearts."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕即有處置。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I shall presently arrange matters."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I will see to your release."

sentences.zh: 武后知之，促詔杖二人百，剔其手足，反接投釀甕中，曰：「令二嫗骨醉！」

translations.literal: When Empress Wu learned of it, she urgently ordered both beaten a hundred times, stripped of hands and feet, bound back-to-front and thrown into a wine vat, saying: "Let the two old crones' bones grow drunk!"
translations.idiomatic: When Wu learned of the visit she immediately ordered both women beaten a hundred strokes, had their limbs cut off, bound them hand to foot, and threw them into a wine vat, saying, "Let the two hags soak until their bones are drunk!"

sentences.zh: 數日死，殊其屍。

translations.literal: Within days they died; their corpses were mutilated.
translations.idiomatic: They died within days, and their bodies were disfigured beyond recognition.

sentences.zh: 初，詔旨到，后再拜曰：「陛下萬年！

translations.literal: When the edict first arrived, the empress bowed twice and said: "May Your Majesty live ten thousand years!
translations.idiomatic: When the deposition edict arrived, Wang bowed twice and said, "May Your Majesty live ten thousand years!

sentences.zh: 昭儀承恩，死吾分也。」

translations.literal: The Bright Consort enjoys the emperor's favor—death is my allotted portion.
translations.idiomatic: Wu enjoys your favor now—death is only what I deserve.

sentences.zh: 至良娣，罵曰：「武氏狐媚，翻覆至此！

translations.literal: As for the concubine, she cursed: "The Wu clan's bewitching sorcery has brought things to this reversal!
translations.idiomatic: Xiao cursed, "The Wu woman's sorcery has overturned everything!

sentences.zh: 我後為貓，使武氏為鼠，吾當扼其喉以報。」

translations.literal: In the next life I shall be a cat and make the Wu clan mice—I will throttle their throats in requital.
translations.idiomatic: In my next life I will be a cat and the Wu clan will be mice—I will seize them by the throat and repay this debt.

sentences.zh: 后聞，詔六宮毋畜貓。

translations.literal: When the empress heard, she ordered the six palaces not to keep cats.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu heard this she forbade cats throughout the six palaces.

sentences.zh: 武后頻見二人被髮瀝血為厲，惡之，以巫祝解謝，即徙蓬萊宮，厲復見，故多駐東都。

translations.literal: Empress Wu frequently saw the two, hair disheveled and blood dripping, as malign spirits; she detested it and used shamans for rites of release. She moved to Penglai Palace, but the spirits appeared again, hence she often stayed in the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wu repeatedly dreamed she saw the two women, hair loose and dripping blood, as vengeful ghosts. Horrified, she had shamans perform rites of appeasement and moved to Penglai Palace, but the visions returned, so she spent much of her time in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，皆復其姓。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, both surnames were restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong came to the throne, both women's original surnames were restored.

sentences.zh: 高宗則天武皇后高宗則天順聖皇后武氏，并州文水人。

translations.literal: Empress Wu Zetian of Gaozong—Gaozong's Sagely Empress Zetian of the Wu clan—was a native of Wenshui in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu Zetian of Emperor Gaozong—formally the Sagely Empress Zetian of the Wu clan—was born in Wenshui, Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父士彠，見《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Her father Shi Yi—see the biography of imperial affines.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Wu Shiyi is treated in the biography of imperial affines.

sentences.zh: 文德皇后崩，久之，太宗聞士彟女美，召為才人，方十四。

translations.literal: After Empress Wende died, long afterward Taizong heard that Shi Yi's daughter was beautiful and summoned her as Talented Lady—she was fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: Long after Empress Wende's death, Taizong heard that Shiyi's daughter was beautiful and summoned her to the palace as a Talented Lady. She was fourteen.

sentences.zh: 母楊，慟泣與訣，后獨自如，曰：「見天子庸知非福，何兒女悲乎？」

translations.literal: Her mother Yang wept and took leave in grief; the future empress alone was composed, saying: "To see the Son of Heaven—how know it is not fortune? Why the tears of a mere girl?
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Yang wept as they parted, but the girl herself was calm and said, "Who knows that meeting the Son of Heaven may not be a blessing? Why weep like an ordinary daughter?

sentences.zh: 母韙其意，止泣。

translations.literal: Her mother approved her meaning and stopped weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother took her point and dried her tears.

sentences.zh: 既見帝，賜號武媚。

translations.literal: Once she saw the emperor, she was given the name Wu Mei.
translations.idiomatic: When she was presented to the emperor he gave her the name Wu Mei.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，與嬪御皆為比丘尼。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, she with the consorts and attendants all became Buddhist nuns.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's death she and the other palace women were sent to a convent as Buddhist nuns.

sentences.zh: 高宗為太子時，入侍，悅之。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was crown prince, he entered to attend her and was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: While still crown prince, Gaozong visited her and became infatuated.

sentences.zh: 王后後久無子，蕭淑妃方幸，后陰不悅。

translations.literal: Empress Wang afterward long had no sons; Concubine Xiao Shuji was then favored—the empress was secretly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang had long been childless, while Concubine Xiao Shuji now held the emperor's favor; the empress resented this in secret.

sentences.zh: 它日，帝過佛廬，才人見且泣，帝感動。

translations.literal: Another day the emperor passed the Buddhist lodge; the Talented Lady saw him and wept—the emperor was moved.
translations.idiomatic: One day, as the emperor passed the convent, Wu saw him and wept; he was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 后廉知狀，引內後宮，以撓妃寵。

translations.literal: The empress learned the circumstance, brought her into the inner palace, to check the concubine's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang learned what had happened and brought Wu back into the inner palace, intending to use her to undercut Xiao's influence.

sentences.zh: 才人有權數，詭變不窮。

translations.literal: The Talented Lady had schemes of power, craft and shifts without end.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was resourceful and treacherous, with stratagems that never ran dry.

sentences.zh: 始，下辭降體事后，后喜，數譽於帝，故進為昭儀。

translations.literal: At first she lowered her words and humbled her body before the empress; the empress was pleased and often praised her to the emperor, hence she was advanced to Bright Consort.
translations.idiomatic: At first she spoke humbly and deferred to the empress, who was delighted and praised her often to the emperor, so Wu was promoted to Bright Consort.

sentences.zh: 一旦顧幸在蕭右，寖與后不協。

translations.literal: Once imperial favor fell on Xiao's side, she gradually fell out with the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor's favor shifted toward Xiao, Wu slowly turned against the empress.

sentences.zh: 后性簡重，不曲事上下，而母柳見內人尚宮無浮禮，故昭儀伺后所薄，必款結之，得賜予，盡以分遺。

translations.literal: The empress was by nature plain and grave, not bending to serve those above and below; her mother Liu saw that inner women and the Chief of Palace had no empty ceremony—so the Bright Consort watched whom the empress slighted and always formed warm ties, dividing all gifts received among them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang was reserved and upright and did not court those above or below her. Her mother Liu noticed that senior palace women such as the Chief of Palace disliked empty flattery, so Wu befriended everyone the empress neglected and shared every gift she received among them.

sentences.zh: 由是后及妃所為必得，得輒以聞，然未有以中也。

translations.literal: Hence whatever the empress and concubine did was always learned; once learned it was reported—but none could yet be struck down by it.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Wu learned everything Wang and Xiao did and reported it at once, yet she still lacked proof that would bring them down.

sentences.zh: 昭儀生女，后就顧弄，去，昭儀潛斃兒衾下，伺帝至，陽為歡言，發衾視兒，死矣。

translations.literal: The Bright Consort bore a daughter; the empress came to look and play, then left. The Bright Consort secretly smothered the child beneath the coverlet. When the emperor arrived she feigned merry speech, then lifted the coverlet—the child was dead.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu bore a daughter, Wang came to visit and played with the infant, then left. Wu secretly smothered the child under the bedding. When the emperor arrived she spoke cheerfully, then lifted the covers—the baby was dead.

sentences.zh: 又驚問左右，皆曰：「后適來。」

translations.literal: She feigned shock and asked those about—all said: "The empress had just come.
translations.idiomatic: She feigned horror and questioned the attendants; all said, "The empress had just been here.

sentences.zh: 昭儀即悲涕，帝不能察，怒曰：「后殺吾女，往與妃相讒媢，今又爾邪！」

translations.literal: The Bright Consort at once wept in grief. The emperor could not discern the truth and raged: "The empress killed my daughter—before she slandered each other with the concubine, and now this again!
translations.idiomatic: Wu burst into tears. Unable to see through the ruse, the emperor raged, "The empress killed my child! She and Xiao have slandered each other before, and now this again!

sentences.zh: 由是昭儀得入其訾，后無以自解，而帝愈信愛，始有廢后意。

translations.literal: Hence the Bright Consort could lodge her accusations; the empress had no way to clear herself, and the emperor believed and loved her all the more—he first harbored intent to depose the empress.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Wu could press her accusations unchecked. Wang could not defend herself, and the emperor trusted Wu all the more—he first began to consider deposing the empress.

sentences.zh: 久之，欲進號「宸妃」，侍中韓瑗、中書令來濟言：「妃嬪有數，今別立號，不可。」

translations.literal: Long afterward he wished to advance her title to "Consort of the Inner Court." Attendant-in-Waiting Han Yuan and Chancellor Lai Ji said: "Consorts and concubines are of fixed number; to establish a separate title now is not permissible."
translations.idiomatic: After some time he wished to create for her the new title "Consort of the Inner Court." Han Yuan, attendant-in-waiting, and Chancellor Lai Ji objected: "The ranks of consorts are fixed by statute; you cannot invent a new title."

sentences.zh: 昭儀乃誣后與母厭勝，帝挾前憾，實其言，將遂廢之。

translations.literal: The Bright Consort then accused the empress and her mother of witchcraft against harm. The emperor, nursing prior resentment, credited her words and was about to depose the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Wu then accused Wang and her mother of witchcraft. The emperor, still angry over the child's death, believed her and prepared to depose Wang.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌、褚遂良、韓瑗及濟瀕死固爭，帝猶豫；

translations.literal: Changsun Wuji, Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, and Ji argued to the death in protest—the emperor hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Wuji, Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, and Lai Ji argued fiercely against the move, even at the risk of their lives, and the emperor hesitated.

sentences.zh: 而中書舍人李義府、衛尉卿許敬宗素險側，狙勢即表請昭儀為后，帝意決，下詔廢后。

translations.literal: But Secretariat Drafter Li Yifu and Commandant of the Guard Xu Jingzong, by nature crafty and crooked, spied the trend and at once memorialized to make the Bright Consort empress. The emperor's mind was settled; he issued an edict deposing the empress.
translations.idiomatic: But Li Yifu, a secretariat drafter, and Xu Jingzong, commandant of the guard—both unscrupulous men—sensed which way power was moving and immediately petitioned to make Wu empress. The emperor's resolve hardened, and he issued an edict deposing Wang.

sentences.zh: 詔李勣、于志寧奉璽綬進昭儀為皇后，命群臣及四夷酋長朝后肅義門，內外命婦入謁。

translations.literal: He ordered Li Ji and Yu Zhining to bear the seal and sash and advance the Bright Consort as empress; he commanded ministers and chieftains of the four barbarians to attend the empress at Suoyi Gate; ladies within and without the palace entered to pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Li Ji and Yu Zhining to present the seal and sash and invest Wu as empress, commanded civil and military officials and the chiefs of the four frontier peoples to attend her at Suoyi Gate, and required all titled women inside and outside the palace to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 朝皇后自此始。

translations.literal: Court audience to the empress began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: Formal court audiences for the empress began from that day.

sentences.zh: 后見宗廟，再贈士彠至司徒，爵周國公，謚忠孝，配食高祖廟。

translations.literal: When the empress appeared at the ancestral temple, Shi Yi was posthumously promoted again to Minister of Works, enfeoffed Duke of Zhou with posthumous title Loyal and Filial, receiving sacrifice in the temple of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu was presented at the ancestral temple, her father Shiyi was posthumously raised to Minister of Works, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhou with the posthumous title Loyal and Filial, and granted a place in the shrine of Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 母楊，再封代國夫人，家食魏千戶。

translations.literal: Her mother Yang was again enfeoffed Lady of Dai, the household receiving a stipend of a thousand households from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Yang was again enfeoffed as Lady of Dai, with a household stipend of a thousand households drawn from Wei.

sentences.zh: 后乃製《外戚誡》獻諸朝，解釋譏譟。

translations.literal: The empress then composed Admonitions on Imperial Kin and presented them to the court, explaining away ridicule and clamor.
translations.idiomatic: Wu then wrote Admonitions for Imperial Kin and presented them to the court to answer the public mockery.

sentences.zh: 於是逐無忌、遂良，踵死徙，寵煽赫然。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wuji and Suiliang were driven out; deaths and banishments followed in succession, and imperial favor blazed conspicuously.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Changsun Wuji and Chu Suiliang were driven from power; executions and exiles followed one after another, and Wu's influence burned bright.

sentences.zh: 后城宇深，痛柔屈不恥，以就大事，帝謂能奉己，故扳公議立之。

translations.literal: The empress's mind was deep as a fortress; she deemed soft yielding no shame in attaining the great aim. The emperor thought she could serve him, and thus marshaled public opinion to install her.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was inwardly shrewd and felt no shame in bending low to reach her goal. The emperor believed she would defer to him, and so he overcame opposition to make her empress.

sentences.zh: 已得志，即盜威福，施施無憚避，帝亦懦昏，舉能鉗勒，使不得專，久稍不平。

translations.literal: Once her aim was gained, she at once usurped authority and favor, moving at ease without fear or avoidance. The emperor too was timid and dull; only together could they clamp and bridle her so she could not monopolize power—after long time he grew somewhat resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned she seized power openly and acted without restraint. Gaozong was weak and indecisive; only when he and his ministers worked together could they check her, and in time he grew quietly resentful.

sentences.zh: 麟德初，后召方士郭行真入禁中為蠱祝，宦人王伏勝發之，帝怒，因是召西臺侍郎上官儀，儀指言后專恣，失海內望，不可承宗廟，與帝意合，乃趣使草詔廢之。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Linde, the empress summoned the adept Guo Xingzhen into the forbidden quarters for witchcraft rites. Eunuch Wang Fusheng exposed it; the emperor was angry and on that account summoned Secretariat Vice Director Shangguan Yi. Yi pointed out that the empress was willful and exclusive, had lost the hope of the realm, and could not inherit the ancestral temples—the emperor's thought aligned, and he hurried him to draft an edict of deposition.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Linde era Wu summoned the magician Guo Xingzhen into the inner palace to perform sorcery. The eunuch Wang Fusheng reported it, and the enraged emperor summoned Shangguan Yi, vice director of the Secretariat. Yi declared that the empress was domineering, had forfeited the people's trust, and was unfit to receive the ancestral rites. The emperor agreed and ordered him to draft a deposition edict at once.

sentences.zh: 左右馳告，后遽從帝自訴，帝羞縮，待之如初，猶意其恚，且曰：「是皆上官儀教我！」

translations.literal: Attendants rushed to inform her; the empress hurriedly followed the emperor to plead in person. The emperor shrank in shame and treated her as before, still thinking her resentful, and said: "It was all Shangguan Yi who taught me!"
translations.idiomatic: Servants rushed to warn her. Wu ran after the emperor and pleaded her case in person. Ashamed, he relented and treated her as before, still fearing her anger, and said, "Shangguan Yi put me up to this!"

sentences.zh: 后諷許敬宗構儀，殺之。

translations.literal: The empress prompted Xu Jingzong to frame Shangguan Yi, and he was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wu then had Xu Jingzong fabricate charges against Shangguan Yi, and Yi was executed.

sentences.zh: 初，元舅大臣怫旨，不閱歲屠覆，道路目語，及儀見誅，則政歸房帷，天子拱手矣。

translations.literal: At first, maternal uncles and great ministers who offended the imperial will were slaughtered and overthrown within the year; people exchanged glances on the roads. When Yi was executed, government returned to the inner chambers, and the Son of Heaven merely folded his hands.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, any maternal uncle or senior minister who crossed her was ruined within the year, and the streets buzzed with whispered fear. Once Shangguan Yi was killed, power passed behind the curtain, and the emperor stood idle with folded hands.

sentences.zh: 群臣朝、四方奏章，皆曰「二聖」。

translations.literal: When the ministers attended court and memorials arrived from the four quarters, all spoke of the "Two Sages."
translations.idiomatic: At court and in memorials from every province, officials now addressed them as the Two Sages.

sentences.zh: 每視朝，殿中垂簾，帝與后偶坐，生殺賞罰惟所命。

translations.literal: At each audience the hall hung curtains; the emperor and empress sat as a pair, and life, death, reward, and punishment followed their command alone.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they held court, curtains were drawn in the hall while emperor and empress sat side by side; who lived, who died, who was honored or punished—all was theirs to decide.

sentences.zh: 當其忍斷，雖甚愛，不少隱也。

translations.literal: When she resolved to be ruthless, even those she greatly loved received no lenience.
translations.idiomatic: Once she set her mind to cruelty, not even those she cherished were spared.

sentences.zh: 帝晚益病風不支，天下事一付后。

translations.literal: In his later years the emperor's wind ailment worsened until he could not sustain himself; all affairs under Heaven were entrusted entirely to the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong grew weaker with age, crippled by recurring strokes, until every matter of state was left in Wu's hands.

sentences.zh: 后乃更為太平文治事，大集諸儒內禁殿，撰定《列女傳》、《臣軌》、《百僚新誡》、《樂書》等，大氐千餘篇。

translations.literal: The empress then turned to peaceful civil governance, gathering many Confucian scholars within the forbidden halls to compile and fix works including Biographies of Exemplary Women, Tracks of Ministers, New Admonitions for the Hundred Officials, and Books of Music—altogether roughly more than a thousand chapters.
translations.idiomatic: She now styled herself a patron of peaceful rule, summoning scholars into the inner palace to produce Biographies of Exemplary Women, Tracks of Ministers, New Admonitions for Officials, treatises on music, and the like—well over a thousand chapters in all.

sentences.zh: 因令學士密裁可奏議，分宰相權。

translations.literal: She therefore had academicians secretly screen and draft memorials fit for presentation, dividing the chancellors' power.
translations.idiomatic: She also had palace scholars secretly vet and draft policy memorials, carving away the chancellors' authority.

sentences.zh: 始，士彠娶相里氏，生子元慶、元爽。

translations.literal: At first Shi Shi married a woman of the Xiangli clan and had sons Yuangqing and Yuanshuang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shi had first married into the Xiangli family and fathered Yuangqing and Yuanshuang.

sentences.zh: 又娶楊氏，生三女：伯嫁賀蘭越石，蚤寡，封韓國夫人；

translations.literal: He also married the Yang clan and had three daughters: the eldest married Helan Yueshi, was widowed early, and was enfeoffed Lady of Han;
translations.idiomatic: He later married Lady Yang, who bore three daughters. The eldest wed Helan Yueshi, was widowed young, and received the title Lady of Han;

sentences.zh: 仲即后；

translations.literal: the middle daughter was the empress;
translations.idiomatic: the second was Wu herself;

sentences.zh: 季嫁郭孝慎，前死。

translations.literal: the youngest married Guo Xiaoshen and died before him.
translations.idiomatic: the youngest married Guo Xiaoshen and predeceased him.

sentences.zh: 楊以后故，寵日盛，徙封榮國。

translations.literal: Because of the empress, the Yang clan's favor grew daily, and they were transferred to the enfeoffment of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Wu, the Yang family's influence swelled day by day, and their fief was raised to the state of Rong.

sentences.zh: 始，兄子惟良、懷運與元慶等遇楊及后禮薄，后銜不置。

translations.literal: At first her brother's sons Weiliang and Huaiyun, together with Yuangqing and the rest, treated the Yang clan and the empress with slight ceremony; the empress brooded on this without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Her cousins Weiliang and Huaiyun, along with Yuangqing and his brothers, had once shown the Yang women scant courtesy, and Wu never forgave it.

sentences.zh: 及是，元慶為宗正少卿，元爽少府少監，惟良司衛少卿，懷運淄州刺史。

translations.literal: At this time Yuangqing was Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, Yuanshuang Vice Director of the Palace Stores, Weiliang Vice Director of the Guards, and Huaiyun prefect of Zi.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yuangqing served as vice director of the imperial clan office, Yuanshuang in the palace stores, Weiliang in the guard bureau, and Huaiyun as prefect of Zi.

sentences.zh: 它日，夫人置酒，酣，謂惟良曰：「若等記疇日事乎？

translations.literal: Another day the Lady of Yang held a feast; when drunk, she said to Weiliang: "Do you recall affairs of former days?
translations.idiomatic: One evening Lady Yang held a banquet, and when the wine had gone deep she asked Weiliang, "Do you remember how you treated us in the old days?

sentences.zh: 今謂何？」

translations.literal: What do you say now?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you say to that now?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「幸以功臣子位朝廷，晚緣戚屬進，憂而不榮也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Fortunate to hold court office as a meritorious minister's son, yet advanced late through kinship—I am anxious, not honored."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I am lucky to hold office as a hero's son, but to rise so late only through kinship fills me with dread, not pride."

sentences.zh: 夫人怒，諷后偽為退讓，請惟良等外遷，無示天下私。

translations.literal: The Lady was angry; she prompted the empress to feign yielding and request that Weiliang and the others be transferred outward, lest the realm see private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang flew into a rage and urged Wu to play at modesty, asking that Weiliang and the others be sent to distant posts so the court would not look partial.

sentences.zh: 繇是，惟良為始州刺史；

translations.literal: Thereupon Weiliang became prefect of Shi;
translations.idiomatic: Weiliang was made prefect of Shi;

sentences.zh: 元慶，龍州；

translations.literal: Yuangqing, Long prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Yuangqing was sent to Long;

sentences.zh: 元爽，濠州，俄坐事死振州。

translations.literal: Yuanshuang, Hao prefecture—soon he died at Zhen for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshuang to Hao, and soon he was condemned and died in exile at Zhen.

sentences.zh: 元慶至州，憂死。

translations.literal: Yuangqing reached his prefecture and died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangqing reached his post and died of despair.

sentences.zh: 韓國出入禁中，一女國姝，帝皆寵之。

translations.literal: The Lady of Han came and went within the forbidden quarters; a daughter was a national beauty, and the emperor doted on both.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Han moved freely in the inner palace; her daughter was famed as the empire's fairest, and the emperor favored them both.

sentences.zh: 韓國卒，女封魏國夫人，欲以備嬪職，難於后，未決。

translations.literal: When the Lady of Han died, the daughter was enfeoffed Lady of Wei; the emperor wished to install her among the consorts, but it was difficult before the empress, and he did not decide.
translations.idiomatic: After the Lady of Han's death her daughter was titled Lady of Wei. The emperor meant to bring her into the harem, but Wu stood in the way, and he hesitated.

sentences.zh: 后內忌甚，會封泰山，惟良、懷運以嶽牧來集，從還京師，后毒殺魏國，歸罪惟良等，盡殺之，氏曰「蝮」，以韓國子敏之奉士彠祀。

translations.literal: The empress harbored deep jealousy within. When the fengshan at Mount Tai occurred, Weiliang and Huaiyun came as regional governors of the sacred peak; on the return to the capital the empress poisoned the Lady of Wei, blamed Weiliang and the rest, and killed them all. The clan was called "Viper"; the Lady of Han's son Minzhi was left to tend Shi Shi's sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Wu burned with jealousy. During the Mount Tai fengshan, Weiliang and Huaiyun arrived as attending governors and followed the court back to Chang'an. She poisoned the Lady of Wei, pinned the crime on her cousins, and wiped out the line, branding the clan Viper. Only Minzhi, son of the Lady of Han, survived to keep Shi Shi's ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 初，魏國卒，敏之入弔，帝為慟，敏之哭不對。

translations.literal: When the Lady of Wei first died, Minzhi came to mourn; the emperor was grief-stricken, but Minzhi wept without responding properly.
translations.idiomatic: At the Lady of Wei's funeral Minzhi came to mourn while the emperor wept openly, yet Minzhi's grief rang hollow.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「兒疑我！」

translations.literal: The empress said: "The boy suspects me!"
translations.idiomatic: Wu said, "The boy thinks I killed her!"

sentences.zh: 惡之。

translations.literal: She hated him.
translations.idiomatic: She came to despise him.

sentences.zh: 俄貶死。

translations.literal: Soon he was demoted and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was disgraced and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 楊氏徙酇、衛二國，咸亨元年卒，追封魯國，謚忠烈，詔文武九品以上及五等親與外命婦赴弔，以王禮葬咸陽，給班劍、葆杖、鼓吹。

translations.literal: The Yang clan was transferred to the states of Zan and Wei. In the first year of Xianheng the mother died; she was posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Lu, posthumous title Loyal and Fierce.
