An edict ordered all civil and military officials of the ninth rank and above, plus fifth-rank kin and titled ladies, to attend the mourning. She was buried at Xianyang with princely rites, given ceremonial swords, canes, and drums.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang women were raised to the states of Zan and Wei. Lady Yang died in the first year of Xianheng and was posthumously made Princess of Lu with the epithet Loyal and Fierce. Officials of the ninth rank and above, close kin of the fifth degree, and titled ladies were ordered to mourn her. She was buried at Xianyang with princely honors, escorted by ceremonial arms, staffs, and music.

sentences.zh: 時天下旱，后偽表求避位，不許。

translations.literal: At that time the realm suffered drought; the empress submitted a feigned memorial asking to retire from position, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: A drought gripped the empire, and Wu sent a show memorial offering to step down; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 俄又贈士彠太尉兼太子太師、太原郡王，魯國忠烈夫人為妃。

translations.literal: Soon Shi Shi was posthumously made Grand Commander and concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and Prince of Taiyuan; the Loyal and Fierce Lady of Lu became princess consort.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shi was soon posthumously made grand commander, grand preceptor of the crown prince, and Prince of Taiyuan, while his wife became princess consort of Lu with the epithet Loyal and Fierce.

sentences.zh: 上元元年，進號天后，建言十二事：一、勸農桑，薄賦徭；

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan her title was advanced to Tianhou; she proposed twelve matters: first, promote agriculture and sericulture, lighten taxes and corvée;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shangyuan she took the title Tianhou and offered twelve reforms: first, encourage farming and sericulture and reduce taxes and labor levies;

sentences.zh: 二、給復三輔地；

translations.literal: second, grant exemptions in the lands of the Three Metropolises;
translations.idiomatic: second, grant tax relief in the capital region;

sentences.zh: 三、息兵，以道德化天下；

translations.literal: third, rest the armies and transform the realm through moral virtue;
translations.idiomatic: third, halt warfare and govern the realm through moral example;

sentences.zh: 四、南北中尚禁浮巧；

translations.literal: fourth, in the northern, southern, and central inner palaces forbid frivolous craft;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, ban extravagant crafts in the inner palaces;

sentences.zh: 五、省功費力役；

translations.literal: fifth, reduce works, expenses, and forced labor;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, cut public works, spending, and corvée;

sentences.zh: 六、廣言路；

translations.literal: sixth, broaden the path of speech;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, widen channels for candid memorials;

sentences.zh: 七、杜讒口；

translations.literal: seventh, stop slanderous mouths;
translations.idiomatic: seventh, suppress malicious rumor;

sentences.zh: 八、王公以降皆習《老子》；

translations.literal: eighth, from princes and dukes downward all should study the Laozi;
translations.idiomatic: eighth, require princes and officials alike to study the Daodejing;

sentences.zh: 九、父在為母服齊衰三年；

translations.literal: ninth, while the father lives, observe three years of coarse hemp mourning for the mother;
translations.idiomatic: ninth, mandate three years of mourning for one's mother even while the father still lives;

sentences.zh: 十、上元前勛官已給告身者無追核；

translations.literal: tenth, for merit offices before Shangyuan whose commission documents had already been issued, do not pursue verification;
translations.idiomatic: tenth, stop investigating merit offices whose patents were issued before Shangyuan;

sentences.zh: 十一、京官八品以上益稟入；

translations.literal: eleventh, for capital officials of the eighth rank and above, increase salary allotments;
translations.idiomatic: eleventh, raise stipends for capital officials of the eighth rank and above;

sentences.zh: 十二、百官任事久，材高位下者得進階申滯。

translations.literal: twelfth, for the hundred officials who have served long, those whose talent exceeds their rank and station may advance in grade and declare their stagnation relieved.
translations.idiomatic: twelfth, promote long-serving officials whose ability outran their rank.

sentences.zh: 帝皆下詔略施行之。

translations.literal: The emperor issued edicts on all and broadly enacted them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promulgated edicts and put most of them into effect.

sentences.zh: 蕭妃女義陽、宣城公主幽掖廷，幾四十不嫁，太子弘言於帝，后怒，酖殺弘。

translations.literal: The daughters of Consort Xiao, the Princesses of Yiyang and Xuancheng, were confined in the palace women quarters, nearly forty years unwed. Crown Prince Hong spoke to the emperor; the empress was furious and killed Hong with poisoned wine.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Xiao's daughters, the princesses of Yiyang and Xuancheng, languished in the palace women's quarters, unmarried for nearly forty years. When Crown Prince Hong pleaded their case to the emperor, Wu flew into a rage and poisoned him.

sentences.zh: 帝將下詔遜位於后，宰相郝處俊固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to issue an edict yielding the throne to the empress; Chancellor Hao Chujun firmly remonstrated, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong nearly issued an edict abdicating in Wu's favor, but Chancellor Hao Chujun protested so fiercely that he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 后欲外示寬裕，劫人心使歸已，即奏言：「今群臣納半俸、百姓計口錢以贍邊兵，恐四方妄商虛實，請一罷之。」

translations.literal: The empress wished outwardly to show magnanimity and seize people's hearts so they would turn to her; she memorialized: "Now the ministers pay half salaries and the common people pay per-capita levies to support border troops—fearing the four quarters will recklessly trade on false reports of strength and weakness, I request that these all be abolished at once."
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to look generous while binding men's loyalty to herself, she memorialized, "Officials now surrender half their salaries and commoners pay head taxes to fund the border armies. Such burdens invite false boasting about our strength. I ask that both be abolished."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved her request.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳三年，群臣、蕃夷長朝後於光順門。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yifeng, ministers and tribal chieftains attended court before the empress at Guangshun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yifeng, ministers and foreign chiefs paid court to Wu at Guangshun Gate.

sentences.zh: 即并州建太原郡王廟。

translations.literal: At once a temple to the Prince of Taiyuan was built in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine to the Prince of Taiyuan was erected in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝頭眩不能視，侍醫張文仲、秦鳴鶴曰：「風上逆，砭頭血可愈。」

translations.literal: The emperor's head swam and he could not see; attending physicians Zhang Wenzong and Qin Minghe said: "Wind rises upward in reversal; bleeding the head with needles can cure it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suffered dizzy blindness, and his physicians Zhang Wenzong and Qin Minghe said, "Wind is rising into the head. Lancing the scalp to draw blood should restore his sight."

sentences.zh: 后內幸帝殆，得自專，怒曰：「是可斬，帝體寧刺血處邪？」

translations.literal: The empress inwardly rejoiced that the emperor might perish and she could rule alone; angrily she said: "These deserve execution—may the imperial body be pricked for blood?"
translations.idiomatic: Wu secretly hoped the emperor would die so she could rule alone, and she raged, "They deserve death! Would you pierce the Son of Heaven's flesh?"

sentences.zh: 醫頓首請命。

translations.literal: The physicians kowtowed and begged for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: The doctors kowtowed and begged for mercy.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「醫議疾，烏可罪？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Physicians discuss illness—how can they be punished?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "They speak as healers must. How can that be a crime?

sentences.zh: 且吾眩不可堪，聽為之！」

translations.literal: Moreover my dizziness is unbearable—let them do it!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, this dizziness is unbearable. Let them treat me!"

sentences.zh: 醫一再刺，帝曰：「吾目明矣！」

translations.literal: The physicians pricked again and again; the emperor said: "My eyes are clear!"
translations.idiomatic: They lanced him again and again until he cried, "I can see!"

sentences.zh: 言未畢，后簾中再拜謝，曰：「天賜我師！」

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking, the empress behind the curtain bowed twice in thanks and said: "Heaven has given me these masters!"
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished, Wu bowed from behind the curtain and exclaimed, "Heaven sent me these physicians!"

sentences.zh: 身負繒寶以賜。

translations.literal: She carried silk treasures on her person to bestow.
translations.idiomatic: She loaded them with silk and jewels.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，中宗即位，天后稱皇太后，遺詔軍國大務聽參決。

translations.literal: The emperor died; Zhongzong ascended the throne; Tianhou styled herself Empress Dowager; the testamentary edict ordered that great affairs of army and state be heard and decided with her participation.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong died, Zhongzong took the throne while Wu styled herself empress dowager. The late emperor's edict left military and civil affairs to her joint decision.

sentences.zh: 嗣聖元年，太后廢帝為廬陵王，自臨朝，以睿宗即帝位。

translations.literal: In the first year of Sisheng the dowager deposed the emperor as Prince of Luling, herself presided over court, and had Ruizong ascend the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Sisheng she deposed Zhongzong as Prince of Luling, ruled in person, and installed Ruizong as emperor.

sentences.zh: 后坐武成殿，帝率群臣上號冊。

translations.literal: The empress sat in Wucheng Hall; the emperor led the ministers in presenting title documents.
translations.idiomatic: Wu took her seat in Wucheng Hall while Ruizong led the ministers in presenting her honorific titles.

sentences.zh: 越三日，太后臨軒，命禮部尚書攝太尉武承嗣、太常卿攝司空王德真冊嗣皇帝。

translations.literal: After three days the dowager faced the throne hall and ordered Minister of Rites acting as Grand Commander Wu Chengsi and Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple acting as Minister of Works Wang Dezhen to invest the successor emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later she held court and had Wu Chengsi, minister of rites acting as grand commander, and Wang Dezhen, director of the ancestral temple acting as minister of works, perform Ruizong's enthronement rites.

sentences.zh: 自是太后常御紫宸殿，施慘紫帳臨朝。

translations.literal: From this time the dowager regularly held court in Zichen Hall, draping a somber purple curtain to preside.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter she habitually held court in Zichen Hall behind a purple curtain.

sentences.zh: 追贈五世祖後魏散騎常侍克己為魯國公，妣裴即其國為夫人；

translations.literal: Her fifth-generation ancestor, Northern Wei Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Keji, was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Lu; mother Pei was made Lady of that state;
translations.idiomatic: She posthumously enfeoffed her fifth-generation ancestor Keji, a Northern Wei attendant, as Duke of Lu, with Lady Pei as his consort;

sentences.zh: 高祖齊殷州司馬居常為太尉、北平郡王，妣劉為王妃；

translations.literal: great-grandfather Juchang, Qi prefecture of Yin military aide, as Grand Commander and Prince of Beiping, mother Liu as princess consort;
translations.idiomatic: her great-grandfather Juchang, a Qi military aide, as grand commander and Prince of Beiping, with Lady Liu as princess consort;

sentences.zh: 曾祖永昌王諮議參軍、贈齊州刺史儉為太尉、金城郡王，妣宋為王妃；

translations.literal: great-great-grandfather Jian, staff adviser to the Prince of Yongchang and posthumous prefect of Qi, as Grand Commander and Prince of Jincheng, mother Song as princess consort;
translations.idiomatic: her great-great-grandfather Jian, once an adviser to the Prince of Yongchang and posthumous prefect of Qi, as grand commander and Prince of Jincheng, with Lady Song as princess consort;

sentences.zh: 祖隋東郡丞、贈并州刺史、大都督華為太尉、太原郡王，妣趙為王妃。

translations.literal: grandfather Hua, Sui assistant magistrate of Dong commandery, posthumous prefect of Bing and grand protector, as Grand Commander and Prince of Taiyuan, mother Zhao as princess consort.
translations.idiomatic: her grandfather Hua, a Sui eastern commandery aide later honored as prefect of Bing, as grand commander and Prince of Taiyuan, with Lady Zhao as princess consort.

sentences.zh: 皆置園邑，戶五十。

translations.literal: For all, park estates were established with fifty households each.
translations.idiomatic: Each received a tomb estate staffed with fifty households.

sentences.zh: 考為太師、魏王，加實戶滿五千，妣為王妃，王園邑守戶百。

translations.literal: Her father was made Grand Preceptor and Prince of Wei, with added real households up to five thousand; her mother was princess consort; the prince's park estate had one hundred guarding households.
translations.idiomatic: Her father became grand preceptor and Prince of Wei with five thousand taxable households added to his fief; her mother became princess consort, and his tomb estate was granted a hundred guardian households.

sentences.zh: 時睿宗雖立，實囚之，而諸武擅命。

translations.literal: At this time although Ruizong was installed, in truth he was imprisoned, while the various Wu kin issued commands at will.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong sat on the throne in name only, kept under house arrest while the Wu clan ruled unchecked.

sentences.zh: 又謚魯國公曰靖，裴為靖夫人；

translations.literal: Further, the Duke of Lu was given posthumous title Jing, and Pei was Lady Jing;
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Lu was posthumously titled Jing, and Lady Pei became Lady Jing;

sentences.zh: 北平郡王曰恭肅，金城郡王曰義康，太原郡王曰安成，妃從夫謚。

translations.literal: the Prince of Beiping was titled Respectful and Solemn, the Prince of Jincheng Righteous and Tranquil, the Prince of Taiyuan Secure and Accomplished; consorts followed their husbands' posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Beiping was titled Respectful and Solemn, the Prince of Jincheng Righteous and Tranquil, and the Prince of Taiyuan Secure and Accomplished, their consorts taking matching epithets.

sentences.zh: 太后遣冊武成殿使者告五世廟室。

translations.literal: The dowager sent envoys bearing investiture documents from Wucheng Hall to announce to the five-generation temple chambers.
translations.idiomatic: She dispatched envoys from Wucheng Hall to announce the honors at the five-generation ancestral shrines.

sentences.zh: 於是柳州司馬李敬業、括蒼令唐之奇、臨海丞駱賓王疾太后脅逐天子，不勝憤，乃募兵殺揚州大都督府長史陳敬之，據州欲迎廬陵王，眾至十萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Jingye, military aide of Liuzhou; Tang Zhiqi, magistrate of Kuocang; and Luo Binwang, assistant magistrate of Linhai—grieved that the dowager coerced and drove out the Son of Heaven, unable to bear their fury—raised troops, killed Chen Jingzhi, chief administrator of the Yangzhou metropolitan prefecture, seized the prefecture intending to welcome the Prince of Luling, and their host reached one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingye of Liuzhou, Tang Zhiqi of Kuocang, and Luo Binwang of Linhai, outraged that the dowager had bullied the emperor from his throne, raised an army. They killed Chen Jingzhi, chief administrator of Yangzhou, seized the prefecture to restore the Prince of Luling, and gathered a force of one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 楚州司馬李崇福連和。

translations.literal: Li Chongfu, military aide of Chuzhou, joined in alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongfu, military aide of Chuzhou, joined their cause.

sentences.zh: 盱眙人劉行舉嬰城不肯從，敬業攻之，不克。

translations.literal: Liu Xingju of Xuyi closed his walls and refused to follow; Jingye attacked him and could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xingju of Xuyi barred his gates and refused to submit. Jingye besieged him without success.

sentences.zh: 太后拜行舉遊擊將軍，擢其弟行實楚州刺史。

translations.literal: The dowager invested Xingju as Mobile Strike General and promoted his younger brother Xingshi to prefect of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu rewarded Xingju with the title Mobile Strike General and made his brother Xingshi prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 敬業南度江取潤州，殺刺史李思文，曲阿令尹元貞拒戰死。

translations.literal: Jingye crossed the river south and seized Run prefecture, killing Prefect Li Siwen; Yin Yuanzhen, magistrate of Qu'e, resisted in battle and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye crossed the Yangzi, seized Runzhou, and killed its prefect Li Siwen. Yin Yuanzhen, magistrate of Qu'e, resisted and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 太后詔左玉鈐衛大將軍李孝逸為揚州道行軍大總管，率兵三十萬討之，戰於高郵，前鋒左豹韜果毅成三朗為唐之奇所殺。

translations.literal: The dowager edicted Left Jade Bell Guard General Li Xiaoyi as Grand Commander of the Yangzhou campaign army, leading three hundred thousand troops to suppress them. They fought at Gaoyou; vanguard Left Leopard Bow Commander Cheng Sanlang was killed by Tang Zhiqi.
translations.idiomatic: She appointed Li Xiaoyi of the Left Jade Bell Guard grand commander of the Yangzhou campaign with three hundred thousand men. At Gaoyou the rebel Tang Zhiqi slew her vanguard commander Cheng Sanlang.

sentences.zh: 又以左鷹揚衛大將軍黑齒常之為江南道行軍大總管，並力。

translations.literal: She also made Left Eagle Yang Guard General Heichi Changzhi Grand Commander of the Jiangnan campaign army, joining forces.
translations.idiomatic: She also named Heichi Changzhi of the Left Eagle Yang Guard grand commander of the Jiangnan front to strike in concert.

sentences.zh: 敬業興三月敗，傳首東都，三州平。

translations.literal: Jingye rose and in three months was defeated; his head was sent to the eastern capital; the three prefectures were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The rebellion lasted three months before Jingye was crushed. His head was sent to Luoyang, and the three prefectures were pacified.

sentences.zh: 始，武承嗣請太后立七廟，中書令裴炎沮止，及敬業之興，下炎獄，殺之，並殺左威衛大將軍程務挺。

translations.literal: At first Wu Chengsi asked the dowager to establish seven temples; Secretariat Director Pei Yan obstructed and stopped it. When Jingye rose, Yan was cast into prison and killed, and Left Majestic Guard General Cheng Wuting was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wu Chengsi had urged her to erect a seven-temple ancestral line, but Chancellor Pei Yan blocked it. After Jingye's revolt she imprisoned and executed Yan, and killed Cheng Wuting of the Left Majestic Guard as well.

sentences.zh: 太后方怫恚，一日，召群臣廷讓曰：「朕於天下無負，若等知之乎？」

translations.literal: The dowager was just then resentful and furious; one day she summoned the ministers to rebuke them in court and said: "I owe nothing to the realm under Heaven—do you know this?"
translations.idiomatic: Still seething, she one day summoned the court and demanded, "I have wronged the empire in nothing. Do you understand that?"

sentences.zh: 群臣唯唯。

translations.literal: The ministers murmured assent.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers murmured agreement.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「朕輔先帝逾三十年，憂勞天下。

translations.literal: The dowager said: "I assisted the late emperor for more than thirty years, laboring in care for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: She continued, "I aided the late emperor for more than thirty years and bore the empire's burdens.

sentences.zh: 爵位富貴，朕所與也；

translations.literal: Ranks, titles, wealth, and honor—I am the one who gave them;
translations.idiomatic: Your ranks and riches came from my hand;

sentences.zh: 天下安佚，朕所養也。

translations.literal: the realm's peace and ease—I am the one who nurtured them.
translations.idiomatic: the peace you enjoy, I preserved.

sentences.zh: 先帝棄群臣，以社稷為托，朕不敢愛身，而知愛人。

translations.literal: The late emperor left the ministers and entrusted the altars of soil and grain; I dare not spare myself, yet I know how to cherish others.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor entrusted me with the state, I did not spare myself, and I have cared for you.

sentences.zh: 今為戎首者皆將相，何見負之遽？

translations.literal: Now those who become leaders of war are all ministers and generals—how is it that I am so quickly seen as owing them wrong?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the rebels were your own ministers and generals. How can you claim I wronged you?

sentences.zh: 且受遺老臣伉扈難制有若裴炎乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, is there among the testamentary old ministers one so haughty and hard to control as Pei Yan?
translations.idiomatic: Was Pei Yan, that arrogant survivor of the late emperor's council, not impossible to govern?

sentences.zh: 世將種能合亡命若徐敬業乎？

translations.literal: Can a hereditary general breed rally the desperate like Xu Jingye?
translations.idiomatic: Could any hereditary general but Xu Jingye rally desperate men as he did?

sentences.zh: 宿將善戰若程務挺乎？

translations.literal: An old commander skilled in battle like Cheng Wuting?
translations.idiomatic: Was Cheng Wuting, that seasoned warrior, not dangerous in his own right?

sentences.zh: 彼皆人豪，不利於朕，朕能戮之。

translations.literal: All were human heroes, harmful to me—I could slay them.
translations.idiomatic: They were formidable men, and I destroyed them when they threatened me.

sentences.zh: 公等才有過彼，蚤為之。

translations.literal: If your talents surpass theirs, do it early.
translations.idiomatic: If any of you think yourselves their betters, try it now.

sentences.zh: 不然，謹以事朕，無詒天下笑。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, serve me carefully and do not bring laughter upon the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise serve me faithfully, and do not make the empire laugh at your folly."

sentences.zh: 群臣頓首，不敢仰視，曰：「惟陛下命。」

translations.literal: The ministers kowtowed, not daring to look up, and said: "Only Your Majesty's command."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers kowtowed without raising their eyes and said, "We obey Your Majesty's command alone."
They spoke no further.

sentences.zh: 久之，下詔陽若復辟者。

translations.literal: After a long time, an edict was issued that outwardly resembled restoration of the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later she issued an edict that pretended to restore imperial rule.

sentences.zh: 睿宗揣非情，固請臨朝，制可。

translations.literal: Ruizong perceived this was not sincere, urgently petitioned to preside over court, and the decree approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong saw through the pretense and urgently petitioned to rule in person; the decree approved his request.

sentences.zh: 乃冶銅匭為一室，署東曰「延恩」，受干賞自言；

translations.literal: Then she cast a copper casket as one chamber; the east was labeled "Extended Grace," to receive pleas for merit rewards and self-recommendation;
translations.idiomatic: She had a copper casket cast as a single unit. The eastern slot, titled "Extended Grace," took submissions seeking rewards and self-promotion;

sentences.zh: 南曰「招諫」，受時政失得；

translations.literal: the south "Summoning Remonstrance," to receive the gains and losses of current governance;
translations.idiomatic: the southern, "Summoning Remonstrance," for criticism of policy successes and failures;

sentences.zh: 西曰「申冤」，受抑枉所欲言；

translations.literal: the west "Pleading Wrongs," to receive what the suppressed and wronged wished to say;
translations.idiomatic: the western, "Pleading Wrongs," for the grievances of the oppressed;

sentences.zh: 北曰「通玄」，受讖步秘策。

translations.literal: the north "Penetrating Mystery," to receive prophecies, divination, and secret stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: the northern, "Penetrating Mystery," for omens, divination, and secret plots.

sentences.zh: 詔中書門下一官典領。

translations.literal: An edict ordered one official of the Secretariat-Chancellery to oversee it.
translations.idiomatic: A Secretariat-Chancellery official was appointed to administer it.

sentences.zh: 太后不惜爵位，以籠四方豪傑自為助，雖妄男子，言有所合，輒不次官之，至不稱職，尋亦廢誅不少縱，務取實材真賢。

translations.literal: The dowager spared no ranks and titles to cage heroes of the four quarters as her own aides; even reckless men, if their words accorded with her aims, were at once given extraordinary appointments; if they proved unfit for office, soon they were dismissed, executed, and not spared in the least—she strove to obtain real talent and true worthies.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager lavished titles to win adventurers from every quarter. Even unscrupulous men won swift promotion if their counsel pleased her; the incompetent were soon removed or killed without mercy. She sought only proven ability and genuine talent.

sentences.zh: 又畏天下有謀反逆者，詔許上變，在所給輕傳，供五品食，送京師，即日召見，厚餌爵賞歆動之。

translations.literal: Also fearing rebels throughout the realm, she decreed that secret denunciations were permitted; locally they were given light relay transport, supplied fifth-rank rations, escorted to the capital, summoned that same day, and richly fed with ranks and rewards to stir their desire.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful of conspiracy, she invited secret denunciation. Informers received relay transport, fifth-rank rations, escort to the capital, and same-day audience, with rank and bounty to inflame their zeal.

sentences.zh: 凡言變，吏不得何詰，雖耘夫蕘子必親延見，稟之客館。

translations.literal: For any who reported changes, officers might not question them; even plowmen and firewood gatherers had to be personally received in audience and lodged in the guest quarters.
translations.idiomatic: No official might interrogate an informer. Even a farmer or woodcutter had to be received in person and lodged at the guesthouse.

sentences.zh: 敢稽若不送者，以所告罪之。

translations.literal: Those who dared delay and failed to forward them were punished with the crime they had reported.
translations.idiomatic: Delay or failure to forward a report was punished as the crime alleged.

sentences.zh: 故上變者遍天下，人人屏息，無敢議。

translations.literal: Thus informers spread throughout the realm; everyone held their breath, none daring to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: Informers spread everywhere. The realm fell silent; none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 新豐有山因震突出，太后以為美祥，赦其縣，更名慶山。

translations.literal: In Xinfeng a mountain protruded through an earthquake; the dowager regarded it as a beautiful omen, pardoned that county, and renamed it Celebratory Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: At Xinfeng an earthquake thrust up a mountain. The empress took it as a blessing, amnestied the county, and renamed it Qingshan, "Celebratory Mountain."

sentences.zh: 荊人俞文俊上言：「人不和，疣贅生；

translations.literal: A man of Jing, Yu Wenjun, memorialized: "When people are not in harmony, warts and excrescences grow;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenjun of Jing submitted a memorial: "When people fall out of harmony, warts and growths appear;

sentences.zh: 地不和，堆阜出。

translations.literal: when earth is not in harmony, mounds and hillocks emerge.
translations.idiomatic: when earth falls out of harmony, mounds rise up.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以女主處陽位，山變為災，非慶也。」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty as a woman ruler occupies the yang position; the mountain's change is disaster, not celebration."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rules as a woman in the yang station. This mountain is a calamity, not a blessing."

sentences.zh: 太后怒，投嶺外。

translations.literal: The dowager in anger exiled him beyond the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: In fury she banished him beyond the Ling ranges.

sentences.zh: 詔毀乾元殿為明堂，以浮屠薛懷義為使督作。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Qianyuan Hall destroyed to build the Bright Hall, with the monk Xue Huaiyi as commissioner to supervise construction.
translations.idiomatic: She decreed the Qianyuan Hall torn down for a Bright Hall and appointed the monk Xue Huaiyi commissioner of works.

sentences.zh: 懷義，鄠人，本馮氏，名小寶，偉岸淫毒，佯狂洛陽市，千金公主嬖之。

translations.literal: Huaiyi was a man of E, originally of the Feng clan, named Xiaobao; tall and virile, lustful and cruel, he feigned madness in Luoyang market; the Princess of a Thousand Gold favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi came from E, born Feng Xiaobao—a towering, vicious libertine who played the madman in Luoyang until the Princess of a Thousand Gold took him as her lover.

sentences.zh: 主上言：「小寶可入侍。」

translations.literal: The princess reported: "Xiaobao may enter attendance."
translations.idiomatic: The princess told her, "Xiaobao is fit to attend upon you."

sentences.zh: 后召與私，悅之。

translations.literal: The empress summoned him for intimacy and was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Wu summoned him privately and was delighted.

sentences.zh: 欲掩跡，得通籍出入，使祝髮為浮屠，拜白馬寺主。

translations.literal: Wishing to conceal traces, she obtained for him registry passage in and out, had him tonsured as a monk, and invested him abbot of White Horse Temple.
translations.idiomatic: To hide the affair she secured him palace registry rights, had him tonsured, and made him abbot of White Horse Temple.

sentences.zh: 詔與太平公主婿薛紹通昭穆，紹父事之。

translations.literal: An edict paired him in clan generation with Xue Shao, husband of Princess Taiping; Shao served him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him generational kin to Princess Taiping's husband Xue Shao, who was required to treat him as a father.

sentences.zh: 給廄馬，中官為騶侍，雖承嗣、三思皆尊事惟謹。

translations.literal: Stable horses were granted, eunuchs as outriders; even Chengsi and Sansi all honored him with utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: He received stable horses and eunuch outriders; even Wu Chengsi and Wu Sansi deferred to him with scrupulous respect.

sentences.zh: 至是護作，士數萬，巨木率一章千人乃能引。

translations.literal: At this time he oversaw construction; laborers numbered tens of thousands; great timbers on average required a thousand men of one fathom-team to draw them.
translations.idiomatic: Now overseeing the project, he commanded tens of thousands of workers; each great timber needed a thousand men to haul it.

sentences.zh: 又度明堂後為天堂，鴻麗巖奧次之。

translations.literal: Further he planned behind the Bright Hall a Hall of Paradise, grand and splendid, second only to its cavernous loftiness.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the Bright Hall he also laid out a Hall of Paradise, magnificent and second only to that hall in scale.

sentences.zh: 堂成，拜左威衛大將軍、梁國公。

translations.literal: When the hall was completed, he was appointed Left Weiwu Guard Grand General and Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When the hall was finished she made him Left Weiwu Guard grand general and Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 始作崇先廟於西京，享武氏。

translations.literal: For the first time the Venerating Ancestors Temple was built in the Western Capital to sacrifice to the Wu clan.
translations.idiomatic: She built the Venerating Ancestors Temple in the western capital for Wu clan sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 承嗣偽款洛水石，導使為帝，遣雍人唐同泰獻之，后號為「寶圖」，擢同泰遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Chengsi forged an inscription on a Luo River stone guiding one to become emperor; he sent Tang Tongtai of Yong to present it; the empress titled it "Treasure Chart," and promoted Tongtai to Mobile Strike General.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi forged an inscription on a Luo River stone prophesying imperial rule and had Tang Tongtai of Yong present it. Wu named it the "Treasure Chart" and made Tongtai Mobile Strike General.

sentences.zh: 於是汜人又上瑞石，太后乃郊上帝謝況，自號聖母神皇，作神皇璽，改寶圖曰「天授聖圖」，號洛水曰永昌水，圖所曰聖圖泉，勒石洛壇左曰「天授聖圖之表」，改汜水曰廣武。

translations.literal: Thereupon a man of Si again presented an auspicious stone; the dowager then sacrificed to God on the outskirts and thanked Heaven's favor, styled herself Holy Mother Divine Sovereign, made a Divine Sovereign seal, changed Treasure Chart to "Heaven-Bestowed Holy Chart," named the Luo River Ever-Flourishing Water, the site of the chart Holy Chart Spring, engraved stone left of the Luo altar "Table of the Heaven-Bestowed Holy Chart," and changed Si River to Broad Martial.
translations.idiomatic: Then a man of Si offered another auspicious stone. She sacrificed to Heaven on the outskirts, thanked divine favor, styled herself Holy Mother and Divine Sovereign, created a divine seal, renamed the chart "Heaven-Bestowed Holy Chart," the Luo "Ever-Flourishing Water," its site "Holy Chart Spring," and engraved "Table of the Heaven-Bestowed Holy Chart" beside the Luo altar, while Si River became Broad Martial.

sentences.zh: 時柄去王室，大臣重將皆撓不得逞，宗室孤外無寄足地。

translations.literal: At this time power had left the imperial house; great ministers and heavy generals were thwarted and could not act; the imperial clan, isolated outside, had no footing.
translations.idiomatic: Power had passed from the Li house. Great ministers and leading generals were paralyzed, and the imperial clan, cut off outside court, had nowhere to stand.

sentences.zh: 於是，韓王元嘉等謀舉兵唱天下，迎還中宗。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince of Han Yuang Jia and others plotted to raise troops and proclaim across the realm to welcome back Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Han Yuang Jia and others then plotted to raise armies and rally the realm to restore Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 瑯邪王沖、越王貞先發，諸王倉卒無應者，遂敗。

translations.literal: Prince of Langye Chong and Prince of Yue Zhen moved first; the princes in haste had no responders, and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Langye Chong and Prince of Yue Zhen rose first, but the other princes could not rally in time and the revolt collapsed.

sentences.zh: 元嘉與魯王靈夔等皆自殺，餘悉坐誅，諸王牽連死滅殆盡，子孫雖嬰褓亦投嶺南。

translations.literal: Yuang Jia and Prince of Lu Lingqi and others all killed themselves; the rest were all executed by association; the princes, implicated, were almost entirely extinguished; descendants even in swaddling clothes were cast into Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuang Jia, Prince of Lu Lingqi, and others took their own lives; the rest were executed. The princely line was nearly annihilated, and even infants were exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 太后身拜洛受圖，天子率太子、群臣、蠻夷以次列，大陳珍禽、奇獸、貢物、鹵簿壇下，禮成去。

translations.literal: The dowager in person bowed at the Luo to receive the chart; the Son of Heaven led the crown prince, ministers, and barbarians in successive array; rare birds, strange beasts, tribute goods, and guards of honor were arrayed below the altar; when rites were complete they departed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress herself bowed at the Luo to receive the chart while the emperor led crown prince, ministers, and foreign chiefs in order below. Rare birds, exotic beasts, tribute, and imperial guards filled the altar precinct until the rites ended.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年，享萬象神宮，改服袞冕，裯大圭，執鎮圭，睿宗亞獻，太子終獻。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang, she sacrificed at the Hall of Myriad Images Spirit Palace, changed to robe and cap, wore the great jade tablet, held the quelling jade, Ruizong as secondary offerer, crown prince as final offerer.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchang she sacrificed at the Hall of Myriad Images, donned imperial robes and cap, bore the great jade tablet and held the quelling jade, with Ruizong as secondary offerer and the crown prince as final offerer.

sentences.zh: 合祭天地，五方帝、百神從，以高祖、太宗、高宗配，引魏王士彠從配。

translations.literal: Combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, with Five-Direction Emperors and hundred spirits attending, matching Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong, and drawing in Prince of Wei Shi Yue as secondary match.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth were sacrificed to together, with the Five-Direction Emperors and myriad spirits in attendance, Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong as chief matches, and Prince of Wei Shi Yue added as secondary match.

sentences.zh: 班九條，訓百官。

translations.literal: She promulgated nine articles to instruct the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: She issued nine injunctions to instruct the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 遂大饗群臣。

translations.literal: Then she feasted the ministers grandly.
translations.idiomatic: Then she held a great feast for the court.

sentences.zh: 號士彠周忠孝太皇，楊忠孝太后。

translations.literal: She titled Shi Yue Zhou Loyal and Filial Grand August, and Yang Loyal and Filial Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: She styled Shi Yue Grand August Loyal and Filial of Zhou and Yang Empress Dowager Loyal and Filial.

sentences.zh: 以文水墓為章德陵，咸陽墓為明義陵。

translations.literal: The tomb at Wenshui was made Zhangde Mausoleum, the tomb at Xianyang Mingyi Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: The tomb at Wenshui became Zhangde Mausoleum and the tomb at Xianyang Mingyi Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 太原安成王為周安成王，金城郡王為魏義康王，北平郡王為趙肅恭王，魯國公為太原靖王。

translations.literal: Prince of Taiyuan Secure and Accomplished was made Zhou Prince Secure and Accomplished, Prince of Jincheng Zhou Prince Righteous and Tranquil, Prince of Beiping Zhao Prince Respectful and Solemn, Duke of Lu Taiyuan Prince Serene.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Taiyuan Secure and Accomplished became Zhou Prince Secure and Accomplished; the Prince of Jincheng became Wei Prince Righteous and Tranquil; the Prince of Beiping became Zhao Prince Respectful and Solemn; and the Duke of Lu became Taiyuan Prince Serene.

sentences.zh: 載初中，又享萬象神宮，以太穆、文德二皇后配皇地祗，引周忠孝太后從配。

translations.literal: In the early Zaiwu years, again sacrificing at Myriad Images Spirit Palace, with Great Serenity and Cultured Virtue empresses matching Earth Queen, drawing Zhou Loyal and Filial Empress Dowager as secondary match.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zaiwu era she again sacrificed at the Hall of Myriad Images, matching Empresses Great Serenity and Cultured Virtue to Earth Queen and adding the Zhou Loyal and Filial Empress Dowager as secondary match.

sentences.zh: 作曌、𠀑、埊、𡆠、囝、〇、𠺞、𢘑、𡕀、𡔈、𠡦、𠙺十有二文。

translations.literal: She created twelve characters: Zhao, and eleven other invented graphs.
translations.idiomatic: She devised twelve new characters, including Zhao and eleven other invented forms.

sentences.zh: 太后自名曌。

translations.literal: The dowager took the name Zhao for herself.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager adopted Zhao as her personal name.

sentences.zh: 改詔書為制書。

translations.literal: Changed edict documents to decree documents.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts were renamed decrees.

sentences.zh: 以周、漢為二王後，虞、夏、殷後為三恪，除唐屬籍。

translations.literal: Zhou and Han were made the two Kings Later, successors of Yu, Xia, and Yin the Three Respectful Withdrawals, and Tang was removed from the genealogical registers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Han were named the two successor dynasties, Yu, Xia, and Yin the three withdrawn lines of respect, and the Tang house was struck from the registers.

sentences.zh: 拜薛懷義輔國大將軍，封鄂國公，令與群浮屠作《大雲經》，言神皇受命事。

translations.literal: Xue Huaiyi was invested Assistant State Grand General, enfeoffed Duke of E, and ordered with the monks to compose the Great Cloud Sutra, speaking of the Divine Sovereign receiving the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Huaiyi was made assistant state grand general and Duke of E and ordered, with other monks, to compose the Great Cloud Sutra proclaiming the divine sovereign's mandate.

sentences.zh: 春官尚書李思文詭言：「《周書·武成》為篇，辭有『垂拱天下治』，為受命之符。」

translations.literal: Minister of Spring Office Li Siwen speciously said: "The Zhou Book chapter 'Martial Completion' has the words 'drooping arch, all under Heaven governed'—the sign of receiving the mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Li Siwen argued deceitfully, "The Zhou Documents chapter 'Completion of the Martial' contains the phrase 'drooping arch, all under Heaven governed'—a token of the received mandate."

sentences.zh: 后喜，皆班示天下，稍圖革命。

translations.literal: The empress was pleased; all were circulated to show the realm; gradually she plotted dynastic change.
translations.idiomatic: She rejoiced, had the texts posted throughout the realm, and began plotting the dynastic change in earnest.

sentences.zh: 然畏人心不肯附，乃陰忍鷙害，肆斬殺怖天下。

translations.literal: Yet fearing hearts would not attach, she was secretly forbearing yet fierce in harm, wantonly beheading and killing to terrify the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fearing the people would not follow, she hid her cruelty while unleashing executions to terrify the realm.

sentences.zh: 內縱酷吏周興、來俊臣等數十人為爪吻，有不慊若素疑憚者，必危法中之。

translations.literal: Within she unleashed cruel officials Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and dozens as fangs and talons; any who displeased her or whom she had long suspected and feared were certainly struck down by perilous law.
translations.idiomatic: She set loose dozens of cruel officials such as Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen as her claws; anyone who displeased her or whom she had long mistrusted was trapped by deadly law.

sentences.zh: 宗姓侯王及它骨鯁臣將相駢頸就鈇，血丹狴戶，家不能自保。

translations.literal: Clansmen, marquises, princes, and other stubborn ministers, generals, and chancellors went neck to neck to the axe; blood reddened the prison gates; families could not preserve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kin, marquises, princes, and stubborn ministers and generals went to the block in ranks; blood stained the prison gates, and no household could protect itself.

sentences.zh: 太后操奩具坐重幃，而國命移矣。

translations.literal: The dowager applied her toilet implements and sat behind heavy curtains, yet the nation's mandate had shifted.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager painted her face and sat behind heavy curtains while the fate of the realm changed hands.

sentences.zh: 御史傅遊藝率關內父老請革命，改帝氏為武。

translations.literal: Censor Fu Youyi led elders within the passes to petition for revolution, changing the imperial surname to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Fu Youyi led elders of the Guanzhong region to petition for revolution and a change of the imperial surname to Wu.

sentences.zh: 又脅群臣固請，妄言鳳集上陽宮，赤雀見朝堂。

translations.literal: Again she coerced the ministers to press firmly, falsely claiming phoenixes gathered at Shangyang Palace and red sparrows appeared in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: She again coerced the ministers to press the demand, fabricating reports that phoenixes had gathered at Shangyang Palace and red sparrows appeared in the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 天子不自安，亦請氏武，示一尊。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was uneasy himself and also petitioned the surname Wu to show single reverence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, ill at ease himself, also petitioned for the Wu surname to signal a single center of authority.

sentences.zh: 太后知威柄在己，因大赦天下，改國號周，自稱聖神皇帝，旗幟尚赤，以皇帝為皇嗣。

translations.literal: The dowager knew authority was in her hands, and with a great amnesty changed the state name to Zhou, styled herself Holy Spirit Emperor, banners honored red, and made the emperor imperial heir.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing power rested with her, she proclaimed a great amnesty, changed the dynastic name to Zhou, styled herself Holy Spirit Emperor, favored red banners, and made the emperor her imperial heir.

sentences.zh: 立武氏七廟於神都。

translations.literal: Established seven Wu clan temples in the Divine Capital.
translations.idiomatic: She established seven Wu ancestral temples in the divine capital.

sentences.zh: 尊周文王為文皇帝，號始祖，妣姒曰文定皇后；

translations.literal: Honored King Wen of Zhou as Cultured Emperor, titled Founding Ancestor, mother Si as Cultured and Settled Empress;
translations.idiomatic: King Wen of Zhou was honored as Cultured Emperor and Founding Ancestor, with Lady Si as Cultured and Settled Empress;

sentences.zh: 武王為康皇帝，號睿祖，妣姜曰康惠皇后；

translations.literal: King Wu as Tranquil Emperor, titled Sagacious Ancestor, mother Jiang as Tranquil and Gracious Empress;
translations.idiomatic: King Wu as Tranquil Emperor and Sagacious Ancestor, with Lady Jiang as Tranquil and Gracious Empress;

sentences.zh: 太原靖王為成皇帝，號嚴祖，妣曰成莊皇后；

translations.literal: Taiyuan Prince Serene as Accomplished Emperor, titled Stern Ancestor, mother as Accomplished and Solemn Empress;
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan Prince Serene as Accomplished Emperor and Stern Ancestor, with his consort as Accomplished and Solemn Empress;

sentences.zh: 趙肅恭王為章敬皇帝，號肅祖，妣曰章敬皇后；

translations.literal: Zhao Prince Respectful and Solemn as Manifest and Reverent Emperor, titled Solemn Ancestor, mother as Manifest and Reverent Empress;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Prince Respectful and Solemn as Manifest and Reverent Emperor and Solemn Ancestor, with his consort as Manifest and Reverent Empress;

sentences.zh: 魏義康王為昭安皇帝，號烈祖，妣曰昭安皇后；

translations.literal: Wei Prince Righteous and Tranquil as Manifest and Secure Emperor, titled Fierce Ancestor, mother as Manifest and Secure Empress;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Prince Righteous and Tranquil as Manifest and Secure Emperor and Fierce Ancestor, with his consort as Manifest and Secure Empress;

sentences.zh: 祖周安成王為文穆皇帝，號顯祖，妣曰文穆皇后；

translations.literal: Grandfather Zhou Prince Secure and Accomplished as Cultured and Solemn Emperor, titled Illustrious Ancestor, mother as Cultured and Solemn Empress;
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Zhou Prince Secure and Accomplished as Cultured and Solemn Emperor and Illustrious Ancestor, with his consort as Cultured and Solemn Empress;

sentences.zh: 考忠孝太皇為孝明高皇帝，號太祖，妣曰孝明高皇后。

translations.literal: Father Loyal and Filial Grand August as Filial and Illustrious High Emperor, titled Grand Ancestor, mother as Filial and Illustrious High Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Her father, the Loyal and Filial Grand August, as Filial and Illustrious High Emperor and Grand Ancestor, with her mother as Filial and Illustrious High Empress.

sentences.zh: 罷唐廟為享德廟，四時祠高祖以下三室，餘廢不享。

translations.literal: Abolished Tang temples as Enjoying Virtue Temple, four seasons sacrificing to three chambers below Gaozu, the rest abolished from sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Tang ancestral temples were reduced to the Enjoying Virtue Temple, with seasonal sacrifice limited to three chambers from Gaozu downward; the rest ceased to receive offerings.

sentences.zh: 至日，祀上帝萬象神宮，以始祖及考妣配，以百神從祀。

translations.literal: On the solstice, sacrificed to God at Myriad Images Spirit Palace, with founding ancestor and father and mother matched, hundred spirits attendant sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On the solstice she sacrificed to Heaven at the Hall of Myriad Images, with the founding ancestor and her parents as chief matches and the myriad spirits in attendance.

sentences.zh: 盡王諸武。

translations.literal: Made all Wu kin princes.
translations.idiomatic: Every member of the Wu clan was ennobled as prince.

sentences.zh: 詔并州文水縣為武興，比漢豐、沛，百姓世給復。

translations.literal: Decreed Bingzhou Wenshui county as Wuxing, comparable to Han Feng and Pei, common people granted tax exemption generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: She decreed Wenshui county in Bingzhou renamed Wuxing, ranked with Han Feng and Pei, its people exempt from taxes in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 以始祖冢為德陵，睿祖為喬陵，嚴祖為節陵，肅祖為簡陵，烈祖為靖陵，顯祖為永陵，章德陵為昊陵，明義陵為順陵。

translations.literal: The founding ancestor's tomb was made Virtue Mausoleum, Sagacious Ancestor Qiao Mausoleum, Stern Ancestor Festival Mausoleum, Solemn Ancestor Simple Mausoleum, Fierce Ancestor Serene Mausoleum, Illustrious Ancestor Everlasting Mausoleum, Zhangde Mausoleum became Vast Mausoleum, Mingyi Mausoleum became Compliance Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: The founding ancestor's tomb became Virtue Mausoleum; the Sagacious Ancestor's, Lofty Mausoleum; the Stern Ancestor's, Festival Mausoleum; the Solemn Ancestor's, Simple Mausoleum; the Fierce Ancestor's, Serene Mausoleum; the Illustrious Ancestor's, Everlasting Mausoleum; Zhangde Mausoleum became Vast Mausoleum; and Mingyi Mausoleum became Compliance Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 太皇雖春秋高，善自塗澤，雖左右不悟其衰。

translations.literal: Though the Grand August's years were high, she was skilled at applying cosmetics; even those beside her did not perceive her decline.
translations.idiomatic: Though advanced in years, the Grand August was expert at cosmetics; even those at her side did not notice her frailty.

sentences.zh: 俄而二齒生，下詔改元為長壽。

translations.literal: Soon two teeth grew; an edict changed the era name to Longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Soon two new teeth appeared, and she changed the era name to Longevity.

sentences.zh: 明年，享神宮，自製大樂，舞工用九百人，以武承嗣為亞獻，三思為終獻。

translations.literal: Next year, sacrificing at Spirit Palace, self-composed great music, nine hundred dancers, Wu Chengsi as secondary offerer, Sansi as final offerer.
translations.idiomatic: The following year she sacrificed at the spirit palace with music of her own composition and nine hundred dancers, Wu Chengsi as secondary offerer and Wu Sansi as final offerer.

sentences.zh: 帝之為皇嗣，公卿往往見之，會尚方監裴匪躬、左衛大將軍阿史那元慶、白澗府果毅薛大信、監門衛大將軍范雲仙潛謁帝，皆腰斬都市，自是公卿不復上謁。

translations.literal: When the emperor was imperial heir, ministers and dukes often saw him; then Director of the Palace Workshops Pei Feigong, Left Guard Grand General Ashina Yuanqing, Baigou Commandery Militia Leader Xue Daxin, and Gate Guard Grand General Fan Yunxian secretly visited the emperor—all were cut at the waist in the market; from this time ministers and dukes no longer paid court.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial heir the emperor was still visited by senior officials until Pei Feigong of the Palace Workshops, Ashina Yuanqing of the Left Guard, Xue Daxin of Baigou commandery, and Fan Yunxian of the Gate Guard secretly called on him. All were executed by waist-cutting in the marketplace, and thereafter no minister dared visit him.

sentences.zh: 有上封事言嶺南流人謀反者，太后遣攝右臺監察御史萬國俊就按，得實即論決。

translations.literal: Someone submitted a sealed memorial saying exiles in Lingnan plotted rebellion; the dowager sent Acting Right Platform Investigating Censor Wan Guojun to investigate on the spot, and if true to decide punishment at once.
translations.idiomatic: A sealed memorial claimed exiles in Lingnan were plotting rebellion. The empress sent Acting Right Platform censor Wan Guojun to investigate and execute the guilty on the spot.

sentences.zh: 國俊至廣州，盡召流人，矯詔賜自盡，皆號哭不服，國俊驅之水曲，使不得逃，一日戮三百餘人。

translations.literal: Guojun reached Guangzhou, summoned all exiles, forged an edict granting suicide; all wailed and refused; Guojun drove them to the river bend so they could not escape, and in one day slaughtered more than three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangzhou Guojun summoned every exile and, by forged edict, ordered them to take their own lives. When they wept and refused, he drove them to a river bend where none could flee and killed more than three hundred in a single day.

sentences.zh: 乃誣奏流人怨望，請悉除之。

translations.literal: Then he falsely memorialized that the exiles harbored resentment and requested that all be eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: He then falsely reported that the exiles nursed resentment and asked that they all be eliminated.

sentences.zh: 於是太后遣右衛翊府兵曹參軍劉光業、司刑評事王德壽、苑南面監丞鮑思恭、尚輦直長王大貞、右武衛兵曹參軍屈貞筠，皆攝監察御史，分往劍南、黔中、安南等六道訊鞫，而擢國俊左臺侍御史。

translations.literal: Thereupon the dowager sent Right Guard Yifu Army Staff Officer Liu Guangye, Judicial Reviewer Wang Deshou, Southern Park Supervisor Bao Sigong, Imperial Carriage Chief Attendant Wang Dazhen, and Right Martial Guard Army Staff Officer Qu Zhenyun—all acting investigating censors—divided among six circuits of Jiannan, Qianzhong, Annan, and others to interrogate, while promoting Guojun to Left Platform Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: She then dispatched Liu Guangye, Wang Deshou, Bao Sigong, Wang Dazhen, and Qu Zhenyun, each acting as investigating censor, to six circuits including Jiannan, Qianzhong, and Annan to conduct inquiries, while promoting Guojun to attending censor of the Left Platform.

sentences.zh: 光業等亦希功於上，惟恐殺人之少。

translations.literal: Guangye and the others also sought merit before the throne, fearing only that they had killed too few.
translations.idiomatic: Guangye and his fellows likewise courted favor above and feared only that their body counts were too low.

sentences.zh: 光業殺者九百人，德壽殺七百人，其餘亦不減五百人。

translations.literal: Guangye killed nine hundred; Deshou seven hundred; the rest no fewer than five hundred each.
translations.idiomatic: Guangye killed nine hundred, Deshou seven hundred, and the others no fewer than five hundred apiece.

sentences.zh: 太后久乃知其冤，詔六道使所殺者還其家。

translations.literal: Only after a long time did the dowager learn of their injustice; an edict ordered the victims killed by the six-circuit envoys restored to their families.
translations.idiomatic: Only later did she learn of the injustice and decree that the victims of the six envoys be returned to their families.

sentences.zh: 國俊等亦相踵而死，皆見有物為厲云。

translations.literal: Guojun and the others also died one after another; all were said to have seen things as vengeful spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Guojun and the others likewise died in succession, each claiming to see vengeful spirits.

sentences.zh: 太后又自加號金輪聖神皇帝，置七寶於廷：曰金輪寶，曰白象寶，曰女寶，曰馬寶，曰珠寶，曰主兵臣寶，曰主藏臣寶，率大朝會則陳之。

translations.literal: The dowager again added to herself the title Golden Wheel Holy Spirit Emperor, set seven treasures in the court: called Golden Wheel Treasure, White Elephant Treasure, Woman Treasure, Horse Treasure, Pearl Treasure, Minister-of-Arms Treasure, Minister-of-Treasury Treasure—at every great court assembly they were displayed.
translations.idiomatic: She further styled herself Golden Wheel Holy Spirit Emperor and placed seven treasures in court—the golden wheel, white elephant, woman, horse, pearl, minister of arms, and minister of treasury—which were displayed at every great assembly.

sentences.zh: 又尊其顯祖為立極文穆皇帝，太祖為無上孝明皇帝。

translations.literal: Further she honored her Illustrious Ancestor as Establishing the Pole Cultured and Solemn Emperor, Grand Ancestor as Supreme Filial and Illustrious Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: She further elevated her Illustrious Ancestor to Establishing-the-Pole Cultured and Solemn Emperor and her Grand Ancestor to Supreme Filial and Illustrious Emperor.

sentences.zh: 延載二年，武三思率蕃夷諸酋及耆老請作天樞，紀太后功德，以黜唐興周，制可。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanzai, Wu Sansi led tribal chiefs of the barbarians and elders to request construction of the Heaven Pivot, recording the dowager's merit and virtue, to displace Tang and exalt Zhou—the decree approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yanzai, Wu Sansi led foreign chiefs and elders to petition for a Heaven Pivot commemorating her merit, supplanting Tang and exalting Zhou. The decree approved.

sentences.zh: 使納言姚璹護作。

translations.literal: She sent Palace Secretariat Director Yao Shuang to oversee construction.
translations.idiomatic: She appointed Secretariat Director Yao Shuang commissioner of the work.

sentences.zh: 乃大裒銅鐵合冶之，署曰「大周萬國頌德天樞」，置端門外。

translations.literal: Then great quantities of copper and iron were gathered and smelted together; it was titled "Great Zhou Ten Thousand States Praising Virtue Heaven Pivot," placed outside Duan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Vast stores of copper and iron were gathered and cast into the "Great Zhou Ten Thousand States Praise-of-Virtue Heaven Pivot," erected outside Duan Gate.

sentences.zh: 其制若柱，度高一百五尺，八面，面別五尺，冶鐵象山為之趾，負以銅龍，石鑱怪獸環之。

translations.literal: Its form was like a pillar, height one hundred fifty feet, eight faces, each face five feet apart; smelted iron shaped like a mountain formed its base, borne on copper dragons, stone-carved strange beasts encircling it.
translations.idiomatic: Shaped like a pillar one hundred fifty feet high with eight faces five feet wide each, it stood on an iron mountain-base borne by copper dragons, ringed with carved stone monsters.

sentences.zh: 柱顛為雲蓋，出大珠，高丈，圍三之。

translations.literal: The pillar's summit was a cloud canopy issuing a great pearl, one zhang high, circumference thrice that.
translations.idiomatic: Its summit bore a cloud canopy and a great pearl one zhang high, three zhang in girth.

sentences.zh: 作四蛟，度丈二尺，以承珠。

translations.literal: Four flood-dragons were made, one zhang two feet long, to bear the pearl.
translations.idiomatic: Four flood-dragons twelve feet long supported the pearl.

sentences.zh: 其趾山周百七十尺，度二丈。

translations.literal: Its mountain-base circumference was one hundred seventy feet, height two zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain-base measured one hundred seventy feet around and two zhang high.

sentences.zh: 無慮用銅鐵二百萬斤。

translations.literal: No less than two million jin of copper and iron were used.
translations.idiomatic: It consumed no less than two million jin of copper and iron.

sentences.zh: 乃悉鏤群臣、蕃酋名氏其上。

translations.literal: Then all ministers' and tribal chiefs' names were carved upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Every minister and foreign chief was inscribed upon it.

sentences.zh: 薛懷義寵稍衰，而御醫沈南璆進，懷義大望，因火明堂，太后羞之，掩不發。

translations.literal: Xue Huaiyi's favor gradually waned, while attending physician Shen Nanqiong advanced; Huaiyi greatly despaired, and set fire to the Bright Hall; the dowager was shamed and concealed it without announcement.
translations.idiomatic: As Xue Huaiyi's favor faded and court physician Shen Nanqiong rose, Huaiyi, bitterly disappointed, burned the Bright Hall. The empress, ashamed, suppressed the news.

sentences.zh: 懷義愈很恣怏怏。

translations.literal: Huaiyi grew ever more fierce and willful, sullen and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi grew ever more violent and sullen.

sentences.zh: 乃密詔太平公主擇健婦縛之殿中，命建昌王武攸寧、將作大匠宗晉卿率壯士擊殺之，以畚車載屍還白馬寺。

translations.literal: Then a secret edict ordered Princess Taiping to choose strong women to bind him in the hall, commanded Prince of Jianchang Wu Youning and Director of Palace Construction Zong Jinqing to lead stalwarts to beat him to death, and carried his corpse back to White Horse Temple in a dustpan cart.
translations.idiomatic: By secret edict Princess Taiping chose strong women to bind him in the hall while Prince of Jianchang Wu Youning and Director of Works Zong Jinqing led brawny men to beat him to death; his body was hauled back to White Horse Temple in a dustpan cart.

sentences.zh: 懷義負幸昵，氣蓋一時，出百官上，其徒多犯法。

translations.literal: Huaiyi relied on favor and intimacy; his air dominated an age, standing above the hundred officials; his followers often broke the law.
translations.idiomatic: Favored and intimate, Huaiyi's arrogance eclipsed his age; he ranked above the bureaucracy, and his followers routinely broke the law.

sentences.zh: 御史馮思勖劾其姦，懷義怒，遇諸道，命左右歐之，幾死，弗敢言。

translations.literal: Censor Feng Sixu impeached his debauchery; Huaiyi in anger, meeting him on the road, ordered attendants to beat him; he nearly died and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Feng Sixu impeached his debauchery, Huaiyi had his men beat Feng nearly to death in the street, and Feng dared not speak of it.

sentences.zh: 默啜犯塞，拜新平、伐逆、朔方道大總管，提十八將軍兵擊胡，宰相李昭德、蘇味道至為之長史、司馬。

translations.literal: When Mohechuo raided the frontier, Huaiyi was appointed Grand Commander of Xinping, Punish-Rebellion, and Shuofang circuits, leading eighteen generals' troops to strike the barbarians; chancellors Li Zhaode and Su Weidao even served as his chief administrator and aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Mohechuo raided the frontier she made him grand commander of the Xinping, Punish-Rebellion, and Shuofang circuits with eighteen generals under him; chancellors Li Zhaode and Su Weidao even served as his chief administrator and aide-de-camp.

sentences.zh: 後猒入禁中，陰募力少年千人為浮屠，有逆謀。

translations.literal: Later, weary of entering the inner palace, he secretly recruited a thousand strong youths as monks, with a treasonous plot.
translations.idiomatic: Later, loathing the inner palace, he secretly recruited a thousand strong young men as monks and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 侍御史周矩劾狀請治驗，太后曰：「第出，朕將使詣獄。」

translations.literal: Attendant censor Zhou Ju submitted an impeachment memorial requesting investigation and verification. The empress dowager said: "Just go out—I will have him sent to prison."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhou Ju filed an impeachment demanding a formal inquiry. The empress dowager said, "Leave now—I will have him brought to prison.

sentences.zh: 矩坐臺，少選，懷義怒馬造廷，直往坐大榻上，矩召吏受辭，懷義即乘馬去。

translations.literal: Ju sat at the censorate. After a short while Huaiyi, on a furious horse, came to the court, went straight to sit on the great couch. Ju summoned clerks to take testimony; Huaiyi immediately mounted his horse and left.
translations.idiomatic: Ju took his seat at the censorate. Shortly afterward Huaiyi rode in angrily, entered the hall, and seated himself on the great couch. Ju called clerks to take his confession, but Huaiyi mounted his horse and rode off at once.

sentences.zh: 矩以聞，太后曰：「是道人素狂，不足治，力少年聽窮劾。」

translations.literal: Ju reported it. The empress dowager said: "This Taoist has always been wild—not worth prosecuting. Young Li, hear his exhaustive impeachment."
translations.idiomatic: Ju reported the incident. The empress dowager said, "That monk has always been reckless—he is not worth prosecuting. Young Li, hear out his full indictment.

sentences.zh: 矩悉投放醜裔。

translations.literal: Ju cast them all into exile among remote frontier peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Ju had every accused party banished to distant border regions.

sentences.zh: 懷義構矩，俄免官。

translations.literal: Huaiyi framed Ju; soon Ju was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi engineered charges against Ju, and within little time Ju was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 太后祀天南郊，以文王、武王、士彠與唐高祖並配。

translations.literal: The empress dowager sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburb, matching King Wen, King Wu, and Shi Le with Tang Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager offered sacrifice to Heaven at the southern suburb, with King Wen, King Wu, Shi Le, and Tang Gaozu as joint spirit-matches.

sentences.zh: 太后加號天冊金輪聖神皇帝。

translations.literal: The empress dowager added the title Heaven-Proclaiming Golden-Wheel Holy Spirit Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: She added the title Heaven-Proclaiming Golden-Wheel Holy Spirit Emperor.

sentences.zh: 遂封嵩山，禪少室，冊山之神為帝，配為后。

translations.literal: Then she performed feng on Mount Song and chan at Lesser Chamber, enfeoffing the mountain spirit as emperor with a consort as empress.
translations.idiomatic: She then performed the feng rite on Mount Song and the chan rite at Lesser Chamber, enfeoffing the mountain spirit as emperor and pairing a spirit-consort as empress.

sentences.zh: 封壇南有大槲，赦日置雞其杪，賜號「金雞樹」。

translations.literal: South of the feng altar stood a great oak. On amnesty day a cock was placed atop it, and it was granted the name "Golden Cock Tree."
translations.idiomatic: South of the feng altar stood a great oak. On the day of the amnesty a rooster was set atop it, and the tree was given the name Golden Cock Tree.

sentences.zh: 自制《升中述志》，刻石示後。

translations.literal: She herself composed "Ascent to the Middle: Statement of Intent," carving it in stone for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: She herself composed Ascent to the Middle: Statement of Intent and had it carved in stone for posterity.

sentences.zh: 改明堂為通天宮，鑄九州鼎，各位其方，列廷中。

translations.literal: She changed Bright Hall to Palace Reaching Heaven, cast the nine regional cauldrons, placed each in its direction, and arrayed them in the court.
translations.idiomatic: She renamed Bright Hall as Palace Reaching Heaven, cast the Nine Cauldrons of the regions, set each in its proper direction, and lined them up in the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 又斂天下黃金作大儀鐘，不克。

translations.literal: Again she levied gold from the realm to make a great ceremonial bell—she could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: She again levied gold from across the realm to cast a great ceremonial bell, but the project failed.

sentences.zh: 久之，以崇先廟為崇尊廟，禮視太廟，旋復崇尊廟為太廟。

translations.literal: After a long time she made Venerating Ancestors Temple into Venerating and Honored Temple with rites equal to the Grand Temple; soon she restored Venerating and Honored Temple to the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: After some time she made the Venerating Ancestors Temple into the Venerating and Honored Temple with rites equal to the Grand Temple, then soon restored the Venerating and Honored Temple to the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 自懷義死，張易之、昌宗得幸，乃置控鶴府，有監，有丞及主簿、錄事等，監三品，以易之為之。

translations.literal: Since Huaiyi's death, Zhang Yizhi and Changzong gained favor. She then established the Crane-Controlling Office, with a director, vice-director, chief clerk, recorder, and the like; the director was third rank, and Yizhi held the post.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaiyi died, Zhang Yizhi and Changzong won her favor. She established the Crane-Controlling Office with a director, vice-director, chief clerk, recorder, and other posts; the director was third rank, and Yizhi was appointed to it.

sentences.zh: 太后自見諸武王非天下意，前此中宗自房州還，復為皇太子，恐百歲後為唐宗室躪藉無死所，即引諸武及相王、太平公主誓明堂，告天地，為鐵券使藏史館。

translations.literal: The empress dowager herself saw that making the Wu princes rulers was not the will of the realm. Earlier Zhongzong had returned from Fang Prefecture and been restored as crown prince. Fearing that after her hundred years the Tang imperial clan would be trampled with nowhere to die, she summoned the Wu kin together with the Prince of Xiang and Princess Taiping to swear an oath in Bright Hall, announce it to Heaven and Earth, and had iron contracts made for storage in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager knew enthroning the Wu princes did not match the people's will. Earlier Zhongzong had returned from Fang Prefecture and been restored as crown prince. Fearing that after her death the Tang imperial house would be crushed with no refuge, she summoned the Wu clan together with the Prince of Xiang and Princess Taiping to swear an oath in Bright Hall before Heaven and Earth, and had iron contracts drawn up for deposit in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 改昊陵署為攀龍臺。

translations.literal: She changed the Vast Mausoleum Office to Dragon-Scaling Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: The Vast Mausoleum Office was renamed Dragon-Scaling Terrace.

sentences.zh: 久視初，以控鶴監為天驥府，又改奉宸府，罷監為令，以左右控鶴為奉宸大夫，易之復為令。

translations.literal: At the start of the Long Vision era she made the Crane-Controlling Directorate into the Heaven's Steed Office, then changed it again to the Serving-the-Inner Office, abolished the directorate for a commandant, made the left and right Crane-Controllers Serving-the-Inner Grand Masters, and Yizhi again became commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Long Vision era the Crane-Controlling Directorate became the Heaven's Steed Office, then was changed again to the Serving-the-Inner Office; the directorate was abolished for a commandant, the left and right Crane-Controllers became Serving-the-Inner Grand Masters, and Yizhi again held the commandancy.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，太后有疾，久不平，居迎仙院。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Divine Dragon era the empress dowager fell ill and for a long time did not recover, residing in Welcome-the-Immortals Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Divine Dragon the empress dowager fell ill and for a long time did not recover, living in Welcome-the-Immortals Court.

sentences.zh: 宰相張柬之與崔玄暐等建策，請中宗以兵入誅易之、昌宗，於是羽林將軍李多祚等帥兵自玄武門入，斬二張於院左。

translations.literal: Chancellor Zhang Jianzhi and Cui Xuanwei and others devised a plan, asking Zhongzong to enter with troops to execute Yizhi and Changzong. Thereupon Imperial Guard general Li Duozuo and others led troops in through the Xuanwu Gate and beheaded the two Zhangs to the left of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhang Jianzhi, Cui Xuanwei, and others devised a plan and asked Zhongzong to enter with troops to kill Yizhi and Changzong. Imperial Guard general Li Duozuo and others then led soldiers in through the Xuanwu Gate and beheaded the two Zhangs beside the court.

sentences.zh: 太后聞變而起，桓彥範進請傳位，太后返臥，不復語。

translations.literal: The empress dowager heard of the uprising and rose. Huan Yanfan advanced to request the transfer of the throne; the empress dowager returned to lie down and spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager heard of the coup she rose. Huan Yanfan stepped forward to request abdication; she lay down again and said nothing more.

sentences.zh: 中宗於是復即位。

translations.literal: Zhongzong thereupon resumed the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong thereupon resumed the throne.

sentences.zh: 徙太后上陽宮，帝率百官詣觀風殿問起居，後率十日一詣宮，俄朝朔、望。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was moved to Shangyang Palace. The emperor led the hundred officials to Wind-Viewing Hall to inquire after her health; afterward he went once every ten days, and soon attended on the first and fifteenth of the month.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was moved to Shangyang Palace. The emperor led the hundred officials to Wind-Viewing Hall to inquire after her health; afterward he visited once every ten days, and soon came on the new and full moon.

sentences.zh: 廢奉宸府官，選東都武氏廟於崇尊廟，更號崇恩，復唐宗廟。

translations.literal: Serving-the-Inner offices were abolished; the Eastern Capital Wu clan temple was chosen over the Venerating and Honored Temple, renamed Venerating Grace, and Tang ancestral temples were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Serving-the-Inner offices were abolished; the Eastern Capital Wu clan temple was preferred to the Venerating and Honored Temple, renamed Venerating Grace, and the Tang ancestral temples were restored.

sentences.zh: 諸武王者咸降爵。

translations.literal: All Wu princes had their noble ranks reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Every Wu prince had his rank lowered.

sentences.zh: 是歲，后崩，年八十一。

translations.literal: That year the empress dowager died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: That year the empress dowager died, aged eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 遺制稱則天大聖皇太后，去帝號。

translations.literal: Her final instructions styled her Zetian Great Sage Empress Dowager and removed the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: Her testament styled her Zetian Great Sage Empress Dowager and stripped the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 謚曰則天大聖后，祔乾陵。

translations.literal: Her posthumous title was Zetian Great Sage Empress; she was enshrined at Qian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She was given the posthumous title Zetian Great Sage Empress and enshrined at Qian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 會武三思蒸韋庶人，復用事。

translations.literal: When Wu Sansi entered an illicit liaison with Consort Wei, he again held power.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sansi took up an illicit affair with Consort Wei, he again held power.

sentences.zh: 於是大旱，祈陵輒雨。

translations.literal: Thereupon a great drought struck; prayers at the mausoleum promptly brought rain.
translations.idiomatic: A great drought followed; prayers at the mausoleum promptly brought rain.

sentences.zh: 三思訹帝詔崇恩廟祠如太廟，齋郎用五品子。

translations.literal: Sansi induced the emperor to decree that Venerating Grace Temple be sacrificed to like the Grand Temple, with ritual officers drawn from sons of fifth-rank officials.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi induced the emperor to decree sacrifice at Venerating Grace Temple on the model of the Grand Temple, with ritual officers taken from sons of fifth-rank officials.

sentences.zh: 博士楊孚言：「太廟諸郎取七品子，今崇恩取五品，不可。」

translations.literal: Erudite Yang Fu said: "Grand Temple ritual officers are taken from sons of seventh rank; now Venerating Grace takes fifth rank—this cannot stand.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Yang Fu said, "Grand Temple ritual officers are drawn from sons of seventh rank, yet Venerating Grace now takes fifth rank—that will not do.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「太廟如崇恩可乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Can the Grand Temple follow Venerating Grace?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Can the Grand Temple follow Venerating Grace instead?"

sentences.zh: 孚曰：「崇恩太廟之私，以臣準君則僭，以君準臣則惑。」

translations.literal: Fu said: "Venerating Grace is private to the Grand Temple. Measured by subject against ruler it is presumptuous; measured by ruler against subject it is confused."
translations.idiomatic: Fu said, "Venerating Grace is a private adjunct to the Grand Temple. Judged as subject against ruler it is presumptuous; judged as ruler against subject it is muddled."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The matter was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was halted.

sentences.zh: 及韋、武黨誅，詔則天大聖皇后復號天后，廢崇恩廟及陵。

translations.literal: When the Wei and Wu factions were executed, an edict restored the title Great Sage Empress to Zetian Great Sage Empress, and Venerating Grace Temple and its mausoleum were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei and Wu factions were executed, an edict restored the title Great Sage Empress to Zetian Great Sage Empress and abolished Venerating Grace Temple and its mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，號大聖天后。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Radiant Cloud era she was titled Great Sage Empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Radiant Cloud she was titled Great Sage Empress.

sentences.zh: 太平公主奸政，請復二陵官，又尊后曰天后聖帝，俄號聖后。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping meddled in government and requested restoration of the two mausoleum offices; she again honored the empress as Great Sage Holy Emperor, and soon as Holy Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping interfered in government and asked to restore the two mausoleum offices; she again honored the empress as Great Sage Holy Emperor, and soon as Holy Empress.

sentences.zh: 太平誅，詔黜周孝明皇帝號，復為太原郡王，后為妃，罷昊、順等陵。

translations.literal: When Taiping was executed, an edict removed the Zhou title Filial and Illustrious Emperor, restored Taiyuan Prince of the County, the empress became consort, and the Vast, Compliance, and other mausoleums were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiping was executed, an edict stripped the Zhou title Filial and Illustrious Emperor, restored Taiyuan Prince of the County, reduced the empress to consort, and abolished the Vast, Compliance, and other mausoleums.

sentences.zh: 開元四年，追號則天皇后。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Kaiyuan era she was posthumously titled Empress Zetian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan she was posthumously titled Empress Zetian.

sentences.zh: 太常卿姜晈建言：「則天皇后配高宗廟，主題天后聖帝，非是，請易題為則天皇后武氏。」

translations.literal: Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Jiang Jiao submitted a proposal: "Empress Zetian matched in Gaozong's temple with the main tablet reading Great Sage Holy Emperor is incorrect. Please change the tablet to Empress Zetian of the Wu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Imperial Sacrifices Jiang Jiao proposed, "Empress Zetian's spirit tablet in Gaozong's temple, inscribed Great Sage Holy Emperor, is improper. Please change the inscription to Empress Zetian of the Wu clan.

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 中宗和思趙皇后中宗和思順聖皇后趙氏，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Empress He Si of Zhongzong—Empress Zhao, styled Harmonious in Thought and Submissive in Sagacity, of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Empress He Si of Zhongzong—Empress Zhao, styled Harmonious in Thought and Submissive in Sagacity, a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖綽，武德中，戰有功，終右領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Chuo had merit in battle during the Wude era and ended as Right Commander of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Chuo won merit in battle during the Wude era and ended as Right Commander of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 父瓌，尚高祖常樂公主。

translations.literal: Her father Gui married Princess Changle, daughter of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Gui married Princess Changle, daughter of Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 帝為英王，聘后為妃。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Ying he betrothed the empress as consort.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was Prince of Ying he took her as consort.

sentences.zh: 高宗於公主恩尤隆。

translations.literal: Gaozong's favor toward the princess was especially abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong's favor toward the princess was especially great.

sentences.zh: 武后不喜，乃幽妃內侍省。

translations.literal: Empress Wu disliked this and had the consort confined in the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu disliked this and had the consort confined in the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 瓌自定州刺史、駙馬都尉貶括州，絕主朝謁，隨瓌之官。

translations.literal: Gui was demoted from prefect of Dingzhou and Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law to Kuozhou; audiences with the princess ceased, and she followed Gui to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was demoted from prefect of Dingzhou and Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law to Kuozhou; the princess ceased her court audiences, and the consort followed Gui to his post.

sentences.zh: 妃既囚，扃鍵牢謹，日給飼料。

translations.literal: Once the consort was imprisoned, bolts and locks were strict; daily fodder was supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Once imprisoned, the consort was held under strict bolts and locks; fodder was supplied each day.

sentences.zh: 衛者候其突煙數日不出，披戶視之，死腐矣，瓌以壽州刺史與主預越王事，死。

translations.literal: Guards watched until smoke from her cooking failed to rise for several days; they broke open the door and looked—she had died and rotted. Gui, as prefect of Shouzhou, and the princess were implicated in the Prince of Yue affair and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Guards waited until smoke from her cooking failed to rise for several days, then broke open the door and found her dead and decayed. Gui, as prefect of Shouzhou, and the princess were implicated in the Prince of Yue affair and were executed.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，追謚妃曰恭皇后，贈瓌左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Divine Dragon the consort was posthumously titled Respectful Empress and Gui was given Left Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Divine Dragon the consort was posthumously titled Respectful Empress and Gui was granted Left Guard General.

sentences.zh: 中宗崩，蕆陵事，韋庶人不臣，不得祔，有司加上尊謚，以后祔定陵。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong died and burial affairs were arranged, Consort Wei was not a legitimate wife and could not be enshrined; the relevant offices added a lofty posthumous title and enshrined the empress at Ding Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong died and burial affairs were arranged, Consort Wei was not a legitimate wife and could not be enshrined; the relevant offices added a lofty posthumous title and enshrined the empress at Ding Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 中宗韋皇后中宗庶人韋氏，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Empress Wei of Zhongzong—Consort Wei of Zhongzong, a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei of Zhongzong—Consort Wei of Zhongzong, a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖弘表，貞觀中曹王府典軍。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Hongbiao was a staff officer in Prince Cao's household during the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Hongbiao served as a staff officer in Prince Cao's household during the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 帝在東宮，后被選為妃。

translations.literal: When the emperor was crown prince she was chosen as consort.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was crown prince she was chosen as consort.

sentences.zh: 嗣聖初，立為皇后。

translations.literal: At the start of the Restoration of the Sage era she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Restoration of the Sage she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 俄與帝處房陵，每使至，帝輒恐，欲自殺。

translations.literal: Soon she and the emperor were confined at Fangling. Whenever an envoy arrived the emperor would grow fearful and wish to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she and the emperor were confined at Fangling. Whenever an envoy arrived the emperor would grow fearful and wish to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 後止曰：「禍福何常，早晚等死耳，無遽！」

translations.literal: The empress stopped him, saying: "Fortune and misfortune have no constancy—you will die sooner or later all the same. Do not hurry!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress stopped him, saying, "Fortune and misfortune have no constancy—you will die sooner or later all the same. Do not hurry!

sentences.zh: 及帝復即位，后居中宮。

translations.literal: When the emperor resumed the throne the empress held the central palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor resumed the throne the empress held the central palace.

sentences.zh: 是時，上官昭容與政事，方敬暉等將盡誅諸武，武三思懼，乃因昭容入請，得幸於后，卒謀暉等誅之。
