translations.literal: At that time Shangguan Zhaorong shared in government affairs. Jing Hui and others were about to execute the Wu clan entirely; Wu Sansi grew afraid and, through Zhaorong, entered to plead and won the empress's favor, finally plotting to execute Hui and the others.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shangguan Zhaorong shared in government. Jing Hui and others were about to execute the entire Wu clan; Wu Sansi grew afraid and, through Zhaorong, entered to plead and won the empress's favor, finally plotting to kill Hui and his party.

sentences.zh: 初，帝幽廢，與后約：「一朝見天日，不相制。」

translations.literal: Earlier, while the emperor was in disgrace, he and the empress agreed: "Once we see the light of day again, we will not restrain each other."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while the emperor was in disgrace, he and the empress agreed, "Once we see the light of day again, we will not restrain each other.

sentences.zh: 至是與三思升御床博戲，帝從旁典籌，不為忤。

translations.literal: Now he and Sansi mounted the imperial couch to gamble, the emperor standing beside them keeping score, not offended.
translations.idiomatic: Now he and Sansi mounted the imperial couch to gamble, with the emperor standing beside them keeping score, unoffended.

sentences.zh: 三思諷群臣上后號為順天皇后。

translations.literal: Sansi induced the ministers to petition adding for the empress the title Heaven-Compliant Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi induced the ministers to petition that the empress be given the title Heaven-Compliant Empress.

sentences.zh: 乃親謁宗廟，贈父玄貞上洛郡王。

translations.literal: She thereupon personally visited the ancestral temple and enfeoffed her father Xuanzhen as Prince of Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: She thereupon personally visited the ancestral temple and enfeoffed her father Xuanzhen as Prince of Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺賈虛己建言：「非李氏王者，盟書共棄之。

translations.literal: Left Reminder Jia Xuji submitted a memorial: "Any king not of the Li clan—the covenant tablet jointly abandons him.
translations.idiomatic: Left Reminder Jia Xuji submitted a memorial: "Any king not of the Li clan—the covenant tablet jointly abandons him.

sentences.zh: 今復國未幾，遽私后家，且先朝禍鑒未遠，甚可懼也。

translations.literal: The realm has barely been restored, yet you hasten to favor the empress's clan; moreover the recent disaster of the former court is not far off—this is deeply to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has barely been restored, yet you hasten to favor the empress's clan; moreover the recent disaster of the former court is not far off—this is deeply to be feared.

sentences.zh: 如今皇后固辭，使天下知後宮謙讓，不亦善乎？」

translations.literal: If now the empress firmly declines, letting the realm know the inner palace is modest and yielding—would that not also be good?"
translations.idiomatic: If now the empress firmly declines, letting the realm know the inner palace is modest and yielding—would that not also be good?

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 神龍三年，節愍太子舉兵敗。

translations.literal: In the third year of Divine Dragon the Exasperated and Grieved Crown Prince raised troops and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Divine Dragon the Exasperated and Grieved Crown Prince raised troops and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 宗楚客率群臣請加號「翊聖」，詔可。

translations.literal: Zong Chuke led the ministers to petition adding the epithet "Assisting in Sagacity"; the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke led the ministers to petition adding the epithet Assisting in Sagacity; the edict approved.

sentences.zh: 禁中謬傳有五色雲起后衣笥，帝圖以示諸朝，因大赦天下，賜百官母、妻封號。

translations.literal: Within the palace it was falsely rumored that five-colored clouds had risen over the empress's clothes chest. The emperor painted it and showed the court, then proclaimed a great amnesty for the realm and granted noble titles to the mothers and wives of the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace it was falsely rumored that five-colored clouds had risen over the empress's clothes chest. The emperor had it painted and shown to the court, then proclaimed a great amnesty and granted noble titles to officials' mothers and wives.

sentences.zh: 太史迦葉志忠表上《桑條歌》十二篇，言后當受命，曰：「昔高祖時，天下歌《桃李》；

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Ye Zhizhong submitted twelve chapters of "Mulberry Branch Songs," saying the empress was destined to receive the mandate: "In Gaozu's time the realm sang Peach and Plum;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Ye Zhizhong submitted twelve chapters of Mulberry Branch Songs, saying the empress was destined to receive the mandate: "In Gaozu's time the realm sang Peach and Plum;

sentences.zh: 太宗時，歌《秦王破陣》；

translations.literal: in Taizong's time they sang Break the Enemy Array of the Prince of Qin;
translations.idiomatic: in Taizong's time they sang Break the Enemy Array of the Prince of Qin;

sentences.zh: 高宗歌《堂堂》；

translations.literal: in Gaozong's time they sang Stately;
translations.idiomatic: in Gaozong's time they sang Stately;

sentences.zh: 天后世，歌《武媚娘》；

translations.literal: in the empress's era they sang Lady Wu;
translations.idiomatic: in the empress's era they sang Lady Wu;

sentences.zh: 皇帝受命，歌《英王石州》；

translations.literal: when the emperor received the mandate they sang Prince of Ying's Stone Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor received the mandate they sang Prince of Ying's Stone Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 后今受命，歌《桑條韋》，蓋后妃之德專蠶桑，共宗廟事也。」

translations.literal: now that the empress receives the mandate they sing Mulberry Branch Wei—the empress's virtue lies wholly in sericulture and mulberry, jointly serving the ancestral temple."
translations.idiomatic: now that the empress receives the mandate they sing Mulberry Branch Wei—the empress's virtue lies wholly in sericulture and mulberry, jointly serving the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 乃賜志忠第一區，綵七百段。

translations.literal: He was granted a first-class residence and seven hundred bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a first-class residence and seven hundred bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿鄭愔因之被樂府。

translations.literal: Director of Sacrifices Zheng Yin thereupon had it admitted to the Music Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Sacrifices Zheng Yin thereupon had it admitted to the Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 楚客又諷補闕趙延禧離釋《桑條》為九十八代，帝大喜，擢延禧諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Chuke again induced Reminder Zhao Yanxi to expound Mulberry Branch as ninety-eight generations; the emperor was greatly pleased and promoted Yanxi to Remonstrating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke again induced Reminder Zhao Yanxi to expound Mulberry Branch as ninety-eight generations; the emperor was greatly pleased and promoted Yanxi to Remonstrating Censor.

sentences.zh: 於是昭容以武氏事動后。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhaorong moved the empress with Wu clan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhaorong moved the empress with Wu clan affairs.

sentences.zh: 即表增出母服；

translations.literal: She memorialized to extend mourning for mothers;
translations.idiomatic: She memorialized to extend mourning for mothers;

sentences.zh: 民以二十三為丁，限五十九免；

translations.literal: commoners were registered as adult laborers at twenty-three, exempted at fifty-nine;
translations.idiomatic: commoners were registered as adult laborers at twenty-three, exempted at fifty-nine;

sentences.zh: 五品而上母、妻不繇夫、子封者，喪得用鼓吹。

translations.literal: for fifth rank and above, mothers and wives not ennobled through husband or son might use drums and pipes at funerals.
translations.idiomatic: for fifth rank and above, mothers and wives not ennobled through husband or son might use drums and pipes at funerals.

sentences.zh: 數改制度，陰儲人望。

translations.literal: Institutions were changed again and again, secretly storing up popular regard.
translations.idiomatic: Institutions were changed again and again, secretly storing up popular regard.

sentences.zh: 稍寵樹親屬，封拜之。

translations.literal: She gradually favored and enfeoffed her kin.
translations.idiomatic: She gradually favored and enfeoffed her kin.

sentences.zh: 昭容與母及尚宮賀婁等多受金錢。

translations.literal: Zhaorong, her mother, Palace Attendant He Lou, and others received much gold and money.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaorong, her mother, Palace Attendant He Lou, and others received much gold and money.

sentences.zh: 封巫趙隴西夫人，出入禁中，勢與上官埒。

translations.literal: The shaman Zhao was enfeoffed as Lady of Longxi and went in and out of the inner palace, her power equal to Shangguan's.
translations.idiomatic: The shaman Zhao was enfeoffed as Lady of Longxi and went in and out of the inner palace, her power equal to Shangguan's.

sentences.zh: 繇是墨敕斜封出矣。

translations.literal: From this issued improperly sealed edicts at a slant.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth came the slant-sealed edicts of illicit appointment.

sentences.zh: 三年，帝親郊，引后亞獻。

translations.literal: In the third year the emperor personally sacrificed at the suburban altar and led the empress as secondary offerer.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the emperor personally sacrificed at the suburban altar and led the empress as secondary offerer.

sentences.zh: 明年，正月望夜，帝與后微服過市，彷徉觀覽，縱宮女出遊，皆淫奔不還。

translations.literal: The next year, on the night of the first full moon, the emperor and empress went in plain dress through the market, strolling to view sights; palace women were released to roam, and many ran off in debauchery and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on the night of the first full moon, the emperor and empress went in plain dress through the market, strolling to view sights; palace women were released to roam, and many ran off in debauchery and did not return.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒葉靜能善禁架，常侍馬秦客高醫，光祿少卿楊均善烹調，皆引入後廷。

translations.literal: Director of the National University Ye Jingneng was skilled at occult confinement; Regular Attendant Ma Qinke was a fine physician; Vice Director of the Imperial Commissary Yang Jun was skilled at cookery—all were brought into the empress's rear apartments.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the National University Ye Jingneng was skilled at occult confinement; Regular Attendant Ma Qinke was a fine physician; Vice Director of the Imperial Commissary Yang Jun was skilled at cookery—all were brought into the empress's rear apartments.

sentences.zh: 均、秦客蒸於后，嘗喪免，不歷旬輒起。

translations.literal: Jun and Qinke had illicit relations with the empress; when they occasionally observed mourning they were restored within less than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Qinke had illicit relations with the empress; when they occasionally observed mourning they were restored within less than ten days.

sentences.zh: 帝遇弒，議者讙咎秦客及安樂公主。

translations.literal: The emperor met assassination; opinion clamored against Qinke and Princess Anle.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor met assassination; opinion clamored against Qinke and Princess Anle.

sentences.zh: 后大懼，引所親議計，乃以刑部尚書裴談、工部尚書張錫輔政，留守東都，詔將軍趙承福、薛簡以兵五百衛譙王重福，與兄溫定策，立溫王重茂為皇太子，列府兵五萬分二營屯京師，然後發喪。

translations.literal: The empress was greatly afraid and summoned her intimates to deliberate. She made Minister of Justice Pei Tan and Minister of Works Zhang Xi assist in government, remaining to guard the Eastern Capital, and decreed generals Zhao Chenfu and Xue Jian with five hundred troops to guard Prince Chongfu of Qiao; with her brother Wen she settled on making Prince Chongmao of Wen crown prince, arraying fifty thousand household troops in two camps stationed at the capital, and then issuing the mourning announcement.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was terrified and summoned her intimates to plot. She appointed Pei Tan, Minister of Justice, and Zhang Xi, Minister of Works, to assist in government while she remained to guard the Eastern Capital; she ordered generals Zhao Chenfu and Xue Jian with five hundred troops to guard Prince Chongfu of Qiao. With her brother Wen she resolved to make Prince Chongmao of Wen crown prince, mustered fifty thousand household troops in two camps around the capital, and only then announced the mourning.

sentences.zh: 太子即位，是為殤帝。

translations.literal: The crown prince ascended the throne—this was the Lamented Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince ascended the throne—this was the Lamented Emperor.

sentences.zh: 皇太后臨朝，溫總內外兵，檢護宮省。

translations.literal: The empress dowager held court; Wen commanded inner and outer troops and inspected the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager held court; Wen commanded inner and outer troops and inspected the palace precincts.

sentences.zh: 族弟濯、播，宗子捷、璿，璿甥高崇及武延秀，分領左右屯營、羽林、飛騎、萬騎。

translations.literal: Clansmen Zhuo and Bo, lineage kin Jie and Xuan, Xuan's nephew Gao Chong, and Wu Yanxiu each commanded the left and right encampment guards, Imperial Guard, Flying Cavalry, and Ten Thousand Riders.
translations.idiomatic: Clansmen Zhuo and Bo, lineage kin Jie and Xuan, Xuan's nephew Gao Chong, and Wu Yanxiu each commanded the left and right encampment guards, Imperial Guard, Flying Cavalry, and Ten Thousand Riders.

sentences.zh: 京師大恐，傳言且革命。

translations.literal: The capital was greatly afraid; rumor spread that a revolution was imminent.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was greatly afraid; rumor spread that a revolution was imminent.

sentences.zh: 播、璿入軍中，鞭督萬騎欲立威，士怨不為用。

translations.literal: Bo and Xuan entered the army, lashing and urging the Ten Thousand Riders to establish authority; the soldiers resented it and would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Bo and Xuan entered the army, lashing and urging the Ten Thousand Riders to establish authority; the soldiers resented it and would not obey.

sentences.zh: 俄而臨淄王引兵夜披玄武門入羽林，殺璿、播、崇於寢，斧關叩太極殿，后遁入飛騎營，為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: Before long the Prince of Linzi led troops by night, broke through the Xuanwu Gate into the Imperial Guard, killed Xuan, Bo, and Chong in their quarters, axed the gate and knocked on the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; the empress fled into the Flying Cavalry camp and was killed by the mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Prince of Linzi led his men by night through the Xuanwu Gate into the Imperial Guard, slew Xuan, Bo, and Chong in their beds, hacked down the gate, and hammered on the Hall of Supreme Ultimate. The empress fled into the Flying Cavalry camp and was cut down by the mutineers.

sentences.zh: 斬延秀、安樂公主。

translations.literal: Yanxiu and Princess Anle were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxiu and Princess Anle were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 分捕諸韋、諸武與其支黨，悉誅之，梟后及安樂首東市。

translations.literal: They were hunted down separately—all the Weis, all the Wus, and their branch partisans—and all were executed; the empress's and Anle's heads were displayed at the Eastern Market.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei and Wu clans and their partisans were hunted down in separate sweeps and put to death. The empress's head and Anle's were displayed at the Eastern Market.

sentences.zh: 翌日，追貶為庶人，葬以一品禮。

translations.literal: The next day she was posthumously demoted to commoner and buried with first-rank rites.
translations.idiomatic: The next day she was posthumously stripped to commoner rank and buried with the rites due a first-rank consort.

sentences.zh: 上官昭容上官昭容者，名婉兒，西臺侍郎儀之孫。

translations.literal: Shangguan Zhaorong—Shangguan Zhaorong, named Wan'er, was granddaughter of Secretariat Vice Director Yi of the Western Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Zhaorong—her name was Wan'er—was granddaughter of Shangguan Yi, vice director of the Western Terrace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父廷芝，與儀死武后時。

translations.literal: Her father Tingzhi died together with Yi in Empress Wu's time.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Tingzhi had been executed with Yi in the time of Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 母鄭，太常少卿休遠之姊。

translations.literal: Her mother Zheng was elder sister of Vice Minister of Imperial Rites Xiuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother, surnamed Zheng, was elder sister to Xiuyuan, vice minister of imperial rites.

sentences.zh: 婉兒始生，與母配掖廷。

translations.literal: When Wan'er was first born, she and her mother were assigned to the Palace Reclusion Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At her birth Wan'er and her mother were assigned to the Palace Reclusion Bureau.

sentences.zh: 天性韶警，善文章。

translations.literal: By nature she was gifted and quick-witted, skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Naturally gifted and quick-witted, she excelled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 年十四，武后召見，有所制作，若素構。

translations.literal: At age fourteen Empress Wu summoned her; whatever she composed seemed long premeditated.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen she was summoned by Empress Wu; whatever she wrote seemed as though it had been composed long before.

sentences.zh: 自通天以來，內掌詔命，掞麗可觀。

translations.literal: From the Tongtian era onward she managed edicts within; her polished prose was admirable.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tongtian era onward she controlled edicts within the palace, and her polished prose was a pleasure to read.

sentences.zh: 嘗忤旨當誅，後惜其才，止黥而不殺也。

translations.literal: Once she offended the intent and should have been executed; the empress prized her talent and only tattooed her face, not killing her.
translations.idiomatic: Once she offended the throne and was condemned to die, but the empress valued her talent and commuted the sentence to facial tattooing.

sentences.zh: 然群臣奏議及天下事皆與之。

translations.literal: Yet on all matters of ministers' memorials and affairs under Heaven she was consulted.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless she was consulted on every memorial from the ministers and on affairs throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，大被信任，進拜昭容，封鄭沛國夫人。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne she was greatly trusted, advanced to Zhaorong, and enfeoffed Lady of Zheng and Peiguo.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong took the throne she won his deep trust, was promoted to Zhaorong, and enfeoffed as Lady of Zheng and Peiguo.

sentences.zh: 婉兒通武三思，故詔書推右武氏，抑唐家，節愍太子不平。

translations.literal: Wan'er was intimate with Wu Sansi; therefore edicts favored the Wu clan and suppressed the house of Tang, and Crown Prince Jiemin was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Wan'er was intimate with Wu Sansi, so edicts favored the Wu clan and slighted the Tang house, to Crown Prince Jiemin's outrage.

sentences.zh: 及舉兵，叩肅章門索婉兒，婉兒曰：「我死，當次索皇后、大家矣！」

translations.literal: When he raised troops and knocked at Suozhang Gate demanding Wan'er, Wan'er said: "If I die, you will next demand the empress and the Great One!"
translations.idiomatic: When he raised troops and knocked at Suozhang Gate demanding Wan'er, she said, "If you kill me, you will next demand the empress and the Great One!"

sentences.zh: 以激怒帝，帝與后挾婉兒登玄武門避之。

translations.literal: To enrage the emperor—the emperor and empress took Wan'er up onto the Xuanwu Gate to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: She meant to enrage the emperor; he and the empress took Wan'er up onto the Xuanwu Gate ramparts to escape him.

sentences.zh: 會太子敗，乃免。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was defeated, she was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was defeated, she was spared.

sentences.zh: 婉兒勸帝侈大書館，增學士員，引大臣名儒充選。

translations.literal: Wan'er urged the emperor to expand the Hall of Literature, increase the number of academicians, and draw great ministers and renowned scholars to fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Wan'er urged the emperor to enlarge the Hall of Literature, add academicians, and appoint leading ministers and famous scholars to the posts.

sentences.zh: 數賜宴賦詩，群臣賡和，婉兒常代帝及后、長寧安樂二主，眾篇並作，而采麗益新。

translations.literal: Repeatedly banquets were granted for composing verse; the ministers responded in chorus; Wan'er often composed in place of the emperor, empress, and the two princesses of Changning and Anle—many pieces at once—and literary adornment grew ever fresher.
translations.idiomatic: The court held repeated banquets for poetry; ministers answered in verse; Wan'er often wrote for the emperor, the empress, and the princesses of Changning and Anle at once, and the anthology grew ever more brilliant.

sentences.zh: 又差第群臣所賦，賜金爵，故朝廷靡然成風。

translations.literal: She also ranked the ministers' compositions and bestowed gold cups, so the court swept into the fashion.
translations.idiomatic: She also ranked the ministers' poems and bestowed gold cups, and the whole court fell into the fashion.

sentences.zh: 當時屬辭者，大抵雖浮靡，然所得皆有可觀，婉兒力也。

translations.literal: Those who composed at the time, though mostly florid and extravagant, yet produced work worth viewing—Wan'er's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Writers of the day, though often florid, still produced work worth reading, and that was Wan'er's influence.

sentences.zh: 鄭卒，謚節義夫人。

translations.literal: When Zheng died, she was posthumously titled Lady of Chaste Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother Zheng died, she was posthumously titled Lady of Chaste Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 婉兒請降秩行服，詔起為婕妤，俄還昭容。

translations.literal: Wan'er asked to lower her rank to observe mourning; an edict recalled her as Jieyu, and soon she returned to Zhaorong.
translations.idiomatic: Wan'er asked to step down in rank to observe mourning; an edict recalled her as Jieyu, and soon restored her to Zhaorong.

sentences.zh: 帝即婉兒居穿沼築巖，窮飾勝趣，即引侍臣宴其所。

translations.literal: The emperor at Wan'er's residence bored ponds and piled rockeries, exhausting ornament for scenic delight, and at once led attendant ministers to feast there.
translations.idiomatic: At Wan'er's residence the emperor had ponds dug and rockeries built, lavishing ornament on the scenery, and often led his attendant ministers to feast there.

sentences.zh: 是時，左右內職皆聽出外，不何止。

translations.literal: At that time all inner attendants left and right were permitted to go outside; they were not stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At that time inner attendants on left and right were allowed to leave the palace, and no one stopped them.

sentences.zh: 婉兒與近嬖至皆營外宅，衺人穢夫爭候門下，肆狎昵，因以求劇職要官。

translations.literal: Wan'er and the nearest favorites all maintained outer residences; wicked men and vile husbands vied to wait at their gates, wantonly familiar, and thereby sought weighty offices and key posts.
translations.idiomatic: Wan'er and her closest favorites all kept houses outside the palace; rogues and low companions crowded their gates, trading familiarity for high office.

sentences.zh: 與崔湜亂，遂引知政事。

translations.literal: She had an affair with Cui Shi and thereby drew him into knowing government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Through an affair with Cui Shi she brought him into the councils of state.

sentences.zh: 湜開商山道，未半，因帝遺制，虛列其功，加甄賞。

translations.literal: Shi opened the Shangshan road; before it was half done, by the emperor's dying edict his merit was falsely entered and rewards were increased.
translations.idiomatic: Shi began the Shangshan road; before it was half finished, the dying edict credited him with merit he had not earned and heaped rewards upon him.

sentences.zh: 韋后之敗，斬闕下。

translations.literal: When Empress Wei fell, she was beheaded below the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei fell, Wan'er was beheaded below the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 初，鄭方妊，夢巨人畀大稱曰：「持此稱量天下。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zheng was pregnant, she dreamed a giant gave her a great steelyard saying: "Take this steelyard and weigh all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Zheng was pregnant, she dreamed a giant handed her a great steelyard and said, "Take this and weigh all under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 婉兒生逾月，母戲曰：「稱量者豈爾邪？」

translations.literal: When Wan'er was just over a month old, her mother jested: "Can the weigher be you?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wan'er was barely a month old, her mother teased, "Can you be the one who weighs the realm?"

sentences.zh: 輒啞然應。

translations.literal: She at once responded with a knowing sound.
translations.idiomatic: The infant answered with a knowing murmur.

sentences.zh: 後內秉機政，符其夢云。

translations.literal: Later, holding civil power within, she matched that dream.
translations.idiomatic: Later she held power within the palace, fulfilling the dream.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，追復昭容，謚惠文。

translations.literal: In the Jingyun era she was posthumously restored to Zhaorong and given the posthumous title Huiven.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingyun era she was posthumously restored to Zhaorong and titled Huiven.

sentences.zh: 始，從母子王昱為拾遺，昱戒曰：「上往囚房陵，武氏得志矣，卒而中興，天命所在，不可幸也。

translations.literal: At the beginning, her cousin's son Wang Yu was Reminder; Yu admonished: "The emperor was once imprisoned at Fang Prefecture; the Wu clan gained its will; at last the house was restored—where Heaven's mandate lies cannot be gambled on.
translations.idiomatic: At first her cousin's son Wang Yu served as Reminder. Yu warned her, "The emperor was once a prisoner at Fang; the Wu clan rose to power, yet the Tang was restored in the end. Where Heaven's mandate rests is not a thing to wager on.

sentences.zh: 三思雖乘釁，天下知必敗，今昭容上所信，而附之，且滅族！」

translations.literal: Sansi though seizing the breach—all under Heaven knew he must fail; now Zhaorong is what the emperor trusts, yet you attach to her—you will destroy the clan!"
translations.idiomatic: Sansi may seize his chance, but the realm knows he must fall. Zhaorong has the emperor's trust, yet you cling to her—you will destroy our clan!"

sentences.zh: 鄭以責婉兒，不從。

translations.literal: Zheng reproached Wan'er; she would not heed.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Zheng rebuked Wan'er, but she would not listen.

sentences.zh: 節愍誅三思，果索之，始憂懼。

translations.literal: When Jiemin executed Sansi and indeed came seeking her, she first grew fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiemin killed Sansi and came for her as well, fear seized her at last.

sentences.zh: 及草遺制，即引相王輔政。

translations.literal: When drafting the dying edict, she at once brought in the Prince of Xiang to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: When she drafted the dying edict, she named the Prince of Xiang to assist in government.

sentences.zh: 臨淄王兵起，被收。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Linzi's troops rose, she was seized.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Linzi rose in arms, she was taken.

sentences.zh: 婉兒以詔草示劉幽求，幽求言之王，王不許，遂誅。

translations.literal: Wan'er showed the draft edict to Liu Youqiu; Youqiu spoke of it to the prince; the prince would not agree, and she was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wan'er showed the draft edict to Liu Youqiu; Youqiu urged it on the prince, but the prince refused, and she was put to death.

sentences.zh: 開元初，裒次其文章，詔張說題篇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan her writings were collected and ordered; Zhang Yue was decreed to compose the preface.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan her writings were collected and an edict commissioned Zhang Yue to write the preface.

sentences.zh: 睿宗肅明劉皇后睿宗肅明順聖皇后劉氏，祖德威，自有傳。

translations.literal: Empress Suoming of Ruizong—Empress Suoming Shunsheng Liu of Ruizong: her grandfather was Dewei, who has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Suoming of Ruizong—Empress Suoming Shunsheng, née Liu: her grandfather Dewei has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，帝在籓，納為孺人，俄為妃。

translations.literal: In the Yifeng era, when the emperor was in the fief, she was taken in as Lady; soon she became Consort.
translations.idiomatic: During Yifeng, while he was still a prince, she entered his household as Lady and soon became Consort.

sentences.zh: 生寧王、壽昌代國二公主。

translations.literal: She bore the Prince of Ning and the two princesses of Shouchang and Daiguo.
translations.idiomatic: She bore the Prince of Ning and the princesses of Shouchang and Daiguo.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，為皇后。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, she became empress.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne she became empress.

sentences.zh: 會帝降號皇嗣，復為妃。

translations.literal: When the emperor was demoted to the title Heir Apparent of the Emperor, she again became consort.
translations.idiomatic: When he was reduced to heir apparent she again became consort.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，為戶婢誣與竇德妃挾蠱道祝詛武后，並殺之宮中，葬秘莫知。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou, a household maid falsely accused her and Virtuous Consort Dou of employing witchcraft to curse Empress Wu; both were killed in the palace; burial was secret and unknown.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changshou a household maid accused her and Virtuous Consort Dou of sorcery against Empress Wu; both were killed in the palace and buried in secret, their graves unknown.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，追謚肅明皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun she was posthumously titled Empress Suoming.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingyun she was posthumously titled Empress Suoming.

sentences.zh: 睿宗昭成竇皇后睿宗昭成順聖皇后竇氏，曾祖抗，父孝諶，自有傳。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaocheng of Ruizong—Empress Zhaocheng Shunsheng Dou of Ruizong: her great-grandfather was Kang; her father Xiaochen has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaocheng of Ruizong—Empress Zhaocheng Shunsheng, née Dou: her great-grandfather was Kang; her father Xiaochen has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 后婉淑，尤循禮則。

translations.literal: The empress was gentle and refined, especially observant of ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and refined, she was especially strict in ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 帝為相王，納為孺人；

translations.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Xiang, she was taken in as Lady;
translations.idiomatic: When he was Prince of Xiang she entered his household as Lady;

sentences.zh: 即位，進德妃。

translations.literal: upon taking the throne she was advanced to Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: on his accession she was promoted to Virtuous Consort.

sentences.zh: 生玄宗及金仙、玉真二公主。

translations.literal: She bore Xuanzong and the two princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Xuanzong and the princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen.

sentences.zh: 與肅明同追謚，並招魂葬東都之南，肅明曰惠陵，後曰靖陵，立別廟曰儀坤以享云。

translations.literal: Together with Suoming she received posthumous titles; both were buried by summoning the soul south of the Eastern Capital—Suoming's called Huiling, the empress's Jingling; a separate temple called Yikun was established for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: She and Suoming received posthumous titles together; both were given soul-summoning burials south of the Eastern Capital—Huiling for Suoming, Jingling for Dou—and a separate temple, Yikun, was built for their rites.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，追稱皇太后，與肅明祔橋陵。

translations.literal: When the emperor died she was posthumously styled Empress Dowager and, with Suoming, was enshrined at Qiao Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: At Ruizong's death she was posthumously styled empress dowager and enshrined with Suoming at Qiao Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 後以子貴，故先祔睿宗室。

translations.literal: The empress, because her son was exalted, was therefore first enshrined in Ruizong's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Because her son became emperor, she was enshrined in Ruizong's temple before Suoming.

sentences.zh: 肅明以開元二十年乃得祔廟。

translations.literal: Suoming only in the twentieth year of Kaiyuan obtained enshrinement in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Suoming was not enshrined in the ancestral temple until the twentieth year of Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，太常加謚後曰「大昭成」。

translations.literal: At first the Court of Imperial Sacrifices added to the empress's posthumous title "Great Zhaocheng."
translations.idiomatic: At first the Court of Imperial Sacrifices added the epithet "Great Zhaocheng" to her posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 或言：「法宜引『聖真』冠謚，而曰『大昭成』，非也。

translations.literal: Someone said: "By regulation one should take 'Holy and True' to crown the posthumous title, yet it says 'Great Zhaocheng'—this is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Someone objected, "By regulation the epithet should begin with 'Holy and True,' not 'Great Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 以單言配之，應曰『聖昭』若『睿成』；

translations.literal: Matched with a single word, it should read 'Holy Zhao' or 'Sagacious Cheng';
translations.idiomatic: With a single epithet it should read 'Holy Zhao' or 'Sagacious Cheng';

sentences.zh: 以復言配之，應曰『大聖昭成』、『聖真昭成』。」

translations.literal: matched with a doubled phrase, it should read 'Great Holy Zhaocheng' or 'Holy and True Zhaocheng.'"
translations.idiomatic: with a doubled epithet it should read 'Great Holy Zhaocheng' or 'Holy and True Zhaocheng.'"

sentences.zh: 又引太穆皇后始謚穆，及高祖崩，合帝謚曰太穆，追增太穆神皇后；

translations.literal: He also cited Empress Taimu, who was first posthumously titled Mu; when Gaozu died, combined with the emperor's title she became Taimu; she was further advanced to Divine Empress Taimu;
translations.idiomatic: He cited Empress Taimu, first titled simply Mu; at Gaozu's death her title was joined with his as Taimu and she was advanced to Divine Empress Taimu;

sentences.zh: 文德皇后始謚文德，及太宗崩，合謚文德聖皇后。

translations.literal: Empress Wende was first posthumously titled Wende; when Taizong died, combined she became Holy Empress Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wende was first titled Wende alone; at Taizong's death she became Holy Empress Wende.

sentences.zh: 又援范曄著漢光烈等為比。

translations.literal: He also cited Fan Ye's writing of Han Guanglie and others as parallels.
translations.idiomatic: He also cited Fan Ye's titles such as Han Guanglie as precedents.

sentences.zh: 太常謂：「曄以帝號標后謚，是史家記事體，婦人非必與夫同也。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices said: "Ye used the emperor's title to label the empress's posthumous name—that is the historian's narrative form; a woman need not necessarily share with her husband.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices replied, "Fan Ye prefixed the emperor's title to the empress's epithet in the manner of historians; a wife need not share her husband's title.

sentences.zh: 入廟稱后，繫夫；

translations.literal: In the temple she is called empress, tied to the husband;
translations.idiomatic: In the ancestral temple she is called empress and tied to her husband;

sentences.zh: 在朝稱太，繫子。

translations.literal: at court she is called Grand, tied to the son.
translations.idiomatic: at court she is styled Grand and tied to her son.

sentences.zh: 『文母』，生號也；

translations.literal: 'Mother Wen' is the living title;
translations.idiomatic: 'Mother Wen' was her title in life;

sentences.zh: 『文王』，既沒謚也。

translations.literal: 'King Wen' is the posthumous title after death.
translations.idiomatic: 'King Wen' was his posthumous title after death.

sentences.zh: 周公豈以夫從婦乎？

translations.literal: Did the Duke of Zhou take the husband's title from the wife?
translations.idiomatic: Did the Duke of Zhou derive the husband's title from the wife?

sentences.zh: 漢法不可以為據。」

translations.literal: Han regulations cannot serve as authority."
translations.idiomatic: Han precedent cannot govern this case."

sentences.zh: 制曰「可」。

translations.literal: The decree said "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decreed, "Approved."

sentences.zh: 天寶八載制詔，自太穆而下六皇后，並增上「順聖」二謚云。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao an imperial decree added the two-character posthumous epithet "Shunsheng" to the six empresses from Taimu downward.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianbao a decree added the epithet "Shunsheng" to the six empresses from Taimu onward.

sentences.zh: 玄宗王皇后玄宗皇后王氏，同州下邽人。

translations.literal: Empress Wang of Xuanzong—Empress Wang of Xuanzong, a native of Xiaji in Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang of Xuanzong—Empress Wang, a native of Xiaji in Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 梁冀州刺史神念之裔孫。

translations.literal: Descendant of Liang Inspector General Shennian.
translations.idiomatic: She was a descendant of Liang's inspector general Wang Shennian.

sentences.zh: 帝為臨淄王，聘為妃。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Linzi, she was betrothed as consort.
translations.idiomatic: When he was Prince of Linzi she was betrothed as his consort.

sentences.zh: 將清內難，預大計。

translations.literal: About to settle the inner crisis, she took part in the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: When he prepared to settle the palace crisis, she took part in the great plan.

sentences.zh: 先天元年，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiantian she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiantian she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 久無子，而武妃稍有寵，后不平，顯詆之。

translations.literal: Long without a son, while Consort Wu gradually gained favor, the empress was displeased and openly slandered her.
translations.idiomatic: Childless for years while Consort Wu slowly won favor, the empress grew resentful and openly maligned her.

sentences.zh: 然撫下素有恩，終無肯譖短者。

translations.literal: Yet in treating subordinates she had long shown kindness; in the end none would speak ill of her.
translations.idiomatic: Yet she had always treated her attendants with kindness, and in the end none would speak against her.

sentences.zh: 帝密欲廢后，以語姜晈。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly wished to depose the empress and told Jiang Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly planned to depose her and confided in Jiang Jiao.

sentences.zh: 晈漏言，即死。

translations.literal: Jiao leaked the words and was immediately put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao leaked the plan and was executed at once.

sentences.zh: 后兄守一懼，為求厭勝，浮屠明悟教祭北斗，取霹靂木刻天地文及帝諱合佩之，曰：「後有子，與則天比。」

translations.literal: The empress's elder brother Shouyi grew afraid and sought sorcery for victory; the monk Mingwu taught sacrificing to the Northern Dipper, taking thunderbolt wood to carve the text of Heaven and Earth and the emperor's taboo name combined as a talisman, saying: "Later there will be a son, comparable to Empress Zetian."
translations.idiomatic: Her brother Shouyi, in fear, sought sorcery; the monk Mingwu taught rites to the Northern Dipper and fashioned a talisman from thunderbolt wood carved with the cosmic script and the emperor's taboo name, saying, "She will yet bear a son to rival Wu Zetian."

sentences.zh: 開元十二年，事覺，帝自臨劾有狀，乃制詔有司：「皇后天命不祐，華而不實，有無將之心，不可以承宗廟、母儀天下，其廢為庶人。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kaiyuan the affair was discovered; the emperor personally interrogated and the evidence was clear; then a decree to the offices: "The empress lacks Heaven's blessing, is showy without substance, harbors a mind of no heir—she cannot inherit the ancestral temples or mother the realm; let her be deposed as commoner."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Kaiyuan the plot was exposed; the emperor interrogated her himself and found proof. His decree to the ministries read, "The empress lacks Heaven's blessing, is splendid without substance, and harbors treasonous intent. She cannot receive the ancestral rites or mother the realm. Depose her as a commoner."

sentences.zh: 賜守一死。

translations.literal: Shouyi was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 始，后以愛弛，不自安。

translations.literal: At the beginning, because the empress's favor had slackened, she was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: From the time his affection waned, the empress lived in unease.

sentences.zh: 承閒泣曰：「陛下獨不念阿忠脫紫半臂易斗麵，為生日湯餅邪？」

translations.literal: Seizing an interval she wept: "Does Your Majesty alone not remember Loyal taking off his purple half-sleeve to exchange for a peck of flour to make birthday noodles?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, catching him at leisure, she wept, "Does Your Majesty not remember Loyal stripping off his purple half-sleeve to trade for flour so we could have birthday noodles?"

sentences.zh: 帝憫然動容。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved to compassion and showed it on his face.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face softened with pity.

sentences.zh: 阿忠，后呼其父仁皎云。

translations.literal: Loyal was what the empress called her father Renjiao.
translations.idiomatic: "Loyal" was the empress's name for her father Renjiao.

sentences.zh: 繇是久乃廢。

translations.literal: Because of this, long afterward she was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Because of that memory, her deposition was long delayed.

sentences.zh: 當時王諲作《翠羽帳賦》諷帝。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Ren composed "Green Feather Canopy Rhapsody" to admonish the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ren then wrote "Rhapsody on the Green Feather Canopy" to admonish the emperor.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，以一品禮葬。

translations.literal: Before long she died and was buried with first-rank rites.
translations.idiomatic: She died soon after and was buried with first-rank rites.

sentences.zh: 後宮思慕之，帝亦悔。

translations.literal: The inner palace mourned her; the emperor also regretted.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace mourned her, and the emperor regretted his act.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，追復后號。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying her empress title was posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying her empress title was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 玄宗貞順武皇后玄宗貞順皇后武氏，恒安王攸止女，幼入宮。

translations.literal: Empress Zhenshun Wu of Xuanzong—Empress Zhenshun Wu of Xuanzong, daughter of Prince of Heng'an Youzhi, entered the palace young.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhenshun Wu of Xuanzong—Empress Zhenshun Wu, daughter of Prince of Heng'an Youzhi, entered the palace as a girl.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，寖得幸。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, she gradually gained favor.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne she gradually won his favor.

sentences.zh: 時王皇后廢，故進冊惠妃，其禮秩比皇后。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Wang was deposed; therefore she was advanced and enfeoffed as Huifei, her ritual rank equal to empress.
translations.idiomatic: With Empress Wang deposed, she was advanced to Huifei, her ceremonial rank equal to an empress.

sentences.zh: 初，帝在潞，趙麗妃以倡幸，有容止，善歌舞。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when the emperor was at Lu, Consort Zhao Lihua as a singing girl gained favor—she had bearing and grace, skilled in song and dance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while he was at Lu, Consort Zhao Lihua, a singing girl, won his favor. Graceful in bearing, she excelled at song and dance.

sentences.zh: 開元初，父兄皆美官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, father and elder brothers all held fine offices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, her father and brothers all held distinguished posts.

sentences.zh: 及妃進，麗妃恩亦弛，以十四年卒，謚曰和。

translations.literal: When the consort was advanced, Consort Li's favor also slackened; in the fourteenth year she died, posthumous name He.
translations.idiomatic: As Consort Wu rose, Zhao Lihua's favor waned as well; Zhao died in the fourteenth year and was given the posthumous name He.

sentences.zh: 生太子瑛。

translations.literal: She bore Crown Prince Ying.
translations.idiomatic: She bore the crown prince, later Prince Ying.

sentences.zh: 而皇甫德儀生鄂王，劉才人生光王，皆藩邸之舊，後愛薄，而妃乃專寵。

translations.literal: Whereas Huangfu Deyi bore the Prince of E and Liu Cairen bore the Prince of Guang—all old companions of the princely residence—later their favor grew thin, while the consort alone enjoyed exclusive favor.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Deyi had borne the Prince of E and Liu Cairen the Prince of Guang, all veterans of his days as heir; their favor later faded, but Consort Wu held his affection alone.

sentences.zh: 封所生母楊鄭國夫人，弟忠國子祭酒，信秘書監。

translations.literal: Her birth mother Yang was enfeoffed as Lady of Zheng State; younger brother Zhong was made Director of the National University; Xin was made Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother, Lady Yang, was made Lady of Zheng; her brother Zhong became Director of the National University and Xin Secretary Director.

sentences.zh: 將遂立皇后，御史潘好禮上疏曰：「《禮》，父母讎，不共天。

translations.literal: About to proceed to establish her as empress, Censor Pan Haoli submitted a memorial saying: "The Rites: a parent's enemy—cannot share Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor was about to make her empress, Censor Pan Haoli memorialized: "The Rites teach that one cannot live under the same Heaven as one's parents' enemy.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》，子不復讎，不子也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals: the son who does not avenge—he is no son.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals holds that a son who will not avenge his father is no son at all.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲以武氏為后，何以見天下士！

translations.literal: Your Majesty wishes to make the Wu clan empress—how will you face the gentlemen of the realm!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would raise a woman of the Wu clan to empress, how will you face the scholars and officials of the realm?

sentences.zh: 妃再從叔三思也，從父延秀也，皆干紀亂常，天下共疾。

translations.literal: The consort's second cousin Sansi and cousin by the father's side Yanxiu—both violated statutes and disturbed norms; all under Heaven jointly loathed them.
translations.idiomatic: Her kinsmen Wu Sansi and Wu Yanxiu had both violated law and upset custom, and the empire hated them alike.

sentences.zh: 夫惡木垂蔭，志士不息；

translations.literal: Now, a wicked tree hangs its shade—men of resolve do not rest beneath it;
translations.idiomatic: A noble heart will not rest in the shade of a wicked tree;

sentences.zh: 盜泉飛溢，廉夫不飲。

translations.literal: the Thieving Spring flows brimming—a man of integrity will not drink from it.
translations.idiomatic: nor will an honest man drink from a spring called Thieving.

sentences.zh: 匹夫匹婦尚相擇，況天子乎？

translations.literal: Even common men and women still choose one another—how much more the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Even common folk choose their mates with care—how much more must the Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 願慎選華族，稱神祇之心。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will carefully select a noble clan, fitting the mind of the gods.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to choose carefully from a noble house, that your choice may accord with Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》：宋人夏父之會，無以妾為夫人；

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals: at the Assembly of Xiafu of Song, none made a concubine a Lady;
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that at the Assembly of Xiafu, the men of Song would not make a concubine a Lady;

sentences.zh: 齊桓公誓葵丘曰：『無以妾為妻。』

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi swore at Kuiqiu: 'Do not take a concubine as wife.'
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi swore at Kuiqiu, 'Do not elevate a concubine to wife.'

sentences.zh: 此聖人明嫡庶之分。

translations.literal: This is how the sages clarified the distinction of principal wife and secondary.
translations.idiomatic: Thus did the sages mark the line between principal wife and concubine.

sentences.zh: 分定，則窺競之心息矣。

translations.literal: Once the distinction is settled, the mind of coveting and contending ceases.
translations.idiomatic: Once rank is fixed, the impulse to scheme and contend dies away.

sentences.zh: 今人間咸言右丞相張說欲取立后功圖復相，今太子非惠妃所生，而妃有子，若一儷宸極，則儲位將不安。

translations.literal: Now among the people all say Right Chancellor Zhang Yue seeks merit in establishing the empress to plot restoration to chancellor; the present crown prince was not born of Huifei, yet the consort has sons—if she stands beside the August Apex, the heir's position will not be secure.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor says Chancellor Zhang Yue hopes to earn credit by helping make her empress and regain his post. The crown prince is not Consort Wu's son, yet she has sons of her own. If she sits beside the emperor, the heir's place will no longer be secure.

sentences.zh: 古人所以諫其漸者，有以也！」

translations.literal: That ancients admonished against letting evil advance gradually—there was reason!"
translations.idiomatic: The ancients warned against letting trouble grow by degrees—and they were right!

sentences.zh: 遂不果立。

translations.literal: In the end she was not established.
translations.idiomatic: The plan to make her empress was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 妃生子必秀嶷，凡二王、一主，皆不育。

translations.literal: Whenever the consort bore a son he was sure to be fair and tall; of two princes and one princess, all died young.
translations.idiomatic: Every son she bore was strikingly handsome; yet of two princes and one princess, none survived.

sentences.zh: 及生壽王，帝命寧王養外邸。

translations.literal: When she bore the Prince of Shou, the emperor ordered the Prince of Ning to raise him in an outer residence.
translations.idiomatic: When she bore the Prince of Shou, the emperor had Prince Ning raise him outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 又生盛王、咸宜太華二公主。

translations.literal: She also bore the Prince of Sheng and the Princesses Xianyi and Taihua.
translations.idiomatic: She later bore the Prince of Sheng and the Princesses Xianyi and Taihua.

sentences.zh: 後李林甫以壽王母愛，希妃意陷太子、鄂光二王，皆廢死。

translations.literal: Later Li Linfu, because the Prince of Shou's mother was favored, curried the consort's intent and framed the crown prince and the Princes of E and Guang—both deposed and dead.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Linfu, playing on the favor shown the Prince of Shou's mother, did Consort Wu's bidding and destroyed the crown prince and the Princes of E and Guang; all were deposed and died.

sentences.zh: 會妃薨，年四十餘，贈皇后及謚，葬敬陵。

translations.literal: Just then the consort died, aged forty-some; empress title and posthumous name were granted; buried at Jing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after she died, in her forties; posthumous empress rank and an epithet were granted, and she was buried at Jingling.

sentences.zh: 玄宗元獻楊皇后玄宗元獻皇后楊氏，華州華陰人。

translations.literal: Empress Yuanyuan Yang of Xuanzong—Empress Yuanyuan Yang, native of Huayin in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yuanyuan Yang of Xuanzong—Lady Yang of Huayin in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖士達，為隋納言。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Shida served as Receptionist of the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-grandfather Shida had been Receptionist under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 天授中，以武后母黨，追封士達為鄭王，父知慶太尉。

translations.literal: In Tianshou, because of ties to Empress Wu's mother's clan, Shida was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Zheng, father Zhiqing as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianshou, as kin of Empress Wu's mother's line, Shida was posthumously made Prince of Zheng and her father Zhiqing Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 帝在東宮，后以景雲初入宮為良媛。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Eastern Heir, the lady at Jingyun's beginning entered the palace as Lady of Excellent Fairness.
translations.idiomatic: While he was heir apparent, she entered the palace as a Lady of Excellent Fairness in the first year of Jingyun.

sentences.zh: 時太平公主忌帝，而宮中左右持兩端，纖悉必聞。

translations.literal: At the time Princess Taiping resented the emperor; palace attendants hedged both ways—every trifle was sure to reach her ears.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping was hostile to the heir, and palace attendants played both sides, so every whisper reached her.

sentences.zh: 媛方娠，帝不自安，密語侍讀張說曰：「用事者不欲吾多子，奈何？」

translations.literal: The Lady was newly pregnant; the emperor was ill at ease and secretly told Lector Zhang Yue: "Those in power do not wish me many sons—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: When she became pregnant he grew uneasy and confided to his tutor Zhang Yue, "Those in power do not want me to have many sons. What can I do?

sentences.zh: 命說挾劑以入，帝於曲室自煮之。

translations.literal: He ordered Yue to bring in medicine; the emperor in a side chamber boiled it himself.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yue bring in an abortifacient, and in a side chamber boiled it himself.

sentences.zh: 夢若有介而戈者環鼎三，而三煮盡覆。

translations.literal: He dreamed as if armored men with spears circled the tripod thrice, and thrice the boiling was overturned.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed armored men with spears circling the cauldron three times, and three times the brew was overturned.

sentences.zh: 以告說，說曰：「天命也！」

translations.literal: Telling Yue, Yue said: "Heaven's mandate!"
translations.idiomatic: He told Yue, who said, "It is Heaven's will!

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Then he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned the attempt.

sentences.zh: 生男，是為肅宗。

translations.literal: She bore a boy—this was Suzong.
translations.idiomatic: She bore a son who would become Emperor Suzong.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，為貴嬪。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, she became Noble Lady of Excellence.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne she was made Noble Lady of Excellence.

sentences.zh: 其姊，節愍太子妃也。

translations.literal: Her elder sister was consort to the Jiemin Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder sister had been consort to Crown Prince Jiemin.

sentences.zh: 初，肅宗生，卜云：「不宜養。」

translations.literal: At first, when Suzong was born, divination said: "Not fit to raise."
translations.idiomatic: At Suzong's birth the diviners said he should not be raised in the palace.

sentences.zh: 乃命王皇后舉之。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered Empress Wang to raise him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore entrusted him to Empress Wang.

sentences.zh: 后無子，撫肅宗如所生。

translations.literal: The empress had no son; she nurtured Suzong as if born of herself.
translations.idiomatic: Childless herself, she reared Suzong as her own.

sentences.zh: 後又生寧親公主，乃薨。

translations.literal: Later she also bore Princess Ningqin, then died.
translations.idiomatic: She later bore Princess Ningqin, then died.

sentences.zh: 說以舊恩，故子垍得尚寧親。

translations.literal: Yue for old favor—therefore son Yu married Princess Ningqin.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Zhang Yue's old favor, his son Yu was given Princess Ningqin in marriage.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，至德二載，太上皇自蜀誥有司「其議尊稱」，遂上冊謚。

translations.literal: When Suzong took the throne, second year of Zhide, the Retired Emperor from Shu ordered the offices "discuss her honored title"; thereupon enfeoffment and posthumous name were raised.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong ascended, in the second year of Zhide the retired emperor from Shu ordered the ministries to deliberate her honors, and she received enfeoffment and a posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 寶應末，祔泰陵。

translations.literal: Near the end of Baoying, she was affiliated to Tailing.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Baoying she was installed at Tailing.

sentences.zh: 玄宗貴妃楊氏玄宗貴妃楊氏，隋梁郡通守汪四世孫。

translations.literal: Noble Consort Yang of Xuanzong—Noble Consort Yang, four-generations-descendant of Wang, Tongshou of Liang Commandery of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Noble Consort Yang of Xuanzong—Lady Yang, fourth-generation descendant of Wang, Tongshou of Liang under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 徙籍蒲州，遂為永樂人。

translations.literal: Registry moved to Puzhou; thus she became native of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: Her household register was moved to Puzhou, and she became a subject of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，養叔父家。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, raised in uncle's household.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, she was raised by her uncle.

sentences.zh: 始為壽王妃。

translations.literal: At first she was consort to the Prince of Shou.
translations.idiomatic: She was first married to the Prince of Shou.

sentences.zh: 開元二十四年，武惠妃薨，後廷無當帝意者。

translations.literal: Twenty-fourth year of Kaiyuan, Consort Wu Huifei died; the rear court had none matching the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Kaiyuan Consort Wu died, and none in the inner palace pleased him.

sentences.zh: 或言妃姿質天挺，宜充掖廷，遂召內禁中，異之，即為自出妃意者，丐籍女官，號「太真」，更為壽王聘韋昭訓女，而太真得幸。

translations.literal: Some said the consort's looks were heaven-endowed, fit to fill the Rear Court; therefore she was summoned into the forbidden inner quarter. Finding her extraordinary, he immediately had her express the consort's wish: beg registry as female official, styled "Grand Perfection," changed to betroth to the Prince of Shou the daughter of Wei Zhaoxun, while Grand Perfection gained favor.
translations.idiomatic: Some said her beauty was heaven-sent and she ought to fill the inner quarters. Summoned into the palace, he found her extraordinary; at her wish she was registered as a female official under the name Taizhen, the Prince of Shou was given Wei Zhaoxun's daughter instead, and Taizhen won his favor.

sentences.zh: 善歌舞，邃曉音律，且智算警穎，迎意輒悟。

translations.literal: Skilled in song and dance, deeply versed in music, and moreover clever in calculation, alert and keen—meeting intent she at once understood.
translations.idiomatic: She excelled at song and dance and knew music deeply; quick-witted and sharp, she grasped his mood before he spoke.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，遂專房宴，宮中號「娘子」，儀體與皇后等。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly delighted, then monopolized her bedchamber feasts; within the palace she was called "Niangzi," ceremonial form equal to empress.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, he kept her to himself alone; the palace called her Niangzi, and her ceremonial rank equaled an empress.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，進冊貴妃。

translations.literal: Early Tianbao, advanced and enregistered as Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao she was advanced to Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 追贈父玄琰太尉、齊國公。

translations.literal: Her father Xuanyan posthumously granted Grand Marshal and Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xuanyan was posthumously made Grand Marshal and Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 擢叔玄珪光祿卿，宗兄銛鴻臚卿，錡侍御史，尚太華公主。

translations.literal: Uncle Xuangui promoted Minister of the Imperial Clan; clan elder brother Xian Supervisor of Guests; Qi Attending Censor, married Princess Taihua.
translations.idiomatic: Her uncle Xuangui became Minister of the Imperial Clan; her cousin Xian Supervisor of Guests; Qi Attending Censor, who married Princess Taihua.

sentences.zh: 主，惠妃所生，最見寵遇。

translations.literal: The princess was born of Huifei, most seen in favor and treatment.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was Consort Wu's daughter and enjoyed the deepest favor.

sentences.zh: 而釗亦寖顯。

translations.literal: And Zhao also gradually came to prominence.
translations.idiomatic: Her cousin Zhao likewise grew in influence.

sentences.zh: 釗，國忠也。

translations.literal: Zhao was Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was Yang Guozhong.

sentences.zh: 三姊皆美劭，帝呼為姨，封韓、虢、秦三國，為夫人，出入宮掖，恩寵聲焰震天下。

translations.literal: Three elder sisters all had beautiful bearing; the emperor called them aunts, enfeoffed Han, Guo, and Qin states as Ladies, entering and leaving palace quarters; favor and renown shook all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Her three sisters were renowned beauties; the emperor called them "aunt" and made them Ladies of Han, Guo, and Qin. Passing in and out of the palace, their favor and fame shook the realm.

sentences.zh: 每命婦入班，持盈公主等皆讓不敢就位。

translations.literal: Whenever titled ladies entered court formation, Princess Chiying and others all yielded, not daring to take position.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever court ladies took their places, even Princess Chiying and others stepped aside, not daring to stand before them.

sentences.zh: 臺省、州縣奉請托，奔走期會過詔敕。

translations.literal: Terrace provinces and commanderies-counties fulfilled entreaties, running to appointments surpassing imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Ministries and local officials hurried to do their bidding, outrunning imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 四方獻餉結納，門若市然。

translations.literal: From four directions tribute-offerings and patronage—doors like a market.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts and clients streamed in from every quarter until their gates seemed a marketplace.

sentences.zh: 建平、信成二公主以與妃家忤，至追內封物，駙馬都尉獨孤明失官。

translations.literal: Princesses Jianping and Xincheng for clashing with the consort's family—even chased to recover inner-palace sealed goods; Commandery-Consort Dugu Ming lost office.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses Jianping and Xincheng, having offended the Yang clan, were made to return palace gifts; their husbands' consort Dugu Ming lost his post.

sentences.zh: 它日，妃以譴還銛第，比中仄，帝尚不御食，笞怒左右。

translations.literal: Another day the consort for reprimand returned to Xian's residence; nearing noon, the emperor still had not taken food, flogging and raging at attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Once, banished to Xian's house, she lingered past noon while the emperor refused his meal and beat his attendants in fury.

sentences.zh: 高力士欲驗帝意，乃白以殿中供帳、司農酒餼百餘車送妃所，帝即以御膳分賜。

translations.literal: Gao Lishi wishing to test the emperor's mind, reported sending over a hundred carts of palace provisioning and Commissary wine and provisions to the consort's place—the emperor immediately divided imperial fare as gift.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi, testing the emperor's mood, had more than a hundred carts of palace provisions and Commissary stores sent to her; the emperor at once shared his own meal with her.

sentences.zh: 力士知帝旨，是夕，請召妃還，下鑰安興坊門馳入。

translations.literal: Lishi knowing the emperor's intent, that evening requested summoning the consort back, unlocking Anxing Ward gate and galloping in.
translations.idiomatic: Reading his intent, Lishi that night asked to bring her back; the Anxing Ward gate was unbolted and she rode in at speed.

sentences.zh: 妃見帝，伏地謝，帝釋然，撫尉良渥。

translations.literal: The consort seeing the emperor, prostrated in thanks; the emperor was relieved, soothing and comforting with great warmth.
translations.idiomatic: She prostrated herself before him; his anger lifted, and he comforted her with exceptional tenderness.

sentences.zh: 明日，諸姨上食，樂作，帝驟賜左右不可貲。

translations.literal: Next day the various aunts presented food, music played; the emperor suddenly bestowed on attendants beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The next day her sisters presented a feast with music, and he showered gifts on those around him beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 由是愈見寵，賜諸姨錢歲百萬為脂粉費。

translations.literal: From this she was all the more favored; granted the various aunts money yearly a million for rouge-and-powder expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Her favor only grew; each year he gave her sisters a million cash for cosmetics alone.

sentences.zh: 銛以上柱國門列戟，與銛、國忠、諸姨五家第舍聯亙，擬憲宮禁，率一堂費緡千萬。

translations.literal: Xian with Upper Pillar-of-State rank—gates lined with halberds—with Xian, Guozhong, and the various aunts, five families' mansions stretched connected, matching imperial palace prohibition; commonly one hall cost strings of cash ten million.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was made Upper Pillar of State with halberds at his gate; the five Yang households—Xian, Guozhong, and the sisters—built mansions in a row rivaling the palace, each hall costing ten million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 見它第有勝者，輒壞復造，務以瓌侈相誇詡，土木工不息。

translations.literal: Seeing another residence that surpassed, they would destroy and rebuild, striving with rare extravagance to boast one another—earth-and-wood work unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: If another house outshone theirs, they tore it down and rebuilt, vying in outrageous luxury; builders never rested.

sentences.zh: 帝所得奇珍及貢獻分賜之，使者相銜於道，五家如一。

translations.literal: The emperor's obtained rare treasures and tribute offerings were divided and bestowed on them; envoys linked along the road—the five families as one.
translations.idiomatic: Rare treasures and tribute were divided among them, with couriers crowding the roads—all five households alike.

sentences.zh: 妃每從遊幸，乘馬則力士授轡策。

translations.literal: Whenever the consort followed on tour, if riding horse then Lishi handed reins and whip.
translations.idiomatic: When she joined his outings on horseback, Lishi himself held her bridle and whip.

sentences.zh: 凡充錦繡官及冶瑑金玉者，大抵千人，奉須索，奇服秘玩，變化若神。

translations.literal: All filling brocade offices and smelting-inlaying gold and jade—roughly a thousand—served her demands; strange garments and secret curios, transformations like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly a thousand artisans in brocades, gold, and jade served her whims; garments and curios appeared as if by sorcery.

sentences.zh: 四方爭為怪珍入貢，動駭耳目。

translations.literal: From four directions they competed presenting freakish treasures; always startling eye and ear.
translations.idiomatic: Every region vied to send bizarre tribute that astonished all who saw it.

sentences.zh: 於是嶺南節度使張九章、廣陵長史王翼以所獻最，進九章銀青階，擢翼戶部侍郎，天下風靡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Lingnan Military Commissioner Zhang Jiuzhang and Guangling Chief Administrator Wang Yi for their offerings being foremost—Jiuzhang advanced one Silver-Green rank, Yi promoted Vice Minister of Revenue—the realm swept by the fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuzhang of Lingnan and Wang Yi of Guangling, whose gifts were judged finest, were promoted—Jiuzhang given a Silver-Green grade and Yi made Vice Minister of Revenue—and the empire rushed to imitate them.

sentences.zh: 妃嗜荔支，必欲生致之，乃置騎傳送，走數千里，味未變已至京師。

translations.literal: The consort craved lychee, must have it brought living; therefore established horse relay transport, running several thousand li—flavor not yet changed already arriving at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: She loved lychees fresh from the tree; relays were set up to gallop them thousands of li to the capital before the flavor changed.

sentences.zh: 天寶九載，妃復得譴還外第，國忠謀於吉溫。

translations.literal: Ninth year of Tianbao, the consort again received reprimand and returned to outer residence; Guozhong schemed with Ji Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Tianbao she was banished again to her family's house; Guozhong consulted Ji Wen.

sentences.zh: 溫因見帝曰：「婦人過忤當死，然何惜宮中一席廣為鈇鑕地，更使外辱乎？」

translations.literal: Wen therefore seeing the emperor said: "A woman excessive in offense should die—yet why spare not one mat within the palace widely made into an axe-block ground, yet further suffer outer disgrace?"
translations.idiomatic: Wen told the emperor, "A woman who offends may deserve death, but why turn a palace chamber into an execution ground only to shame her before the world?

sentences.zh: 帝感動，輟食，詔中人張韜光賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved, stopped eating, ordered eunuch Zhang Taoguang to bestow on her.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, the emperor left his meal and sent the eunuch Zhang Taoguang with gifts.

sentences.zh: 妃因韜光謝帝曰：「妾有罪當萬誅，然膚髮外皆上所賜，今且死，無以報。」

translations.literal: The consort through Taoguang thanked the emperor: "Your handmaid has guilt deserving ten thousand executions, yet skin and hair without—all bestowed by Your Majesty; now about to die, nothing wherewith to repay."
translations.idiomatic: Through Taoguang she told him, "I deserve ten thousand deaths, yet every hair on my body is Your Majesty's gift. About to die, I have no way to repay you.

sentences.zh: 引刀斷一繚髮奏之，曰：「以此留訣。」

translations.literal: Drawing knife she severed one lock of hair and presented it, saying: "With this I leave farewell."
translations.idiomatic: She cut a lock of her hair and sent it, saying, "Take this as my farewell."

sentences.zh: 帝見駭惋，遽召入，禮遇如初。

translations.literal: The emperor seeing was startled and grieved, hastily summoned her in; courtesy and treatment as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Stricken, he summoned her back at once and received her as before.

sentences.zh: 因又幸秦國及國忠第，賜兩家鉅萬。

translations.literal: Then again visited Qin State and Guozhong's residence, bestowed on both families huge ten-thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He visited the households of Qin and Guozhong and gave each vast sums.

sentences.zh: 國忠既遙領劍南，每十月，帝幸華清宮，五宅車騎皆從，家別為隊，隊一色，俄五家隊合，爛若萬花，川谷成錦繡，國忠導以劍南旗節。

translations.literal: Guozhong already holding distant command of Jiannan; every tenth month the emperor visited Huaqing Palace—the five mansions' chariots and horses all followed; each household separately formed a troop, troops one color; soon the five households' troops joined, brilliant as ten thousand flowers, valleys and streams becoming brocade; Guozhong led with Jiannan flags and insignia.
translations.idiomatic: With Guozhong holding remote command of Jiannan, each tenth month when the emperor went to Huaqing Palace all five Yang households followed in their own colored columns; when the columns merged, the procession blazed like ten thousand flowers and turned valleys to brocade, Guozhong leading with the banners of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 遺鈿墮舄，瑟瑟璣琲，狼藉於道，香聞數十里。

translations.literal: Lost hairpins and fallen slippers, sese and pearl strands, scattered on the road—fragrance heard several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Hairpins and slippers fell along the way, sese gems and beads littering the road, their perfume drifting for miles.

sentences.zh: 十載正月望夜，妃家與廣寧主僮騎爭闤門，鞭挺讙競，主墮馬，僅得去。

translations.literal: Tenth year first month lantern-night, the consort's family and Princess Guangning's servants and riders contested the market gate—whips and clubs, clamor and struggle; the princess fell from horse, barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: On the Lantern Festival of the tenth year, her household and Princess Guangning's retinue fought at the market gate with whips and cudgels; the princess was thrown from her horse but barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 主見帝泣，乃詔殺楊氏奴，貶駙馬都尉程昌裔官。

translations.literal: The princess seeing the emperor wept; thereupon edict killed Yang household slave, demoted Commandery-Consort Cheng Changyi's office.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping before the emperor, she secured an edict to execute a Yang servant and demote her husband's consort Cheng Changyi.

sentences.zh: 國忠之輔政，其息昢尚萬春公主，暄尚延和郡主；

translations.literal: Guozhong in assisting governance—his son Min married Princess Wanchun, Xuan married Princess Yanhe;
translations.idiomatic: Once Guozhong held power, his son Min married Princess Wanchun and Xuan Princess Yanhe;

sentences.zh: 弟鑑尚承榮郡主。

translations.literal: Younger brother Jian married Princess Chengrong.
translations.idiomatic: his brother Jian married Princess Chengrong.

sentences.zh: 又詔為玄琰立家廟，帝自書其碑。

translations.literal: Again edict established for Xuanyan a clan temple; the emperor personally wrote its stele.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also founded a clan temple for Xuanyan, and the emperor wrote the stele himself.

sentences.zh: 銛、秦國早死，故韓、虢與國忠貴最久。

translations.literal: Xian and Qin State died early; therefore Han and Guo with Guozhong were noble longest.
translations.idiomatic: Xian and Lady Qin had died young, so the Ladies of Han and Guo and Guozhong enjoyed favor longest.

sentences.zh: 而虢國素與國忠亂，頗為人知，不恥也。

translations.literal: Yet Lady Guo had long been in disorder with Guozhong—fairly known to others; she felt no shame.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo and Guozhong had long carried on an affair openly known, yet she felt no shame.

sentences.zh: 每入謁，並驅道中，從監、侍姆百餘騎，炬蜜如盡，靚妝盈里，不施幃障，時人謂為「雄狐」。

translations.literal: Each time entering audience, driving abreast in the roadway—follower stewards and attendant nurses over a hundred riders; torches honey-thick as if exhausted, splendid makeup filling the lane, not applying carriage screens—people of the time called them "male fox."
translations.idiomatic: When they went to court they drove abreast down the avenue, attended by more than a hundred stewards and nurses, torches blazing like day, splendid dress filling the street without carriage curtains; people called them the "male fox."

sentences.zh: 諸王子孫凡婚聘，必先因韓、虢以請，輒皆遂，至數百千金以謝。

translations.literal: All princely sons and grandsons who sought marriage betrothal—must first through Han and Guo request—all at once succeeded, even to several hundred thousand in gold as thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Any prince or royal grandson seeking a marriage had first to petition through Han or Guo; they always succeeded and paid hundreds of thousands in gold in thanks.

sentences.zh: 初，安祿山有邊功，帝寵之，詔與諸姨約為兄弟，而祿山母事妃，來朝，必宴餞結歡。

translations.literal: At first An Lushan had frontier merit; the emperor favored him, edicted with the various aunts to covenant as brothers; Lushan treated the consort as mother, coming to court must feast and farewell to bind joy.
translations.idiomatic: Early on An Lushan had won merit on the frontier and earned the emperor's favor; he was made sworn brother to her sisters, treated the consort as mother, and was feasted whenever he came to court.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，以誅國忠為名，且指言妃及諸姨罪。

translations.literal: Lushan rebelled, taking execution of Guozhong as name, and moreover pointing to declare the consort and various aunts' crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled he named Guozhong as his target and denounced the consort and her sisters.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以皇太子撫軍，因禪位，諸楊大懼，哭於廷。

translations.literal: The emperor wished the crown prince to pacify the army, thereby yielding the throne; all Yang greatly feared, weeping in the court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to have the crown prince take command and then abdicate; the Yang clan panicked and wept in open court.

sentences.zh: 國忠入白妃，妃銜塊請死，帝意沮，乃止。

translations.literal: Guozhong entered to inform the consort; the consort held a lump and begged death; the emperor's intent discouraged—then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong told the consort, who begged to die with a stone in her mouth; the emperor's resolve failed, and he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 及西幸至馬嵬，陳玄禮等以天下計誅國忠，已死，軍不解。

translations.literal: When the western flight reached Mawei, Chen Xuanli and others, for the sake of the realm, executed Guozhong; he was already dead, yet the army would not disperse.
translations.idiomatic: When the flight west reached Mawei, Chen Xuanli and others put Yang Guozhong to death for the good of the empire. Even after he was dead, the troops would not stand down.

sentences.zh: 帝遣力士問故，曰：「禍本尚在！」

translations.literal: The emperor sent a strongman to ask the reason; they said: 'The root of the calamity is still here!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a strongman to inquire why. They answered, 'The source of the disaster is still alive!

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，與妃訣，引而去，縊路祠下，裹屍以紫茵，瘞道側，年三十八。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice; he took leave of the consort and led her away. She was strangled beneath a roadside shrine, her corpse wrapped in purple matting and buried beside the road at age thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not refuse. He bade the consort farewell and led her away. She was strangled under a roadside shrine, her body wrapped in purple matting and buried by the road. She was thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 帝至自蜀，道過其所，使祭之，且詔改葬。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from Shu, passing the place on the road, he had offerings made and also decreed reburial.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from Shu the emperor passed the spot, sent offerings, and ordered that she be reburied.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎李揆曰：「龍武將士以國忠負上速亂，為天下殺之。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Li Kui said: 'The Longwu soldiers killed Guozhong because he betrayed His Majesty and hastened rebellion, doing it for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Li Kui said, 'The Longwu troops killed Guozhong because he betrayed the emperor and brought rebellion on the empire.

sentences.zh: 今葬妃，恐反仄自疑。」

translations.literal: If the consort is now buried in state, I fear they will grow suspicious and uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: If we now give the consort a state burial, I fear the soldiers will grow suspicious and turn against us.

sentences.zh: 帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 密遣中使者具棺槨它葬焉。

translations.literal: Secretly he sent a palace envoy to prepare coffin and casket and bury her elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: In secret he sent a palace envoy to provide a coffin and bury her elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 啟瘞，故香囊猶在，中人以獻，帝視之，淒感流涕，命工貌妃於別殿，朝夕往，必為鯁欷。

translations.literal: Opening the burial, her old perfumed pouch was still there; the envoy presented it. The emperor looked at it, wept in grief, and ordered artisans to paint the consort's likeness in a separate hall. Morning and evening he went there and always choked with sobs.
translations.idiomatic: When the grave was opened her old perfumed pouch was still inside. The envoy presented it; the emperor wept at the sight and ordered artists to paint her portrait in a side hall. He visited morning and evening and always broke into sobs.

sentences.zh: 馬嵬之難，虢國與國忠妻裴柔等奔陳倉，縣令率吏追之，意以為賊，棄馬走林。

translations.literal: At the Mawei crisis, the Guo state and Guozhong's wife Pei Rou and others fled to Chencang; the magistrate led clerks in pursuit, taking them for bandits; they abandoned their horses and ran into the woods.
translations.idiomatic: During the Mawei crisis the Guo state and Guozhong's wife Pei Rou fled to Chencang. The magistrate pursued them with his officers, mistaking them for rebels. They abandoned their horses and fled into the forest.

sentences.zh: 虢國先殺其二子，柔曰：「丐我死！」

translations.literal: The Guo state first killed her two sons; Rou said: 'Grant me death!
translations.idiomatic: The Guo state killed her two sons first. Rou cried, 'Let me die!

sentences.zh: 即並其女刺殺之，乃自剄，不殊，吏載置於獄，問曰：「國家乎？

translations.literal: She then stabbed her daughter as well, then cut her own throat but did not die; the clerks loaded her into a cart and placed her in jail, asking: 'For the state?
translations.idiomatic: She then stabbed her daughter as well and cut her own throat but did not die. The officers put her in a cart and took her to jail, asking, 'Was it for the state?

sentences.zh: 賊乎？」

translations.literal: Or for bandits?
translations.idiomatic: Or for the rebels?

sentences.zh: 吏曰：「互有之。」

translations.literal: The clerks said: 'A bit of both.'
translations.idiomatic: They answered, 'A little of both.'

sentences.zh: 乃死，瘞陳倉東郭外。

translations.literal: She then died and was buried outside the eastern wall of Chencang.
translations.idiomatic: She died and was buried outside the eastern gate of Chencang.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：或稱武、韋亂唐同一轍，武持久，韋亟滅，何哉？

translations.literal: The commentator says: Some call the disorders of Wu and Wei the same track in Tang chaos—Wu endured long, Wei perished quickly; why?
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Some say the disorders wrought by Wu and Wei followed the same path—yet Wu's rule lasted while Wei's was swiftly destroyed. Why?

sentences.zh: 議者謂否。

translations.literal: Discussants say it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Those who debate the question say this is wrong.

sentences.zh: 武后自高宗時挾天子威福，脅制四海，雖逐嗣帝，改國號，然賞罰己出，不假借群臣，僭於上而治於下，故能終天年，阽亂而不亡。

translations.literal: From Gaozong's time Empress Wu wielded the Son of Heaven's authority and blessings, coercing all within the seas; though she drove out the heir emperor and changed the dynastic name, rewards and punishments already issued from her hand without borrowing ministers—usurping above yet governing below—therefore she could complete her natural years, on the brink of chaos yet not perishing.
translations.idiomatic: From Gaozong's reign Wu Zetian held the emperor's power in her grasp and bent the realm to her will. Though she deposed heirs and changed the dynastic name, reward and punishment issued from her alone without relying on ministers. She ruled from above while governing below, and so lived out her years on the edge of chaos without the dynasty's fall.

sentences.zh: 韋氏乘夫，淫蒸於朝，斜封四出，政放不一，既鴆殺帝，引睿宗輔政，權去手不自知，戚地已疏，人心相挻，玄宗藉其事以撼豪英，故取若掇遺，不旋踵宗族夷丹，勢奪而事淺也。

translations.literal: The Wei clan rode upon her husband, incest steaming in court, slanting seals going out on all sides, government released without unity; having poisoned the emperor and drawn Ruizong to assist in government, power left her hand yet she did not know it, her kin's ground already thin, people's hearts pulling one another—Xuanzong used the affair to shake the mighty, therefore taking it was like picking up something dropped; before a turn of the heel the clan was exterminated to the red, power seized yet the affair shallow.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei clan rose on her husband's back, debauchery filled the court, illicit appointments spread everywhere, and policy lacked coherence. After she poisoned the emperor and installed Ruizong as regent, power slipped from her hands before she knew it. Her kin had lost their footing and popular sentiment turned against her. Xuanzong seized the moment to strike down the powerful elite; victory came as easily as picking up something dropped. Within moments the clan was annihilated—her grasp on power was shallow, and her schemes shallow with it.

sentences.zh: 然二后遺後王戒，顧不厚哉！

translations.literal: Yet the warning the two empresses left for later kings—is it not weighty!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the warning these two empresses left for later rulers—how weighty it remains!
